The lighting is soft and natural, casting gentle shadows that enhance the dish's depth. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green from a blurred potted plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly beside the plate, and a single, unadorned fork rests nearby, completing the understated, elegant presentation.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Carrot: Wash and peel 400g carrots. Shred finely. In a bowl, massage shredded carrots with 10g sea salt for 5 minutes until liquid forms. Pack tightly into a clean glass jar. Press down to remove air bubbles. Cover carrots completely with their liquid or add filtered water if needed. Seal with an airlock lid or loosely cover. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Prepare Roasted Tomato Conserve: Preheat oven to 150°C. Wash tomatoes. Quarter them. Place in a baking dish. Add 2 crushed garlic cloves and 2 thyme sprigs. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 1.5 to 2 hours, until tomatoes are soft and slightly caramelized. Remove thyme sprigs. Mash lightly or leave rustic. Set aside.

Prepare Root Medallions: Wash and scrub potatoes and remaining 200g carrots. Do not peel. Cut potatoes into 2 cm thick rounds. Cut carrots into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potato rounds. Boil for 5 minutes. Add carrot rounds. Boil for another 3-4 minutes, until tender-crisp. Drain well.

Sear Medallions: Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add potato and carrot medallions in a single layer. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and slightly crispy. Add remaining garlic clove, minced, and remaining thyme sprigs during the last 2 minutes of searing. Season with salt and pepper.

Assemble and Serve: Arrange 2-3 roasted potato medallions and 2-3 roasted carrot medallions on each plate. Place a generous spoonful of fermented carrot kraut next to the medallions. Spoon roasted tomato conserve alongside. Serve immediately.
notes: For zero-waste, collect potato and carrot peels to make vegetable stock for future recipes.
Fermentation time for carrots can be adjusted based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Balsamic Braised Pork and Beef with Roasted Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Balsamic Braised Pork and Beef is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table. Tender, dark brown chunks of braised pork and beef are artfully arranged, not fanned, alongside golden-brown, crispy-edged roasted potato wedges. Vibrant red, slightly blistered Roma tomato halves are nestled amongst the meat and potatoes. A rich, glossy, dark brown balsamic braising sauce is generously spooned over the dish, catching the light. The entire composition is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley, providing a vibrant contrast. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. Standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin rest beside the plate, all bathed in natural, even lighting within a casual bistro setting, highlighting the approachable elegance of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a hearty main course with crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder and beef chuck into 4-5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks until browned on all sides. Remove from pot. Repeat with beef chunks. Remove from pot.
Dice onions. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Sauté diced onions until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in balsamic vinegar. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared pork and beef to the pot. Ensure meat is mostly submerged. Cover the pot.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until meat is very tender.
While meat braises, prepare potatoes and Roma tomatoes. Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges. Halve Roma tomatoes.
Toss potato wedges with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Toss halved Roma tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a separate baking sheet.
After meat has braised for 2 hours, place potato wedges in the oven. Roast for 30-40 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and tender.
Add Roma tomatoes to the oven for the last 15-20 minutes of potato roasting, or until slightly softened.

Remove braised meat from oven. Carefully remove meat chunks from the sauce. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaves. If sauce is too thin, reduce it over medium heat on the stovetop until desired consistency. Season sauce to taste.
Chop fresh parsley for garnish.

To plate, arrange a mound of roasted potato wedges on a clean white porcelain plate. Place several chunks of braised pork and beef next to the potatoes. Nestle roasted Roma tomato halves among the meat and potatoes. Spoon a generous amount of the rich balsamic braising sauce over the meat and vegetables. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For extra depth of flavor, sear the meat until a deep brown crust forms.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin, Chicken Roulade, Mushroom Duxelles, Tomato Gel, Olive Dust
recipes.visual_description: A singular, perfectly seared beef tenderloin medallion, displaying a rich, deep brown crust and a tender, pink interior, anchors the plate. Adjacent, two precisely cut, plump chicken roulade discs reveal a delicate, herb-infused filling. A small, elegant quenelle of earthy mushroom duxelles rests nearby, its rich brown contrasting with the lighter elements. Scattered artfully are translucent, ruby-red squares of clear tomato gel, catching the light and adding a vibrant, geometric accent. A light dusting of deep black olive powder provides a textural contrast and an umami burst. A subtle sheen of reduced jus glazes the components. The composition is minimalist, with generous negative space on an oversized, round, pristine white bone china plate with a subtle silver rim. The setting is a smooth, cool grey marble surface, with a precisely folded white linen napkin to the side. Dramatic, directional overhead lighting creates defined shadows, highlighting textures and forms. The background is uncluttered, a soft, diffused grey, allowing maximum focus on the meticulously plated dish. A single, elegant silver fork rests beside the plate, completing the refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small, elegant shot of chilled premium vodka.
Offer a delicate rye bread crisp on the side.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Roulade: Butterfly chicken breasts, pound to 5mm thickness. Finely chop 2 garlic cloves, 1 shallot, and parsley. Mix with chicken mince, salt, and pepper. Spread mixture evenly over chicken breasts. Tightly roll chicken into cylinders. Wrap each roulade securely in cling film, twisting ends to seal. Poach roulades in simmering water (not boiling) until internal temperature reaches 75°C (approx. 18-20 minutes). Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Chill completely. Unwrap and slice into 2cm thick discs.

Prepare Mushroom Duxelles: Finely chop mixed wild mushrooms, 1 shallot, and 1 garlic clove. Melt 20g butter in a pan over medium heat. Add chopped mushrooms, shallot, and garlic. Sauté, stirring frequently, until all moisture evaporates and mixture is dry. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Prepare Clear Tomato Gel: Coarsely chop tomatoes. Blend in a food processor until puréed. Pass purée through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth-lined colander. Press gently to extract clear juice, do not force pulp. Season juice with salt. Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes. Gently warm a small portion of the tomato juice; dissolve bloomed gelatin in it. Stir gelatin mixture back into remaining tomato juice. Pour into a shallow, flat tray (approx. 1cm deep). Chill until firmly set (approx. 2-3 hours). Cut into small, precise 1.5cm squares.

Prepare Olive Dust: Preheat oven to 80°C. Spread Kalamata olives on a baking sheet. Dehydrate in oven until completely dry and brittle (approx. 2-3 hours, or use a dehydrator). Blitz dried olives in a spice grinder or mortar and pestle until a fine, uniform powder forms. Store in an airtight container.

Prepare Beef Tenderloin: Season beef medallions generously with salt and black pepper. Heat olive oil and remaining butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Ensure internal temperature reaches at least 63°C for medium-rare. Rest beef on a warm plate, loosely tented with foil, for 5 minutes.
Prepare Jus: Reduce beef stock over medium heat until thickened to a light coating consistency. Season to taste.

Assemble and Serve: Place one seared beef tenderloin medallion slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange two chicken roulade discs beside the beef. Spoon a small, elegant quenelle of mushroom duxelles near the chicken. Artfully place 3-4 translucent tomato gel squares around the main components. Lightly dust a small area of the plate with olive powder. Drizzle a small amount of the reduced jus around the elements. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken roulade is fully chilled before slicing for clean cuts.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing beef to ensure proper browning.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Onion Macaroni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken with macaroni is presented on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The chicken thigh, cooked to a golden-brown exterior, sits as a whole, un-sliced piece, its surface subtly glistening. Beside it, a neat, slightly free-form mound of creamy macaroni showcases its al dente texture. The macaroni is enriched with melted cheese, creating a subtle sheen. A small, vibrant pile of thinly sliced fermented red onion, displaying shades of pink and purple, provides a bright visual and textural contrast to the side of the macaroni. A scattering of finely chopped fresh green herbs, either parsley or chives, adds a final touch of color and freshness. The plate is positioned with ample negative space, allowing each component to breathe. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing the natural colors and textures. An undyed linen napkin is subtly folded nearby, and the background remains clean and minimalist, perhaps with a hint of natural plant life in soft focus.
instructions: Prepare fermented onions: Thinly slice the red onion into rings. In a clean jar, combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Stir until dissolved. Add onion rings. Seal and refrigerate for at least 24 hours, ideally 3-5 days. This can be done in advance.
Boil macaroni: Cook macaroni pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Reserve 50ml pasta cooking water.

Sear chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down (if skin-on) or presentation-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Reduce heat to medium. Cook for another 7-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.

Prepare macaroni sauce: Dice the small brown onion. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.

Combine macaroni: Add cooked macaroni to the skillet with the stock. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until melted and creamy. If needed, add a splash of reserved pasta water for desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Plate the dish: Divide macaroni among four plates. Place one seared chicken thigh alongside the macaroni. Top each portion of macaroni with a small spoonful of fermented onion. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Crispy Garlic-Herb Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, its skin deeply golden and visibly crisp, rests on a pristine white porcelain plate. Beside it, a generous serving of crispy roasted potato wedges, golden-brown and irregular in shape, are piled neatly. Small flecks of dark green rosemary and thyme adhere to the potato surfaces. A glossy, rich brown pan sauce is artfully drizzled over a portion of the chicken and pools slightly on the plate. The vibrant green of chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a final flourish. The arrangement is clean and professional, with thoughtful spacing. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting textures and warm colors in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm wedges or irregular chunks. Do not peel.
In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with 30 ml olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a large baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until fork-tender and golden-crisp.
While potatoes roast, heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place chicken thighs, skin-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes without moving, until the skin is deeply golden-brown and crispy.
Flip chicken thighs. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from the skillet. Place on a cutting board and rest for 5 minutes.
Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. Pour in chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, reducing slightly.
Remove from heat. Whisk in butter until melted and sauce is slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Plate one chicken thigh alongside a generous portion of crispy garlic-herb potatoes. Drizzle the pan sauce over the chicken and potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Massaman Pork Curry
recipes.visual_description: A rich, creamy Massaman Pork Curry is presented in a deep white porcelain bowl, positioned slightly off-center on a simple wooden table. Tender, slow-cooked pork shoulder chunks, golden-brown from initial searing, are nestled amongst soft, quartered waxy potatoes and translucent, large onion wedges. Halved vibrant red cherry tomatoes and whole roasted peanuts are scattered throughout the thick, aromatic, reddish-brown curry sauce, which shimmers with coconut oil. The sauce has a moderate viscosity, clinging to the ingredients. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green coriander leaves provides a fresh counterpoint. A pristine white porcelain plate with a serving of fluffy jasmine rice sits beside the curry bowl. A set of elegant, simple flatware rests on a folded natural cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's warmth and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of Ajaad (cucumber relish) for a refreshing contrast.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 3-4cm chunks.
Quarter small waxy potatoes. Cut onion into large wedges. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add Massaman curry paste. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pork chunks to the pot. Sear until browned on all sides.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir well to combine with the paste.
Add quartered potatoes and onion wedges to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until pork is very tender and potatoes are cooked through.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Add halved cherry tomatoes and roasted peanuts. Simmer for 5 more minutes.
Serve Massaman Pork Curry hot with jasmine rice. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors: sweet, sour, salty, spicy.
Sautéing curry paste until fragrant to release aromatics.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coq au Vin is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are positioned centrally, coated in a glossy, deep-burgundy wine sauce. Surrounding the chicken are whole, golden-brown button mushrooms, translucent pearl onions, and crispy bacon lardons. The sauce is rich and thick, clinging to the meat. A pinch of fresh green parsley is scattered over the top. The background features a dark wood bistro table with a clean white cotton napkin and a small side plate of crusty baguette. Natural, even lighting highlights the velvety texture of the sauce and the rustic, braised appearance of the vegetables. The entire plate is visible with elegant negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of the same red wine used in the braise
Serve in wide, shallow bowls

ingredients.name: dry red wine (Pinot Noir or Burgundy)

instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken in a heavy pot over medium-high heat until skin is golden. Remove from pot.
Fry bacon lardons in the same pot until crisp.
Add whole pearl onions and whole mushrooms to the bacon fat. Brown for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the pot. Pour in red wine and chicken stock.
Add thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise over low heat for 30 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Mix butter and flour into a smooth paste.
Whisk the paste into the simmering liquid to thicken the sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes until glossy. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry red wine for the best flavor profile
Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato Confit, Vanilla Potato, Mustard Seed Tuile, Chicken Consommé Caramel
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist dessert presented on a pristine white bone china plate. Three to four ruby-red, vanilla-roasted cherry tomatoes, slightly shriveled and glistening, are artfully arranged on one side of the plate. A delicate, translucent potato-vanilla lace tuile, with its intricate web-like pattern and golden-brown edges, stands upright, offering a subtle architectural element. Beside it, a shard of dark, crisp candied mustard seed tuile provides a contrasting texture and deep hue. A glossy, amber chicken consommé caramel is drizzled in an organic, flowing line across the plate. A tiny, concentrated dot of dark caramelized onion puree completes the composition, adding a profound savory-sweet anchor. The ample white space emphasizes precise placement and refined textures. Dramatic side lighting creates intentional shadows, highlighting the dish's sculptural quality on a dark polished wood surface.
instructions: Prepare Vanilla-Roasted Tomato Confit: Preheat oven to 120°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Scrape vanilla bean seeds into a small bowl with a pinch of sugar. Toss tomatoes with vanilla sugar, remaining sugar, and thyme. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 1.5-2 hours until shriveled and intensely sweet. Cool.

Make Chicken Consommé Caramel: Reduce chicken stock in a saucepan over medium-high heat until about 50 ml remains. It should be syrupy. Stir in 10 g granulated sugar until dissolved. Set aside. Keep warm before serving.

Prepare Caramelized Onion Puree: Thinly slice white onion. Sauté onion in a small pan with 5 g butter over very low heat for 30-40 minutes until deeply caramelized and dark brown. Add 20 ml water to deglaze, scrape up bits. Blend with a stick blender until very smooth. Season with a tiny pinch of salt. Set aside.

Make Potato-Vanilla Lace Tuile: Peel and thinly slice potatoes using a mandoline, less than 1 mm thick. Cut into desired shapes. Combine 10 g sugar, 30 ml water, and 1/4 scraped vanilla bean in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add potato slices. Cook gently until tender-crisp. Carefully remove potato slices. Arrange on a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 150°C for 10-15 minutes until crisp and golden lace forms. Cool.

Prepare Candied Mustard Seed Tuile: In a small saucepan, combine black mustard seeds, 20 g sugar, and 30 ml water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer until water evaporates and seeds are coated and slightly candied, about 5-7 minutes. Spread thinly onto a silicone mat. Bake at 150°C for 8-10 minutes until crisp. Cool and break into shards.

Assemble the dish: Place 3-4 confit tomatoes artfully on one side of a white bone china plate. Lean a shard of potato-vanilla lace tuile and a shard of candied mustard seed tuile against the tomatoes or in a complementary arrangement. Drizzle a small amount of warm chicken consommé caramel in an elegant swirl. Add a tiny dot of caramelized onion puree beside the caramel for a contrasting note. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti Carbonara
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Spaghetti Carbonara is artfully twirled into a neat mound on a clean white porcelain plate. The pasta, glistening with a rich, creamy, golden-yellow emulsion, forms the central focus. Scattered generously over the spaghetti are crispy, golden-brown cubes of rendered guanciale, adding textural contrast and deep savory notes. A generous dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese blankets parts of the dish, creating a delicate white layer. Freshly cracked black pepper provides dark speckles across the creamy surface. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a classic silver fork and spoon placed beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the pasta's sheen and the guanciale's crisp edges. The overall presentation is refined yet inviting, embodying a modern bistro style with authentic Italian simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine or sparkling water.
Traditionally eaten with a fork, using a spoon to assist in twirling the pasta.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Dice guanciale into 1 cm cubes.
Heat a large pan over medium heat. Add diced guanciale. Cook slowly until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove crispy guanciale. Leave rendered fat in pan.
Cook spaghetti in boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
While pasta cooks, whisk egg yolks, whole egg, and 80 g grated Pecorino Romano in a bowl. Add half of the freshly ground black pepper.
Drain spaghetti. Add hot spaghetti directly to the pan with rendered guanciale fat. Toss to coat.
Immediately add egg mixture to spaghetti. Stir quickly and vigorously.
Gradually add reserved hot pasta water, 30 ml at a time, while stirring constantly. Continue until a creamy, emulsified sauce forms.
Add crispy guanciale back to the pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining grated Pecorino Romano and fresh black pepper.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Beef and Chicken Kofta with Roasted Tomato and Onion
recipes.visual_description: A small starter portion of Spiced Kofta is elegantly plated on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. Three to four elongated, golden-brown kofta, seared to a slight crisp on the exterior, are positioned centrally. Around them, vibrant red Roma tomato wedges and soft, caramelized red onion petals are artfully arranged, showcasing their roasted char. A small, separate ramekin of creamy, white chili-infused yogurt sauce sits beside the main dish. Fresh green parsley sprigs are scattered over the kofta and vegetables, adding a burst of color and freshness. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich textures and warm colors of the dish. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table and natural, even lighting. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, and a silver fork and knife are placed, ready for dining.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or flatbread for dipping in the yogurt sauce.
Offer a small side of fresh cucumber and mint salad.
instructions: Prepare Kofta Mixture: In a large bowl, combine ground beef, ground chicken, half of the finely diced red onion, minced fresh red chili, chopped parsley, minced garlic, cumin powder, coriander powder, paprika, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until well combined. Do not overmix.
Form Kofta: Divide the mixture into 12-16 equal portions. Shape each portion into an elongated oval or cylindrical kofta.

Roast Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut remaining red onion into thick wedges or petals. Cut Roma tomatoes into quarters or wedges. Toss vegetables with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until tender and slightly charred.

Cook Kofta: Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add kofta in batches. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Prepare Chili Yogurt (Optional): If desired, mix plain yogurt with a pinch of salt and a tiny bit of minced chili for a mild sauce.
Plate Dish: Arrange 3-4 kofta pieces per plate. Place roasted tomato and onion artfully around the kofta. Garnish with fresh parsley sprigs and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately.
notes: The kofta mixture can be prepared in advance and refrigerated for up to 24 hours.
Adjust chili quantity to preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken and Potato Fritters
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents three to four golden-brown, irregular-shaped crispy chicken and potato fritters arranged casually on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Each fritter has a visibly crisp, textured exterior from frying, revealing flecks of shredded chicken and grated potato within. Their warm, earthy tones are complemented by a small, white ramekin of creamy garlic dip positioned alongside. The dip is smooth and opaque, with a hint of minced garlic. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the fritters, adding a touch of freshness. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, warm light consistent with a cozy kitchen setting. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone rests nearby, completing the unpretentious, homely presentation.
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender. Drain and let cool slightly. Grate the cooled potatoes.
Shred cooked chicken into small pieces.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, grated potato, finely diced onion, minced garlic, egg, flour, salt, and pepper. Mix well until combined.
Form the mixture into small, flat patties, about 5-6 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick. This should yield about 12-16 fritters.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Carefully place fritters into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Fry fritters for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Transfer cooked fritters to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
To make the dip: In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, minced garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Serve fritters warm with the creamy garlic dip. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme, Pomme Purée, Black Garlic Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken supreme, skin-on and bone-in, rests centrally on a pristine, matte white bone china plate. The chicken skin is a deep, burnished golden-brown with visible crisp texture. Its flesh is moist, a delicate off-white. Beside it, a flowing, organic swirl of ultra-smooth, glossy ivory pomme purée creates a soft, inviting contrast. Three to four plump, translucent glazed pearl onions, their pale amber hue catching the light, are artfully positioned near the chicken. Elegant, dark charcoal-grey streaks of black garlic emulsion are painted with precision across the plate, providing a dramatic visual anchor and umami depth. A single, vibrant green sprig of fresh chervil is precisely placed atop the chicken, offering a final touch of color and freshness. The plate is surrounded by abundant negative space on a grey marble surface, dramatically lit with soft shadows.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Pat chicken supremes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
Peel and cut potatoes into 3cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain thoroughly. Pass potatoes through a food mill or fine sieve into a warm bowl.
Heat milk and 150g butter in a small saucepan until butter melts. Gradually whisk the hot milk-butter mixture into the sieved potatoes until smooth and creamy. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Combine black garlic, egg yolk, Dijon mustard, 15ml water, and a pinch of salt in a blender. Blend until very smooth. Slowly drizzle in neutral oil while blending until the mixture is emulsified and creamy. Adjust consistency with a little water if too thick.

Peel pearl onions. In a small saucepan, combine pearl onions, chicken stock, sugar, and remaining 50g butter. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook until the liquid reduces to a glossy glaze and onions are tender, about 10-12 minutes.

To plate, spoon an organic pool of pomme purée onto one side of a warm plate. Place one chicken supreme beside the purée. Artfully arrange three to four glazed pearl onions near the chicken. Drizzle or paint elegant streaks of black garlic emulsion across the plate. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh chervil or tarragon. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Fermented Onion Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly braised bone-in chicken thigh rests on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The chicken skin is a rich, caramelized golden-brown, showing crispy texture. A small, organic dollop of smooth, pale beige root vegetable puree, subtly textured, is positioned alongside the chicken. A generous spoonful of vibrant, translucent fermented red and brown onion relish, with its delicate, thin slices, is artfully placed atop the chicken, adding a pop of ruby and amber hues. A few small, fresh thyme leaves are scattered sparingly over the chicken and puree, providing a hint of natural green. The braising liquid, reduced to a glossy, deep amber sauce, lightly coats the chicken and pools minimally around its base. The overall presentation is clean, uncluttered, and focuses on the natural beauty and textures of each component. The plate is centered on a light, naturally textured bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded simply beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the food's organic forms. In the background, a hint of lush green foliage from a potted plant is visible, adding to the eco-conscious aesthetic. No ornate garnishes or elaborate arrangements; the dish embodies a simple, pure beauty.

ingredients.name: Mixed root vegetables (e.g., carrots, celeriac, parsnips)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Onion Relish: Thinly slice red and brown onions. Place in a clean jar. Add 10g sea salt. Massage onions until liquid releases. Cover with filtered water, ensuring onions are submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Refrigerate once desired tang is reached.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Sear Chicken: Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Flip. Sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken.
Sauté Aromatics: Add sliced brown onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Deglaze and Add Liquid: Pour in beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Add chicken stock and herb sprigs.

Braise Chicken: Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Liquid should come halfway up the chicken. Cover pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 170°C (340°F). Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Prepare Root Vegetable Puree: While chicken braises, peel and chop root vegetables into 2 cm chunks. Place in a pot. Cover with vegetable broth. Simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.

Blend Puree: Drain most liquid, reserving some. Blend cooked vegetables with plant-based milk and reserved broth until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Add plant-based butter if desired. Keep warm.
Finish Sauce: Remove chicken from pot. Discard herb sprigs. Skim any excess fat from braising liquid. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until slightly thickened and flavorful.

Plate Dish: Spoon a dollop of root vegetable puree onto each plate. Place one braised chicken thigh beside it. Drizzle chicken with the reduced braising sauce. Top chicken with a spoonful of fermented onion relish.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken, Pasta, and Brown Rice Gratin
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents as a hearty, golden-brown gratin, centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Large, irregular chunks of pan-seared chicken are visible, nestled among al dente penne pasta and individual grains of brown rice, all bound by a creamy sauce. A generous, bubbling layer of melted cheddar and mozzarella cheese forms a golden crust on top, with pockets of deeper caramelization. The rich tones of the cheese contrast with the lighter chicken and pasta, and the earthy brown of the rice. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is scattered over the top, providing a pop of color. The composition is professional and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface with a cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a casual restaurant background.
instructions: Cook brown rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Set aside.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Cut chicken into 2.5 cm chunks. Add chicken to skillet. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Return chicken to the skillet. Stir in cooked pasta and cooked brown rice. Mix well.
Stir in half of the grated cheddar and mozzarella cheese.
Top the mixture with the remaining cheddar and mozzarella cheese.
Bake in a preheated oven at 190°C for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly, and chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Gai Pad Med Ma Muang Hed Hom
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous portion of fragrant steamed jasmine rice is mounded neatly on one side. Adjacent to the rice, the vibrant Gai Pad Med Ma Muang Hed Hom is artfully arranged. Golden-brown chicken chunks are tossed with glossy red and green bell pepper squares, earthy sliced shiitake mushrooms, and tender white onion wedges, all coated in a rich, slightly viscous, reddish-brown sauce. The stir-fry is generously garnished with crunchy roasted cashews, vibrant green spring onion pieces cut into 3cm lengths, and a few crisp, dark red fried dried chilies. The colors are balanced and natural, with the deep tones of the sauce complementing the bright vegetables. Textures range from tender chicken and crisp-tender vegetables to the satisfying crunch of cashews. The plate maintains appropriate negative space, focusing entirely on the food. A set of chopsticks and a traditional Thai wide, shallow spoon are placed neatly beside the plate on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a subtle, blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a small bowl of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies) on the side for those who prefer extra seasoning.
instructions: Cook jasmine rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Cut chicken breast into 2cm bite-sized chunks.
Cut onion into wedges. Slice shiitake mushrooms. Cut red and green bell peppers into 2cm squares. Cut spring onions into 3cm lengths.
Mince garlic.
In a small bowl, whisk together oyster sauce, fish sauce, light soy sauce, sugar, Thai chili paste, and chicken stock. Set sauce aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add dried red chilies. Fry until crisp and slightly darkened, about 30 seconds. Remove chilies and set aside.
Add minced garlic to the wok. Stir-fry for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until chicken is almost cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add onion wedges, sliced mushrooms, red bell pepper squares, and green bell pepper squares to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Pour the prepared sauce mixture over the chicken and vegetables. Stir quickly to coat everything evenly. Cook for 1 minute until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in roasted cashews, spring onion pieces, and the fried dried chilies.
Remove from heat immediately. Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Lightly Fermented Tomato & Basil Polenta Cake with Whipped Mascarpone
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant portion of dessert rests on a round, unglazed ceramic plate in a soft cream hue. A golden-yellow, circular slice of Lemon Polenta Cake, showcasing its fine, slightly coarse texture, is positioned slightly off-center. Adjacent to the cake is a vibrant, glistening mound of Lightly Fermented Tomato & Basil Compote, displaying halved cherry tomatoes with their natural varied reds. Opposite the compote, a natural, un-piped dollop of creamy white Whipped Mascarpone sits. The composition forms a gentle triangle. A single small, fresh green basil leaf adorns the mascarpone, and a delicate, curled strip of lemon zest gracefully tops the polenta cake. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural lighting, highlighting the dish's pure ingredients and minimalist aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, celebrating the fresh flavors and textures.
Present on handcrafted, natural-material plates to emphasize sustainable aesthetics.
instructions: Halve cherry tomatoes. Combine with sugar, basil sprig, pinch of salt, and water in a clean jar. Stir well. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 12-24 hours until lightly macerated and fragrant. Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour four individual ramekins or a 20 cm round cake tin.
Cream softened butter and 100 g granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time until incorporated.
In a separate bowl, whisk together polenta, flour, baking powder, lemon zest, and pinch of salt.
Gradually fold dry ingredients into wet mixture. Stir in milk until just combined.
Pour batter into prepared ramekins. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Combine mascarpone cheese, icing sugar, and vanilla extract in a bowl. Whisk until light and creamy. Do not overmix.
Place a cooled polenta cake on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of lightly fermented tomato and basil compote alongside or on top.
Dollop whipped mascarpone next to the cake and compote. Garnish with a small basil leaf and a thin lemon zest strip.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste by utilizing lemon zest and basil leaves for both flavor and garnish, minimizing food scraps.
The light fermentation/maceration process enhances the natural sweetness and complexity of the tomatoes, aligning with sustainable preservation techniques.
traditional_techniques: Light fermentation/maceration for flavor development and preservation

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Baked Chicken with Mushrooms and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of rustic baked chicken, nestled in a rich, bubbling tomato and mushroom sauce, served on a simple, round ceramic plate. The chicken thigh, with its golden-brown, crisped skin, is partially submerged in the deep red, chunky sauce. Melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese forms a golden-brown crust over the chicken and sauce, with some parts slightly caramelized. Earthy brown mushroom slices and tender diced onions are visible within the sauce. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley contrasts with the warm colors. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Standard, simple cutlery is placed beside the plate. Warm, natural lighting from a kitchen fixture illuminates the dish, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. The overall scene is homely and unpretentious, with natural imperfections in the ceramic and a lived-in feel.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until browned and liquid evaporates.
Stir in minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove skillet from oven. Sprinkle mozzarella cheese evenly over chicken and sauce.
Return to oven for 5-10 minutes, until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken with Olives and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Chicken with Olives and Tomatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown seared chicken thighs, left whole, are centrally placed, partially submerged in a vibrant, rustic tomato-olive sauce. The sauce is rich red from the halved cherry tomatoes, some slightly burst, and dotted with dark, glossy Kalamata olives. Thinly sliced garlic and chili flecks are visible within the sauce. A scattering of fresh, bright green basil leaves provides a pop of color and freshness over the chicken and sauce. The textures are varied: crisp-skinned chicken, tender meat, soft tomatoes, and firm olives. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and warm colors against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add thinly sliced garlic and chili to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add halved cherry tomatoes, dried oregano, and chicken broth to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Add pitted Kalamata olives around the chicken. Cover the pan.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pan. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Reduce sauce slightly if desired. Adjust seasoning.
Serve chicken with the tomato-olive sauce. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper & Asparagus Bruschetta
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Roasted Bell Pepper & Asparagus Bruschetta rests on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table in a cozy, homely kitchen. Each thick slice of toasted sourdough bread, lightly golden and crisp, is topped generously with vibrant red diced tomatoes, roasted red bell pepper strips, and tender green asparagus batons. The roasted vegetables show slight charring. A few fresh, deep green basil leaves are scattered over the topping. A small, simple olive oil cruet and a crumpled linen napkin are casually placed nearby. Warm, natural light streams from a nearby window, illuminating the textures. The scene evokes a relaxed, inviting family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as an antipasto or starter.
Offer a small bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for additional drizzling.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cut bell pepper into 2 cm wide strips. Trim woody ends from asparagus, cut spears into 4 cm batons.
Toss bell pepper and asparagus with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.
While vegetables roast, dice tomatoes into small cubes. Place in a bowl.
Finely mince 2 garlic cloves. Roughly chop most of the basil leaves, reserving some small leaves for garnish.
Add minced garlic and chopped basil to diced tomatoes. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well.
Slice bread. Drizzle both sides of each slice with olive oil.
Toast bread in a dry pan or on a grill until golden and crisp. This takes 2-3 minutes per side.
Cut the remaining 2 garlic cloves in half. Rub the cut side of garlic over one side of each toasted bread slice.
Spoon the tomato mixture generously onto each toasted bread slice. Arrange roasted bell pepper strips and asparagus batons over the tomato.
Garnish with reserved fresh basil leaves. Drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Lemon-Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared salmon is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, placed on a simple light wooden table surface. The salmon fillet features a crisp, golden-brown skin and tender, flaky pink flesh. It is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. A vibrant, glistening lemon-basil sauce, infused with finely diced sautéed onion and minced garlic, is generously spooned over and around the salmon. Beside the salmon, a neat cluster of bright green, crisp-tender asparagus spears is arranged, alongside several halved crimson cherry tomatoes. Thin, translucent slices of fresh lemon and vibrant green basil leaves are artfully placed as garnish, adding fresh color and aroma. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its fresh ingredients and textures against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a light white wine like Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon skin-side down. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip salmon. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until cooked through. Remove salmon from pan. Set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add asparagus and cherry tomatoes. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Season with salt.
Melt butter in the pan. Add finely diced onion. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in broth and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in roughly chopped fresh basil. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Place salmon on plates. Spoon lemon-basil sauce over salmon. Arrange sautéed asparagus and cherry tomatoes alongside. Garnish with fresh lemon slices and extra basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Ricotta & Mushroom Stuffed Chicken Breast with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A seared, golden-brown chicken breast, generously stuffed with creamy ricotta and savory sautéed mushrooms, rests prominently on a classic round white porcelain plate. The chicken is halved diagonally to reveal the rich, textured filling. A vibrant, rustic red tomato-garlic sauce pools underneath and around the chicken, reflecting light. Beside it, a cluster of golden, crispy roasted potato wedges, seasoned with oregano, provides a comforting textural contrast. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the sauce and chicken for a pop of color and freshness. The setting features a simple wooden table, a neatly folded white linen napkin, and classic silver flatware. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's warmth. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced, inviting single portion with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette dressing complements the richness of the dish.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, 1 finely diced for stuffing, 1 finely diced for sauce

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 800g, peeled and cut into 2 cm wedges

ingredients.name: Bread
ingredients.quantity: 2 slices, for breadcrumbs and garlic bread

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C).

Prepare stuffing: Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan. Sauté 1 finely diced onion and 200g finely diced mushrooms over medium heat until tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add 2 minced garlic cloves; cook 1 minute more. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
In a bowl, combine cooled mushroom mixture with 250g ricotta cheese, 50g breadcrumbs (from 1 slice of bread), 5g dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Mix well.

Prepare chicken: Butterfly each chicken breast. Season inside and out with salt and pepper. Divide stuffing mixture evenly among chicken breasts. Fold chicken over stuffing. Secure edges with toothpicks.
Sear chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken breasts 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan.

Make sauce: In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté remaining 1 finely diced onion and 2 minced garlic cloves until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Stir in 800g crushed tomatoes and remaining 5g dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer.

Roast potatoes: On a separate baking tray, toss 800g potato wedges with 15ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, pepper, and dried oregano. Roast in preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until golden and tender.
Finish chicken: Carefully place seared chicken breasts back into the simmering tomato sauce in the pan. Sprinkle 100g grated mozzarella cheese over the chicken. Transfer pan to the oven.
Bake chicken for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Prepare garlic bread: While chicken bakes, melt 20g butter. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves and mix with butter. Spread on remaining bread slice. Toast until golden.

Serve: Carefully remove chicken from oven. Plate one stuffed chicken breast with a generous portion of tomato sauce. Arrange roasted potato wedges beside it. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately with garlic bread.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Toothpicks can be removed before serving or advised to guests.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Oat & Cottage Cheese Bowl with Seared Banana & Honey Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the dish is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The base is a mound of creamy, savory steel-cut oats, showcasing their slightly coarse yet tender texture and warm, earthy tones. A smooth, pale green (from herbs) whipped cottage cheese is elegantly dolloped on top, creating a soft contrast. Three to four golden-brown seared banana medallions, cut into thick, circular slices, are artfully arranged around the cottage cheese. A thin, glistening drizzle of golden honey crisscrosses the dish, catching the light. The dish is finished with a sprinkle of small, dark, toasted chia seeds and vibrant green finely chopped chives, adding visual texture and fresh color. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. Standard, clean flatware is placed beside the bowl on a folded cotton napkin. The setting features natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Finely dice shallot. Mince garlic.
Chop chives and parsley for cottage cheese. Reserve some for garnish.
Combine cottage cheese with half of chopped chives and parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Blend until smooth and creamy using a food processor or immersion blender. Set aside.
Heat olive oil and 15 g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced shallot. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add steel-cut oats to the saucepan. Toast lightly for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring occasionally, until most liquid is absorbed, about 15-20 minutes.

Gradually stir in milk, a little at a time, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding more. Continue cooking until oats are creamy and tender, about 10-15 more minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Slice bananas into 1.5 cm thick medallions.
Heat remaining 15 g butter in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add banana medallions in a single layer. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and slightly caramelized.
Lightly toast chia seeds in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Be careful not to burn.
To serve, spoon creamy oats into individual bowls. Create a slight well in the center.
Dollop a generous spoonful of the whipped herbed cottage cheese into the well.
Arrange 3-4 seared banana medallions artfully around the cottage cheese.
Drizzle honey lightly over the entire dish.
Garnish with toasted chia seeds and reserved fresh chives and parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef Croquettes with Gochujang Aioli
recipes.visual_description: The Spicy Beef Croquettes are presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, arranged in a small, appealing mound. Each croquette is a golden-brown oval, approximately 5cm long, with a visibly crispy panko crust. Several croquettes are stacked loosely, showcasing their inviting texture. Beside the croquettes, a dollop of vibrant, reddish-orange Gochujang Aioli sits, providing a striking color contrast. A sprinkle of thinly sliced bright green scallions garnishes both the croquettes and the aioli, adding freshness. The overall plating is clean and professional, with ample negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting. A folded cotton napkin rests casually beside the plate. The background is minimal, suggesting a relaxed restaurant atmosphere, keeping the focus entirely on the inviting snack.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an 'anju', a Korean drinking snack, alongside beer or soju.
Present as an appetizer or side dish for a casual meal.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well. Mash until smooth.
Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add beef mince. Cook until browned, breaking it up. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger to the beef. Cook 3-5 minutes until softened.
Stir in 15g gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar. Cook 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Combine cooked beef mixture with mashed potatoes in a large bowl. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.
Shape mixture into 12-16 oval or cylindrical croquettes, about 5cm long.
Set up a breading station: one shallow bowl with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with panko breadcrumbs.
Roll each croquette first in flour, then dip in beaten egg, then roll in panko. Ensure a full, even coating.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 170°C.
Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
For the Gochujang Aioli: Combine mayonnaise and 30g gochujang in a small bowl. Mix until smooth.
Serve hot croquettes immediately with the Gochujang Aioli. Garnish generously with thinly sliced scallions.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Lamb Shanks with Lemon-Basil Gremolata and Garlic Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly plated braised lamb shank rests atop a bed of creamy, chunky garlic smashed potatoes on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The lamb shank, dark brown and glistening from its long braise, is fork-tender and appears to be falling off the bone. A rich, deep reddish-brown braising sauce, reduced to a luscious sheen, pools around the base of the lamb and gently coats the potatoes. A vibrant, finely chopped lemon-basil gremolata, a mix of bright green basil flecks, yellow lemon zest, and tiny white garlic bits, is generously sprinkled over the lamb and potatoes, providing a striking contrast in color and texture. The potatoes are off-white with visible small lumps, indicating a rustic smashed texture. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. The setting features traditional Italian flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the rich sauce.
Pair with a full-bodied Italian red wine.
instructions: Pat lamb shanks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear lamb shanks until deeply browned on all sides. Remove shanks from pot.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef/lamb stock. Add rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Return lamb shanks to the pot. Ensure shanks are mostly submerged; add more stock if needed.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until lamb is very tender and falling off the bone.
While lamb braises, boil potatoes. Place potatoes in a large pot with cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until fork-tender, about 20-25 minutes. Drain thoroughly.
Return hot potatoes to the pot. Add butter, warm milk, and minced garlic. Mash roughly with a potato masher or fork until chunky and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, combine finely chopped basil, lemon zest, lemon juice, and minced garlic. Mix well.

Carefully remove lamb shanks from the braising liquid. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Return strained sauce to the pot and reduce slightly over medium heat if desired, until it coats the back of a spoon.

Place a generous portion of garlic smashed potatoes on each plate. Top with a braised lamb shank. Spoon rich braising sauce over the lamb and potatoes. Garnish generously with fresh lemon-basil gremolata.
notes: Braising time may vary based on lamb shank size and oven consistency.
The sauce can be made ahead and reheated.

recipes.recipe_name: Butternut Squash & Poached Chicken Salad with Compressed Pear and Brown Butter-Thyme Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an exquisite, matte white ceramic plate with a wide rim, set upon a polished grey marble surface. Abundant negative space surrounds the central composition. Roasted butternut squash cubes, golden-orange and slightly caramelized, are artfully scattered across one side of the plate. Three small, irregularly shaped chunks of perfectly poached chicken, pristine white and tender, are nestled among the squash. Translucent, thinly sliced compressed pear, with a delicate sheen, is draped elegantly over select pieces of squash and chicken. A delicate drizzle of golden-brown butter vinaigrette glistens on the ingredients, enhancing their natural colors. A small, ethereal cloud of light, white milk-thyme emulsion foam rests precisely beside the main components, adding a subtle textural contrast. A few vibrant green microgreens are meticulously placed as a final, precise garnish. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows that highlight the textures and dimensions of each element, emphasizing a sense of refined simplicity and culinary artistry.
instructions: Combine milk, thyme sprigs, bay leaf, 1 tsp salt, and peppercorns in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add chicken breast. Poach gently for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken.
Strain milk; reserve 50ml for emulsion. Cool chicken completely. Cut chicken into small, irregular chunks.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel, deseed, and cut butternut squash into 1.5 cm cubes or elegant batons.
Toss squash with olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized. Cool slightly.
Peel, core, and very thinly slice the pear (mandoline preferred).
Combine 1 tbsp lemon juice, water, and sugar. Submerge thinly sliced pear in this liquid. Press firmly between parchment paper and heavy objects for 30 minutes, or vacuum seal for 15 minutes.
Melt unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until foamy and butter solids turn golden brown and nutty. Remove from heat.
Immediately whisk in 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, white wine vinegar, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Keep warm.
Gently warm the reserved 50ml strained milk. Add fresh thyme leaves. Use an immersion blender to create a light foam or emulsion.
Arrange a few roasted butternut squash cubes artistically on a fine-dining plate. Place 2-3 small chicken chunks among the squash.
Drape a few compressed pear slices elegantly over the components. Drizzle brown butter vinaigrette sparingly over the salad.
Spoon a small amount of milk-thyme emulsion foam beside the main components. Garnish with a few microgreens or small thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Dijon Cream and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, robust braised chicken thigh, skin golden-brown and slightly crisp, rests atop a bed of golden-roasted potato chunks. The chicken is generously coated with a creamy, pale yellow Dijon sauce, which pools invitingly around the base. Bright red roasted cherry tomatoes, some whole and some slightly burst, are scattered artfully around the chicken and potatoes. Fresh green chopped parsley or chives are lightly sprinkled over the dish for a pop of color. The arrangement is organic yet refined, with moderate negative space on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The setting features a simple wooden table, a silver fork and knife, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the delicious sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine like Sauvignon Blanc or Chardonnay.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs, skin-side down. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown. Flip and sear other side 2 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to skillet. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine (if using), scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in chicken stock and Dijon mustard. Add 2 thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to skillet, skin-side up. Transfer skillet to oven. Braise 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
While chicken braises, toss potato chunks and halved tomatoes with remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast in oven for 20-25 minutes, until potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove chicken from skillet. Place on a plate. Cover loosely to keep warm.
Place skillet on stovetop over medium-high heat. Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce by one-third. Stir in heavy cream and butter. Whisk until sauce thickens slightly.
Discard thyme sprigs from sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Plate roasted potatoes on a white porcelain dinner plate. Arrange one braised chicken thigh on top. Spoon generous amount of Dijon cream sauce over chicken. Scatter roasted tomatoes around the plate. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.
notes: For extra flavor, consider marinating chicken thighs in a little olive oil, salt, pepper, and a pinch of paprika for at least 30 minutes before searing.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Lamb Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Braised Lamb Ragu with Pappardelle is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Long, broad pappardelle ribbons are generously coated in a rich, dark red ragu. Visible shredded lamb chunks are intertwined within the pasta, showcasing its tender texture. The sauce is thick and glossy, clinging beautifully to every strand. A scattering of vibrant green, roughly torn fresh basil leaves is spread naturally over the top, complemented by fine bright yellow lemon zest. A light, even dusting of pale yellow grated Parmesan cheese finishes the dish. The overall composition is organic and flowing, creating a slightly mounded appearance in the center of the bowl. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin with a silver fork and spoon lies beside the bowl. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights the dish's colors and textures, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a robust Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Pat lamb chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear lamb chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove lamb and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce wine by half.
Return seared lamb to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F) or reduce heat to low and simmer gently on the stovetop for 2.5-3 hours, or until lamb is very tender.
Remove lamb from the sauce. Using two forks, shred the lamb meat. Discard any large fatty pieces. Return shredded lamb to the sauce. Stir well.
Simmer the ragu gently for 15-20 minutes to allow it to thicken slightly. Stir in fresh basil leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cook pappardelle in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving about 125ml of pasta water.
Add drained pasta to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to achieve a smooth, clinging consistency.
Serve immediately in deep bowls. Garnish each portion with fresh lemon zest and a generous dusting of grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: This ragu can be made ahead of time; its flavors deepen and improve overnight.
Leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 3 months.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Saltimbocca
recipes.visual_description: Two golden-brown, pan-seared chicken cutlets are elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, slightly overlapping. Each tender chicken cutlet is topped with a thin slice of crispy, savory prosciutto and a vibrant green sage leaf, secured subtly. A glossy, pale yellow pan sauce, infused with white wine and lemon, is generously spooned over and around the chicken, creating a delicate pool. A small, fresh sprig of bright green Italian parsley is placed beside the chicken as a vibrant garnish, adding a pop of color. The dish is arranged with moderate negative space, allowing the golden hues of the chicken and the rich texture of the prosciutto to stand out. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware positioned beside the plate, creating a modern bistro atmosphere under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with a side of simple pasta like spaghetti aglio e olio or roasted asparagus.
Pair with a glass of dry Italian white wine such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Slice each chicken breast horizontally to create two thin cutlets.
Pound each chicken cutlet to 5mm thickness.
Place 1-2 sage leaves on each cutlet. Top with one slice of prosciutto.
Secure prosciutto and sage to chicken with a toothpick.
Lightly dredge each chicken cutlet in flour. Shake off excess flour.
Heat olive oil and 15g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cutlets, prosciutto-side down, for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pan. Keep warm.
Add remaining 15g butter to the pan. Melt.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken broth. Simmer for 2 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Stir in juice from half a lemon. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return chicken to the pan briefly to coat in sauce.
Remove toothpicks before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken cutlets are pounded to an even thickness for uniform cooking.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing; cook chicken in batches if necessary to maintain pan temperature and achieve a good sear.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo y Fideos
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo y Fideos is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous mound of vibrant, golden-orange rice and short pasta (fideo) forms the base, its surface studded with small, tender diced red and green bell peppers and onion. The rice grains are separate yet moist, infused with rich tomato and spice flavors. Nestled atop the rice is a single, perfectly seared chicken thigh, its skin a deep golden-brown, presented whole. The dish is garnished with bright green chopped fresh cilantro and vivid red roasted pimiento strips. A fresh lime wedge rests on the plate's side. The setting includes a simple wooden table, standard flatware, and a folded white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting. The background suggests a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with lime wedges for added freshness.
Can be accompanied by a simple green salad or fried plantains.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads (optional, or 2g turmeric for color)
Roasted red pimientos, cut into strips, for garnish
Lime, cut into wedges, for serving

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden-brown on all sides. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, and saffron (or turmeric). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add rice and fideo. Stir well to coat. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add bay leaves. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Serve immediately with chopped fresh cilantro, pimiento strips, and lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Shaking Beef with Garlic Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Vietnamese Shaking Beef (Bo Luc Lac) and Garlic Fried Rice, presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Cubes of seared beef, approximately 2.5 cm, exhibit a rich, caramelized brown crust, revealing a tender, pinkish interior. They are casually mounded beside a generous portion of pale golden garlic fried rice, studded with finely minced, lightly toasted garlic bits. A vibrant green side salad of crisp watercress, thinly sliced cucumbers, and bright red tomato wedges is neatly arranged next to the beef. Fresh, glossy green Thai basil leaves are scattered over the beef and rice for aromatic garnish. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface with a linen napkin and chopsticks positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the contrasting textures and colors in a professional, approachable manner.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a lime-salt-pepper dipping sauce.
Accompanied by a side salad of watercress, sliced tomatoes, and cucumbers.
Eaten with chopsticks.
instructions: Cut beef into 2.5 cm cubes.

In a bowl, combine beef cubes with 2 minced garlic cloves, 1 tbsp soy sauce, oyster sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 0.5 tsp black pepper, and 1 tbsp vegetable oil. Mix well. Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours refrigerated.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or non-stick pan over medium heat. Add 6 minced garlic cloves. Sauté until fragrant and lightly golden, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked rice. Break up any clumps. Increase heat to medium-high. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until rice is heated through and slightly toasted.
Add 1 tbsp soy sauce, 0.5 tsp sugar, and white pepper to the rice. Stir well to combine. Transfer to a serving platter or individual bowls. Keep warm.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in the same wok or large pan over high heat until smoking. Add thinly sliced shallot (if using) and stir-fry for 15 seconds.
Add marinated beef cubes in a single layer. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Sear beef for 1-2 minutes per side until browned and caramelized.
Quickly toss the beef to ensure even cooking, about 3-4 minutes total for medium-rare.
For the dipping sauce, combine lime juice, fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 minced garlic clove, and 0.5 tsp black pepper in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Arrange cooked beef alongside garlic fried rice on plates. Place watercress, cucumber slices, and tomato wedges as a side salad.
Garnish beef and rice with fresh Thai basil leaves. Serve immediately with the lime dipping sauce on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna and Corn Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Seared Tuna and Corn Salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. Three to four thick, seared tuna medallions, displaying a pink interior with a thin browned crust, are neatly arranged on one side. They are not fanned. Adjacent, a vibrant mound of crisp mixed salad greens forms the base, interspersed with bright yellow blanched corn kernels and delicate, thin cucumber ribbons. The dish is lightly glossed with a subtle, dark amber dressing. A scattering of white toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced green spring onion rounds garnish the tuna and salad. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, with a blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of steamed jasmine rice on the side for a more substantial meal if desired.
instructions: Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated ginger, minced garlic, and honey (if using). Set aside.
Prepare vegetables: Wash and dry salad greens. Cut cucumber into thin ribbons using a peeler, or julienne into thin sticks. Blanch corn kernels in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and cool.
Season tuna: Pat tuna loins dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.

Sear tuna: Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until smoking. Carefully place tuna loins in the hot pan. Sear for 1-2 minutes per side for rare-medium rare. The center should remain pink.
Rest and slice tuna: Remove tuna from pan. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes. Slice tuna against the grain into 1 cm thick medallions.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, gently toss salad greens, cucumber, and corn with half of the dressing.
Plate dish: Divide dressed salad among 4 plates. Arrange tuna medallions neatly beside or on top of the salad.
Garnish: Drizzle remaining dressing over tuna and salad. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust tuna searing time to your preferred doneness.
