Peel potatoes. Slice thinly into 2-3 mm rounds using a mandoline or sharp knife.
Melt butter in a pan over medium heat. Sauté shallot until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Arrange a single layer of potato slices in the prepared baking dish. Season lightly with salt, pepper, and a tiny pinch of nutmeg.
Sprinkle a portion of the grated Gruyère over the potatoes. Scatter some sautéed shallot and garlic.
Repeat layering: potatoes, seasoning, cheese, shallot-garlic mixture, until all ingredients are used. Finish with a layer of potatoes.
Pour the saffron-infused milk and cream mixture evenly over the potatoes. Ensure liquid reaches all layers.
Cover the baking dish loosely with foil. Bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil. Increase oven temperature to 200°C. Bake for another 25-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly.
While gratin bakes, toss cherry tomatoes with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a separate baking tray. Roast alongside gratin for the last 15-20 minutes, until slightly burst and caramelized.
Remove gratin from oven. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Cut gratin into generous portions. Serve immediately with roasted cherry tomatoes and a sprinkle of fresh thyme leaves.
notes: For best results, use a mandoline to slice potatoes uniformly thin, ensuring even cooking.
The resting period allows the gratin to set, making it easier to portion cleanly.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Baked Chicken and Rice rests on a round, light-colored ceramic plate. Two golden-brown, bone-in chicken thighs, seared to a crisp skin, are nestled atop a bed of fluffy, seasoned long-grain rice. The rice shows subtle flecks of diced onion and minced garlic, with a warm, natural off-white hue. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a touch of color. The plate sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in soft, natural light from a nearby window. A casually folded linen napkin lies beside the plate. The overall scene exudes a homely, comforting, and unpretentious family meal aesthetic. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced or fanned.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with salt, pepper, paprika, and dried thyme.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, placing them on top of the rice, skin-side up.
Cover the skillet tightly with a lid or foil.
Bake for 25 minutes. Remove lid/foil; bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and rice is tender and liquid absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Use a deep oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven to prevent overflow.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Tomato Basil Risotto and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Tomato Basil Risotto and Roasted Broccoli is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, vibrant orange-red risotto forms a generous, free-flowing base, not mounded, with visible flecks of crushed tomato and torn green basil. Two thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken medallions, with a slight crust, are carefully placed on one side of the risotto. Scattered alongside the chicken and partially nestled into the risotto are bright green, tender-crisp roasted broccoli florets and softened, slightly charred red cherry tomato halves. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the dish. Fresh, bright green basil leaves, some whole, some gently torn, are artfully placed on top of the chicken and risotto, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware (fork and knife) positioned to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss broccoli florets and halved cherry tomatoes with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Set aside.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions or keep whole.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat remaining 30ml olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine (if using). Stir until completely absorbed.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well. Cook 2-3 minutes.
Begin adding warm chicken broth, one ladle (about 120ml) at a time. Stir constantly.
Wait until most liquid is absorbed before adding the next ladle of broth.
Continue this process for 18-20 minutes, until rice is al dente and risotto is creamy and fluid.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in unsalted butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves, torn.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle creamy risotto onto individual plates.
Arrange pan-seared chicken medallions and roasted broccoli/cherry tomatoes over the risotto.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Squash & Potato Fritters with Tomato-Onion Relish
recipes.visual_description: The snack features golden-brown, rustic fritters arranged casually on a light, natural-textured ceramic plate, possibly with a subtle handmade feel. Each fritter, roughly 7cm in diameter and 1.5cm thick, displays the visible textures of grated squash and potato, showcasing a slightly irregular, crispy edge and a soft, earthy interior. A small, vibrant dollop of the rich red tomato-onion relish sits atop each fritter, providing a contrasting pop of color and glossy texture. The relish contains visible small diced tomato and onion pieces. The plate is kept clean with ample white space, emphasizing the natural beauty and simplicity of the ingredients. A scattering of freshly chopped green parsley or chives provides a delicate, natural garnish. The setting is minimalist, with a light-colored wooden or stone surface, and soft, diffused natural light enhancing the food's organic textures. The presentation is unfussy, highlighting the ingredients' pure form and the sustainable ethos.
instructions: Combine grated squash, potato, and thinly sliced red onion in a large bowl. Add 7g salt. Massage ingredients thoroughly for 5 minutes until liquid releases.

Pack mixture tightly into a clean glass jar. Press down firmly to remove air pockets and ensure vegetables are fully submerged in their own liquid. If not enough liquid, add a small amount of filtered water to cover. Place a small weight on top to keep vegetables submerged.

Seal jar with an airlock lid or cover loosely to allow gas escape. Let ferment at room temperature (18-22°C) for 2-3 days. Taste daily. When slightly tangy and bubbly, it is ready. Remove weight. Refrigerate to slow fermentation.

Combine diced tomatoes, minced garlic, apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, and 3g salt in a small saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Season with pepper. Set aside.
Drain fermented vegetable mixture. Squeeze out excess liquid using a clean cloth. Reserve liquid for other uses.
In a bowl, combine drained vegetables with chickpea flour and baking powder. Mix well.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Spoon 30g portions of mixture into the pan, flattening slightly into fritters (approx. 7cm diameter).
Cook 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Repeat with remaining mixture.
Arrange fritters on a serving plate. Top each with a spoonful of tomato-onion relish. Garnish with fresh parsley or chives.
notes: The liquid drained from the fermented vegetables is rich in probiotics and flavor; use it as a base for dressings, soups, or rehydrating dried vegetables.
Squash and potato skins can be left on if organic and thin, reducing food waste. Otherwise, skins can be roasted into crisps.
Squash seeds can be roasted for a crunchy snack or garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Pork Ragu with Pappardelle, Roasted Potatoes, and Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Cooked Pork Ragu with Pappardelle, Roasted Potatoes, and Poached Egg is presented in a deep white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The rich, dark red-brown ragu, with tender pork chunks, is intertwined with wide pappardelle ribbons. Golden-brown roasted potato cubes, 2 cm, are scattered around the pasta. A perfectly poached egg, with its vibrant yellow yolk visible, sits atop the ragu. The dish is garnished with grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. A cotton napkin and traditional flatware are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the food, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for soaking up the ragu.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500 g, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Pat pork shoulder dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly golden. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and paste darkens slightly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3 minutes until wine reduces by half.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs. Stir well.
Bring ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 2.5-3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally. Remove bay leaves and thyme stems before serving.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Toss diced potatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until golden brown and tender.
Just before serving, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pappardelle according to package directions until al dente.

While pasta cooks, gently poach 4 eggs. Bring a pot of water to a simmer with a splash of vinegar. Crack each egg into a small bowl first, then carefully slide into simmering water. Cook 3-4 minutes for a runny yolk.
Drain pasta. Toss pasta with a few ladles of the pork ragu. Add more ragu as desired.
To serve, place a portion of ragu and pasta in each deep bowl. Arrange roasted potato cubes around the pasta. Gently place one poached egg on top of each serving.
Garnish generously with grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: For the best flavor, make the ragu a day in advance. Flavors deepen overnight.
Ensure pork is well-browned during searing for a richer ragu.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cucumber & Umami Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of clear, light golden broth is presented in a handcrafted, creamy beige ceramic bowl, centered on a light bamboo table surface. The broth holds tender, 1cm diced cucumber pieces and golden-seared 1.5cm tofu cubes, visible beneath the surface. Thin, vibrant green cucumber ribbons are elegantly draped over the bowl's rim, adding a natural, organic flow. A sprinkle of finely sliced spring onion greens and a small sprig of fresh dill rest gently atop the broth. The minimalist composition highlights the natural colors and textures: the crisp green of cucumber, the creamy white and golden crust of tofu, and the clear, inviting warmth of the broth. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige and a simple ceramic spoon accompany the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, with a clean, unobtrusive background featuring subtle hints of natural greenery.
instructions: Rehydrate dried shiitake mushrooms in 500ml warm water for 20 minutes. Reserve mushroom liquid. If using fresh mushrooms, slice caps and reserve stems.

Combine mushroom rehydration liquid (or 500ml fresh water), remaining 1 litre water, kombu, mushroom stems (if using fresh), 20g sliced ginger, 3 crushed garlic cloves, and white parts of 2 spring onions in a pot. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 20 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids.
Cut one cucumber into 1cm dice. Using a vegetable peeler, create thin ribbons from the second cucumber. Reserve a few ribbons for garnish.
Press tofu for 15 minutes to remove excess water. Cut into 1.5cm cubes.
Heat a pan with a little oil. Sear tofu cubes until golden on all sides. Set aside.
In the strained broth, whisk in miso paste until dissolved. Add soy sauce and rice vinegar.
Add diced cucumber to the broth. Simmer for 3 minutes. Do not boil.
Taste broth and adjust salt if needed.
Ladle soup into individual serving bowls. Arrange seared tofu cubes in each bowl.
Garnish with cucumber ribbons, thinly sliced remaining spring onion greens, and a few drops of toasted sesame oil. Add fresh dill or mint sprigs if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Slavic Chicken and Rice Croquettes with Cheesy Tomato Core
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, oblong croquettes are artfully arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Each croquette features a crisp, textured exterior. The interior reveals a tender, moist mixture of finely shredded chicken, fluffy white rice, and mashed potato, flecked with bright orange grated carrot. At the heart of each croquette is a vibrant, molten core of rich red tomato and creamy, melted cheese, creating a delightful contrast. The croquettes are presented on a simple wooden board, with a small ramekin of sour cream for dipping. Fresh dill sprigs are scattered for color and aroma. The scene is set on a light wooden table with natural, even lighting, conveying a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere. Portions are generous, with three to four croquettes per serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream (smetana).

ingredients.name: Meltable cheese (e.g., mozzarella or mild cheddar)

instructions: Boil chicken breast until cooked through. Shred finely or mince. Set aside.
Cook rice according to package directions. Cool completely.
Peel and boil potatoes until tender. Mash thoroughly. Cool.
Peel and finely grate the carrot. Sauté in a small amount of oil until softened. Cool.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, cooked rice, mashed potatoes, and sautéed carrot. Season with salt and black pepper. Mix well to form a cohesive mixture.
For the core, grate the cheese. In a small bowl, mix grated cheese with tomato paste until well combined.
Take a portion of the chicken-rice mixture (about 50g). Flatten it into an oval in your palm. Place a small amount (about 5g) of the cheesy tomato mixture in the center.
Carefully enclose the filling with the chicken-rice mixture, shaping it into an oblong croquette. Ensure the filling is fully sealed inside.
Set up a breading station: one plate with flour, one bowl with beaten egg, and one plate with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each croquette in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Roll in breadcrumbs, pressing gently to ensure full coating.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Oil should be deep enough to cover half of the croquettes.
Fry croquettes in batches for 4-6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Garnish with fresh dill before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef and Pork Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Cooked Beef and Pork Ragu with Pappardelle is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Wide, golden pappardelle noodles are loosely coiled, generously coated in the rich, deep reddish-brown ragu. Visible are large, tender chunks of braised beef and pork, nestled amongst the pasta, showcasing their succulent texture. A generous mound of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese crowns the dish, adding a snowy contrast. A few vibrant green leaves of fresh basil or parsley are placed artfully for a pop of color. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a white linen napkin, and a silver fork beside the plate, all under soft, natural lighting, creating a warm, inviting, and authentic Italian bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
Offer with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Pat beef and pork dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown meat on all sides until deeply caramelized. Remove meat and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring often, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, milk, bay leaves, and rosemary sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Return browned meat to the pot. Ensure meat is mostly submerged. Cover and simmer on low heat for 3-4 hours. Meat should be fork-tender. Internal temperature of pork and beef should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove meat from pot. Discard bay leaves and rosemary sprigs. Shred or pull the meat into large tender chunks.
Return shredded meat to the sauce. Simmer uncovered for 20-30 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately with a generous grating of Parmigiano-Reggiano and fresh herbs.
notes: The longer the ragu simmers, the more complex and tender the flavors become.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Veal Bites with Crispy Macaroni, Cauliflower-Potato Puree, and Basil Mustard Aioli
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, high-contrast composition on a large, matte black or white bone china sharing platter. Central to the plate are several rustic, dark-glazed braised veal chunks, showcasing their fork-tender texture and rich, deep brown hue. Adjacent, a perfectly smooth, ivory-colored cauliflower-potato puree forms an organic, flowing swoosh, its velvety surface reflecting soft light. Scattered with architectural precision are golden, crispy macaroni pieces, each a delicate, airy crunch, providing textural counterpoint. A vibrant, emerald-green basil mustard aioli is strategically dotted or lightly drizzled, offering a bright pop of color and creamy tang. Freshly blanched green bean batons, bright and tender-crisp, are artfully placed alongside a small, verdant cluster of delicate sunflower sprouts, adding height and natural vitality. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing their distinct forms and textures. The setting is a polished grey marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin and dramatic, focused lighting creating elegant shadows.
instructions: Season veal chunks with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear veal until deeply browned on all sides. Remove veal.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Deglaze with beer, scraping up any browned bits. Add stock. Return veal to the pot.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until veal is fork-tender. Remove veal, reduce braising liquid slightly if desired. Keep veal warm.

In a separate pot, combine diced potatoes and cauliflower florets. Cover with water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Return vegetables to the hot pot to dry for 1 minute.
Add butter and American cheese slices to the vegetables. Mash or pass through a ricer. Blend with an immersion blender until completely smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Spread macaroni on a baking sheet lined with paper towels to dry completely.

In a small pot, heat vegetable oil to 175°C. Fry macaroni in small batches until golden brown and crispy, about 1-2 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
In a small blender or food processor, combine mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and fresh basil leaves. Blend until smooth and basil is fully incorporated. Season with a pinch of salt.
Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Add green beans. Blanch for 2 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain thoroughly.

On a large, elegant sharing platter or individual designer plates, artfully arrange the components. Place a few braised veal chunks. Spoon a generous dollop or swoosh of the smooth cauliflower-potato puree. Scatter crispy macaroni around. Drizzle the basil mustard aioli strategically. Arrange a few blanched green bean batons and a small cluster of sunflower sprouts. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Biryani served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features a mound of long-grain Basmati rice. The rice displays a natural color variation from pale white to deep orange-yellow from the spice infusion. Two large, bone-in chicken thigh chunks are nestled within the rice. The chicken is tender and coated in a thick, savory masala. Topping the rice are thin, golden-brown fried onion strips and vibrant green sprigs of fresh coriander. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. A small ceramic bowl of white yogurt raita sits to the side. The background is a dark wood bistro table with a folded linen napkin and a polished brass spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cucumber raita
Accompany with lime wedges and sliced raw red onions
Traditional brass or copper serving spoon

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into large chunks

instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in water for 30 minutes.
Mix chicken chunks with yogurt, spice mix, ginger-garlic paste, and 5g salt. Marinate for 1 hour.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot. Fry sliced onions until dark golden brown. Remove half for garnish.
Boil 1.5 L water with 10g salt. Add soaked rice. Cook until 70% tender. Drain immediately.
Add marinated chicken to the pot with remaining onions and ghee. Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat.
Layer the parboiled rice over the chicken chunks. Top with reserved fried onions, coriander, and mint.
Cover pot with a tight-fitting lid. Use a heavy weight or dough to seal steam inside.
Cook on very low heat for 25 minutes. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Turn off heat. Let the pot rest for 10 minutes before opening.
Gently fluff the rice from the sides to mix colors without breaking grains.
notes: Do not overcook the rice during the initial boil or it will turn mushy during the steaming phase.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot (like a Dutch oven) to prevent the bottom layer of chicken from burning.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Glazed Chicken Bites
recipes.visual_description: Multiple golden-brown, glossy Crispy Glazed Chicken Bites, cut into 3cm cubes, are artfully arranged on a clean, oval white porcelain sharing platter. Each piece is generously coated in a rich, reddish-brown sticky glaze, showcasing a beautiful sheen. The chicken bites are scattered with a liberal sprinkle of white toasted sesame seeds and vibrant green, thinly sliced spring onion rounds, adding contrasting color and texture. The arrangement is natural and organic, with ample negative space around the chicken. The platter rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. The scene is illuminated by soft, even natural light, emphasizing the food's texture and color without harsh shadows.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 3cm cubes

instructions: Pat chicken cubes dry with paper towels.
In a medium bowl, toss chicken cubes with cornstarch until evenly coated.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or deep skillet to 175°C.
Fry chicken in batches for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove chicken with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack set over paper towels to drain excess oil.
For the glaze, combine soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sriracha, grated ginger, minced garlic, and sesame oil in a small saucepan.
Bring glaze to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened.
Add fried chicken to the saucepan with the glaze. Toss to coat chicken evenly.
Transfer glazed chicken to a serving platter.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced spring onion. Serve immediately.
notes: For extra crispiness, you can double-fry the chicken: fry once for 4 minutes, remove, then fry again for 2-3 minutes at 185°C.
Adjust sriracha quantity to suit your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chipotle Black Bean and Brown Rice Stuffed Poblano Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted poblano pepper half is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pepper is generously stuffed with a vibrant, earthy mixture of cooked brown rice, whole black beans, and diced tomatoes. The filling shows specks of bright green cilantro and rich red chipotle. The pepper's skin is slightly blistered and charred from roasting, offering a textural contrast. A light drizzle of white Mexican crema artfully zigzags over the top of the filling. A fresh lime wedge rests beside the pepper. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer additional lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Serve with a small bowl of salsa roja or salsa verde.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained
Mexican crema or sour cream (for serving)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve poblano peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly charred.
While peppers roast, heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, minced chipotle, cumin, oregano, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in vegetable broth and diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook until sauce thickens slightly, about 3 minutes.
Stir in black beans and cooked brown rice. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Remove from heat. Stir in half of the chopped cilantro.
Carefully flip roasted poblano halves. Fill each half generously with the rice and bean mixture. Arrange filled peppers in a baking dish.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until filling is heated through and peppers are tender.
Garnish with remaining fresh cilantro and crumbled Cotija cheese, if using. Serve immediately with lime wedges and a drizzle of Mexican crema.
notes: For extra spice, add an additional chipotle pepper or a pinch of cayenne to the filling.
The brown rice can be cooked ahead of time to save preparation time.
traditional_techniques: Building layers of flavor with spices

recipes.recipe_name: Slavic Chicken and Vegetable Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of 'Slavic Chicken and Vegetable Bake' is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks are nestled amidst fluffy white rice and small elbow macaroni, infused with a savory tomato-broth sauce. Bright orange diced carrots and vibrant green broccoli florets are interspersed throughout the bake. The top layer features a golden crust of melted, bubbly cheese and set, creamy egg. The dish is garnished generously with fresh, finely chopped dill and parsley, adding a vibrant green contrast. The plate rests on a simple, natural wooden table. Beside it, a neatly folded cotton napkin and metal cutlery. In the background, a small rustic ceramic bowl holds traditional pickled cucumbers, hinting at authentic Slavic accompaniments. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's robust ingredients and comforting appeal, set against a subtly blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of sour cream on the side.
Accompany with pickled cucumbers (ogórki kiszone) or a simple cabbage salad.
Offer slices of rye bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice onion. Dice carrots and potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Cut broccoli into small florets. Mince garlic.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add uncooked rice and macaroni to the pot. Return seared chicken to the pot. Gently stir in diced carrots and potatoes. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven. Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove pot from oven. Stir in broccoli florets. Sprinkle grated cheese evenly over the top.
Whisk eggs. Pour whisked eggs over the cheese layer.

Return to oven, uncovered. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender, liquid is absorbed, cheese is melted and bubbly, and eggs are set. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Let the bake rest for 5-10 minutes. Garnish generously with fresh chopped dill and parsley before serving.
notes: This dish is a hearty and comforting one-pot meal, perfect for family dinners. Vegetables can be varied based on seasonal availability.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Rubbed Chicken with Fermented Garlic-Onion Puree and Herbed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. At the center, a perfectly seared chicken thigh, its surface a deep, rich brown from the coffee rub, sits prominently. Beside it, a neat mound of fluffy brown rice, subtly flecked with bright green chopped coriander. A vibrant, smooth green pea puree forms a crescent along one side, its color contrasting with the earthy tones. A scattering of golden, crispy breadcrumbs adds texture over the chicken and rice. A small spoonful of thinly sliced, translucent fermented red onion and garlic, with a subtle sheen, is placed near the chicken. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing ample white space on the plate. The entire dish is bathed in soft, natural light, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin and simple, modern cutlery, creating an eco-conscious, understated elegance.
instructions: 1. Prepare Fermented Garlic-Onion (3-5 days prior): Place thinly sliced red onion and garlic in a clean jar. Dissolve 1 teaspoon sea salt in 250ml filtered water to create brine. Pour brine over onion and garlic, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. 'Burp' jar daily to release gas. Refrigerate once desired tanginess is achieved.
2. Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub chicken evenly with ground coffee, salt, and black pepper.

3. Cook Chicken: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Rest for 5 minutes.
4. Cook Herbed Rice: Rinse brown rice. Cook according to package directions. Once cooked, stir in half of the chopped fresh coriander.
5. Prepare Pea Puree: Blanch green peas in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain well. Blend peas with a small splash of water until smooth. Season with salt to taste.
6. Toast Breadcrumbs: In the same pan used for chicken, add panko breadcrumbs. Toast over medium heat, stirring constantly, until golden brown and crispy.

7. Assemble Dish: Spoon a generous dollop of green pea puree onto each plate. Place a portion of herbed brown rice next to the puree. Arrange one seared chicken thigh on top of or beside the rice. Spoon a small amount of the pre-prepared fermented garlic-onion (or a thin slice) over the chicken. Sprinkle toasted crispy breadcrumbs over the entire dish. Garnish with the remaining fresh coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Cheesy Pasta with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: Baked golden-brown rigatoni pasta, coated in a rich tomato-onion sauce, emerges from a white porcelain gratin dish. Diced roasted potatoes, with their edges slightly crisped, are interspersed throughout the pasta, adding texture and warmth. A generous layer of melted, bubbly sharp cheddar cheese forms the top crust, exhibiting inviting golden-brown spots. The vibrant red of the tomato sauce contrasts with the creamy yellow of the cheese and the pale golden pasta. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green parsley leaves provides a final pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin, under soft, natural light, creating a professional yet approachable bistro aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and lightly browned. Set aside.
While potatoes roast, finely dice the onion. Mince garlic cloves.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Stir in dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing flavors to meld.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente, about 8-10 minutes. Drain well.
Grate cheddar cheese. Reserve 50 g for topping.
Add cooked pasta and roasted potatoes to the tomato sauce in the pot. Add most of the grated cheddar cheese (200 g). Stir until everything is well combined and cheese begins to melt.
Grease a large oven-safe baking dish (approximately 23x33 cm) with butter. Transfer the pasta mixture into the prepared baking dish. Spread evenly.
Sprinkle the reserved 50 g of grated cheddar cheese over the top of the pasta.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is bubbly and golden brown on top. For extra browning, broil for the last 2-3 minutes, watching carefully.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish the baked pasta with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Caramelized Onion Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy chicken and caramelized onion tagliatelle is elegantly twirled and centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pasta strands are glistening with the rich, light-beige cream sauce, interspersed with tender, golden-brown chicken chunks and deep amber caramelized onion slices. Fresh green flecks of chopped parsley are sprinkled over the top, providing a vibrant contrast. The chicken pieces are irregularly cut into 3 cm chunks, showcasing their seared edges. The dish has a natural, slightly elevated presentation, inviting and warm. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, beside a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, casting subtle shadows and highlighting its textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, set aside.
Add butter to the same pan. Add sliced onions. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in heavy cream and fresh thyme. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Gently toss to coat.
Meanwhile, cook tagliatelle according to package instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving 50 ml pasta water.
Add drained tagliatelle to the pan with the sauce. Add grated Parmesan cheese. Toss well.
If needed, add reserved pasta water to achieve desired sauce consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Herbed Risotto and Blistered Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken with herbed risotto and blistered tomatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, off-white risotto forms a natural, flowing base, not mounded or shaped, showcasing its fluid consistency. Two thick, golden-brown pieces of seared chicken breast are positioned elegantly on the risotto. The chicken has a crisp, golden crust. Scattered around the chicken and risotto are vibrant red, slightly burst cherry tomatoes, adding pops of color and texture. Freshly chopped green parsley and chives are sprinkled generously over the entire dish, providing a fresh contrast. The overall composition is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space on the plate. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table surface, reflecting a modern bistro aesthetic. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed neatly beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and colors of the food without harsh shadows. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 4 minutes per side until golden brown.

Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken, rest 5 minutes, then slice each breast into two thick pieces.
While chicken cooks, prepare risotto. In a separate large saucepan, melt 30g butter with 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast grains.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.

Add hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to be almost absorbed before adding next ladle. Continue until rice is creamy and al dente, about 20-25 minutes. Risotto should be fluid, not dry.
Stir in remaining 30g butter, grated Parmesan, half of the chopped parsley, and half of the chopped chives. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a small pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add cherry tomatoes. Cook 3-5 minutes, shaking pan occasionally, until tomatoes blister and soften.

To serve, spoon a generous portion of risotto onto each plate. Place chicken pieces on top of or beside the risotto. Scatter blistered cherry tomatoes over the dish. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Karaage
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, irregularly shaped chicken Karaage pieces are artfully arranged on a clean, simple white porcelain plate. Each piece exhibits a visibly crisp, craggy texture from the double-frying, with a deep golden hue. A few bright yellow lemon wedges are placed beside the chicken, offering a fresh color contrast. The chicken pieces are scattered naturally, allowing for moderate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests adjacent to the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the chicken's inviting texture and color.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Japanese mayonnaise (Kewpie mayo) or a light ponzu dipping sauce.
Often enjoyed as an izakaya snack with a cold beer.
instructions: Cut chicken thigh into 3-4 cm bite-sized pieces.
In a bowl, combine soy sauce, sake, mirin, grated ginger, and grated garlic.
Add chicken pieces to the marinade. Mix well to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours.
Drain chicken from marinade.
Place potato starch in a shallow dish. Dredge each chicken piece thoroughly, ensuring full coverage. Shake off excess.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or wok to 170°C.
Carefully add chicken pieces to the hot oil in batches. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Fry for 3-4 minutes until light golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove chicken from oil. Place on a wire rack to drain excess oil.
For extra crispiness, increase oil temperature to 180°C. Fry chicken again for 1-2 minutes until deeply golden and very crispy.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.
notes: Double-frying ensures maximum crispiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, golden-brown skin. They sit in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl filled with a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Thick-cut bacon lardons and browned, halved button mushrooms are distributed naturally around the chicken. Whole, softened shallots are visible in the sauce. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a linen napkin, and a side of crusty baguette slices. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the textures of the seared skin and the velvety sauce consistency. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles
Pair with a chilled glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry until crisp.
Add halved mushrooms. Sauté until browned.
Stir in shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom to release browned bits.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs.
Place chicken back into the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Whisk heavy cream and butter into the pan juices.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the sauce. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry white wine for the best sauce flavor
Do not boil the sauce vigorously after adding cream to avoid curdling
Keep the skin above the liquid level during braising to maintain crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Clarified Chicken Consommé with Confit Chicken Roulade, Potato Cubes, and Crispy Noodle Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of refined chicken consommé is presented in a wide, shallow, off-white bone china bowl. Crystal-clear, golden consommé forms the base. Two to three thick, succulent confit chicken roulade medallions are nestled centrally. A small cluster of perfectly uniform 1cm precision-cut potato cubes, subtly golden, provides textural contrast. A delicate, irregular golden-brown crispy noodle tuile is perched artfully, adding visual crunch. Small, vibrant green chive oil dots are meticulously drizzled around the consommé. A few microgreens are strategically placed for freshness. The bowl rests on a pristine white Carrara marble surface, accented by a precisely folded white linen napkin and polished silver spoon. Dramatic lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and luxurious simplicity, with ample negative space in the ultra-minimalist background.

ingredients.name: Duck fat or neutral oil (e.g., grapeseed)

instructions: Prepare Chicken Stock: Roast chicken carcass and bones at 200°C for 30 minutes until golden. Transfer to a large pot. Add 1 chopped onion, 1 chopped carrot, 1 chopped celery stalk, bay leaf, peppercorns, and 2 litres cold water. Bring to a simmer. Skim foam. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 3-4 hours. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill overnight. Skim all fat from the surface.

Clarify Consommé: In a large pot, combine cold chicken stock with 3 lightly beaten egg whites and 50g finely minced raw chicken. Whisk constantly over medium heat until raft forms on top. Stop whisking. Create a small hole in the raft. Simmer very gently for 45-60 minutes. Carefully ladle clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve without disturbing the raft. Season with salt.

Prepare Confit Chicken Roulade: Pound chicken thighs flat to even thickness. Season with salt. Roll tightly into a cylinder. Secure with kitchen twine. Place roulades in a small oven-safe dish. Cover completely with duck fat or neutral oil. Cook in oven at 140°C for 1.5-2 hours, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Cool in fat. Remove twine. Slice into thick medallions just before serving.

Prepare Precision Potato Cubes: Peel potatoes. Cut into small, precise 1 cm cubes. Rinse in cold water to remove starch. Blanch potato cubes in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until just tender. Drain well. Pat dry. Sauté lightly in a tiny amount of olive oil until slightly golden, or keep blanched.

Prepare Crispy Noodle Tuile: Cook vermicelli noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Spread a very thin layer of cooked noodles onto parchment paper. Bake at 160°C for 10-15 minutes, or until completely dry and crispy. Break into elegant, irregular pieces.

Prepare Chive Oil: Blanch chives briefly in boiling water. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain. Blend blanched chives with 30ml extra virgin olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for clear oil.

Assemble Dish: Gently warm consommé. Place 2-3 confit chicken roulade medallions and a small cluster of potato cubes in the center of each deep soup bowl. Carefully ladle hot consommé around the components. Place a crispy noodle tuile piece artfully on top or leaning against the chicken. Drizzle small dots of chive oil around the consommé. Garnish with a few microgreens. Serve immediately.
notes: Achieving a perfectly clear consommé requires patience and gentle simmering.
Ensure chicken roulade reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety and tenderness.
The crispy noodle tuile is crucial for textural contrast; ensure it is completely dry and crisp.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin, Saffron Risotto, Mushroom Agnolotti, Confit Tomato
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an expansive, pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, organic ripple texture, resting on a polished grey-veined Carrara marble surface. Dramatic, directional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision and abundant negative space. A single, perfectly seared beef tenderloin medallion, displaying a deep mahogany crust and pink interior, anchors the composition. Adjacent to it, a fluid, golden-yellow swirl of saffron risotto cascades gently, its creamy texture visible. Three delicate, perfectly formed wild mushroom agnolotti, their pale pasta encasing a rich, earthy filling, are strategically placed, creating visual interest. A cluster of three to four glossy, deep red confit cherry tomatoes provides vibrant color and soft texture. A vibrant green basil oil is artfully drizzled in a fine line, adding a pop of color and aromatic flourish. The overall presentation is minimalist, emphasizing flawless execution and the inherent beauty of each premium component. A single, precisely folded white linen napkin and a set of elegant, modern European flatware subtly frame the scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. Place cherry tomatoes in a small baking dish. Add 120ml olive oil, 2 sliced garlic cloves, 2 thyme sprigs, salt, and pepper. Bake for 45-60 minutes, until softened. Cool in the oil.

Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well and squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil with 120ml grapeseed oil and a pinch of salt until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a clear oil. Set aside.

On a clean surface, make a well with the flour. Crack eggs into the well, add a pinch of salt. Gradually incorporate flour into eggs using a fork. Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth. Wrap in cling film and rest for 30 minutes.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté 1 finely minced shallot and 2 minced garlic cloves until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add finely chopped mushrooms. Cook until moisture evaporates and mushrooms are browned. Deglaze with 50ml white wine, cook until evaporated. Stir in 30g Parmesan, parsley, salt, and pepper. Cool completely.

Divide pasta dough into 4 portions. Roll each portion very thinly through a pasta machine (setting 7 or 8). Place small mounds of mushroom filling (about 1 teaspoon) along one edge, spaced 2cm apart. Fold dough over filling. Press firmly around each mound to seal. Cut into individual agnolotti using a fluted wheel or knife. Shape into traditional agnolotti. Lightly dust with semolina or flour. Set aside.

In a medium saucepan, sauté 1 diced shallot and 1 minced garlic clove in 20g butter over medium heat until translucent. Add Carnaroli rice, toast for 1 minute. Pour in 60ml white wine, cook until absorbed. Gradually add hot stock, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for liquid to be absorbed before adding more. After 15 minutes, stir in steeped saffron. Continue adding stock until rice is al dente (18-20 minutes total). Remove from heat, stir in 40g Parmesan and 30g butter. Season with salt. Risotto should be creamy and flowing.

Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml grapeseed oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Place beef medallions in the pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, forming a deep crust. Reduce heat to medium. Add 20g butter, 2 thyme sprigs, and 2 smashed garlic cloves. Baste beef for 1-2 minutes. Remove beef from pan, rest on a wire rack for 5-7 minutes.
Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Carefully add agnolotti. Cook for 2-3 minutes, or until they float and are al dente. Gently remove with a slotted spoon.

On each plate, create a fluid, organic swirl of saffron risotto. Place one seared beef medallion next to the risotto. Arrange 3-4 warm confit cherry tomatoes artfully. Place 3-4 mushroom agnolotti precisely. Drizzle basil oil sparingly around the dish. Garnish with a few micro basil leaves or small fresh basil tips.

recipes.recipe_name: Shakshuka with Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Shakshuka is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The rich, simmering tomato and bell pepper sauce, a deep red-orange, forms the base. Three perfectly poached eggs are nestled within the sauce, their whites set and yolks glistening, just on the verge of runny. Around the edges of the bowl, golden-brown, thick-cut potato chunks are artfully arranged, showcasing their crispy exterior. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley and cilantro adds a fresh pop of color and herbaceous aroma. Small, blistered red cherry tomatoes are interspersed. The dish sits on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and a piece of warm, fluffy pita bread accompany the bowl. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and rustic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or crusty bread for dipping into the sauce and runny yolks.
Offer a side of labneh (strained yogurt) or feta cheese for a creamy, tangy contrast.
Serve directly from the cooking pan (e.g., cast iron skillet) for a rustic, communal feel.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm thick chunks. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast at 200°C (390°F) for 25-30 minutes. Turn once. Roast until golden and crispy.
While potatoes roast, dice onion and red bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large, deep skillet or cast-iron pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, smoked paprika, ground cumin, and chili flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and black pepper. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Sauce should thicken slightly.
Create 6 small wells in the simmering tomato sauce. Carefully crack one egg into each well.
Cover skillet. Cook 8-10 minutes until egg whites are set and yolks are still runny. Adjust cooking time for desired yolk firmness.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Briefly blister them in a separate hot, dry pan or add to the shakshuka during the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Finely chop fresh parsley and cilantro.

Serve shakshuka directly from the pan or portion into individual white porcelain bowls. Arrange crispy potato chunks around or alongside the shakshuka. Garnish generously with fresh herbs and blistered cherry tomatoes.
notes: Adjust chili flakes to your preferred spice level.
For firmer yolks, cook eggs for a few additional minutes covered.
Fresh herbs are crucial for authentic flavor and presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Loin Medallions with Rosemary Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared pork loin medallions is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork, cut into thick, tender chunks, exhibits a beautiful golden-brown crust from searing, with a juicy interior. Beside the pork, a generous mound of golden-brown, herb-roasted potato cubes are piled, their crispy exteriors hinting at a fluffy interior, with visible flecks of green rosemary. A glistening, light pan sauce is artfully spooned over the pork medallions. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, finely chopped parsley, adding a vibrant green contrast. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
In a large bowl, toss potato cubes with 30 ml olive oil, chopped rosemary leaves, 5 g salt, and 2 g black pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
While potatoes roast, pat pork loin dry. Cut into 2.5 cm thick medallions. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook to an internal temperature of 63°C.
Remove pork from pan. Rest on a plate, tented with foil, for 5 minutes.
In the same pan, add minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Deglaze pan with chicken stock, scraping up browned bits from the bottom.
Reduce stock by half over medium-high heat.
Whisk in cold butter until melted and sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange roasted potatoes on individual plates.
Place pork medallions next to potatoes.
Spoon pan sauce over pork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The penne pasta is coated in a luscious, creamy reddish-orange tomato sauce, forming a gently mounded pile. Nestled within and atop the pasta are several golden-brown, seared chicken medallions, cut into thick, substantial chunks, showcasing their tender interior. The dish is garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the food. A standard silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a white cotton napkin. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with standard flatware.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Let rest 5 minutes.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and American cheese slices until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions or substantial chunks.
Serve pasta onto plates. Arrange chicken medallions on top of the pasta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Authentic Kung Pao Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Kung Pao Chicken is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Diced chicken chunks, coated in a glossy, dark reddish-brown sauce, are prominently featured. The chicken pieces are irregularly scattered, showcasing their tender texture. Bright red dried chili segments are interspersed, along with thinly sliced garlic and ginger. Whole roasted peanuts add a contrasting light brown color and textural crunch. Freshly chopped bright green spring onion segments are generously sprinkled over the dish, providing a vibrant color pop and freshness. The sauce glistens under natural, even lighting. The plate has moderate negative space, allowing the dish to breathe. Beside the plate, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks are placed. A small white rice bowl filled with fluffy white jasmine rice sits to the side. The background is a blurred, warm-toned modern bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.
Traditionally accompanied by a clear soup and a simple vegetable stir-fry.
Eat with chopsticks.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm cubes. Place in a bowl. Add 15 ml Shaoxing wine and 5 g cornstarch. Mix well. Marinate for 15 minutes.

Prepare the sauce: In a small bowl, combine light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, remaining 15 ml Shaoxing wine, Chinkiang vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and chicken stock. Whisk until sugar dissolves. Set aside.
Cut dried chilies into 2 cm segments. Discard seeds if desired for less heat. Thinly slice garlic and ginger. Cut spring onions into 2 cm segments, separating white and green parts.
Heat 45 ml vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add marinated chicken cubes. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Reduce heat to medium.
Add dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant and chilies slightly darken. Do not burn.
Add sliced garlic, ginger, and white parts of spring onions. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add roasted peanuts. Increase heat to high.
Re-whisk the prepared sauce. Pour sauce into the wok. Stir quickly to coat chicken and ingredients. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats everything.
Remove from heat. Stir in green parts of spring onions. Serve immediately.
notes: For extra 'ma la' (numbing-spicy) flavor, lightly crush Sichuan peppercorns before adding to the wok.
Adjust dried chili quantity to personal spice preference.
Velveting the chicken with cornstarch and Shaoxing wine ensures tenderness.
traditional_techniques: Flavor layering (incorporating aromatics, spices, and sauce in sequence)

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora con Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, robust individual portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora con Rigatoni is presented on a round, deep, off-white ceramic plate. Golden-brown seared bone-in chicken thighs are nestled amongst al dente rigatoni pasta, all generously coated in a rich, deep red tomato sauce. The sauce features visible diced onion and subtle flecks of herbs. The chicken pieces are whole and substantial, showcasing their tender, braised texture. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a bright color contrast and fresh aroma. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even overhead lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. A subtle, out-of-focus background suggests a casual, inviting restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for dipping in the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Accompany with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until deeply golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated, about 2 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
While chicken simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente.
Remove chicken from pot. Discard rosemary, thyme stems, and bay leaf from sauce.
Shred chicken meat from bones into large chunks. Return shredded chicken to the sauce.
Drain rigatoni. Add cooked pasta directly to the sauce with chicken. Toss to coat.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Cheesy Macaroni and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Cheesy Macaroni and Roasted Vegetables is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, whole pan-seared chicken breast rests slightly off-center, displaying an even sear. Beside it, a generous scoop of creamy, golden cheesy macaroni is neatly mounded. Roasted potato wedges, their skins crisped, are arranged alongside vibrant green broccoli florets and bright orange carrot batons, showing slight charring. A small spoonful of bright red, diced tomato relish garnishes the chicken. A perfectly halved soft-boiled egg, revealing a rich, jammy yolk, sits near the vegetables. The dish is framed by moderate negative space. Colors are natural and inviting. The entire plate is visible on a simple wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Medium potatoes (e.g., Russet or Yukon Gold)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into wedges. Cut broccoli into florets. Peel carrots and cut into batons.
Toss potato wedges with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25 minutes.
Add broccoli florets and carrot batons to the baking sheet. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes more. Vegetables should be tender-crisp.
Cook macaroni according to package directions. Drain. Set aside.
Melt 50g butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in 50g flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Slowly whisk in 500ml milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly. Cook until thickened, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated cheddar and Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Add cooked macaroni. Stir to coat well.
Season chicken breasts with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and paprika.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest for 5 minutes.
For tomato relish: Dice tomatoes. Mince shallot and garlic.

Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a small pan. Sauté minced shallot and garlic for 1 minute. Add diced tomatoes. Cook for 3-5 minutes until slightly softened. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for 6-7 minutes for soft-boiled. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Peel carefully.

Plate each dish: Spoon cheesy macaroni onto a plate. Arrange roasted potato wedges, broccoli, and carrot batons beside the macaroni. Place seared chicken breast next to vegetables. Top chicken with a spoonful of tomato relish. Halve a soft-boiled egg. Place on the plate. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Dijon Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and succulent, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its perfectly seared crust. A rich, creamy Dijon sauce, glistening with a pale yellow hue, is elegantly spooned around the base of the chicken, creating a delicate pool. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives or parsley provides a vibrant green contrast and a fresh aroma. The dish is garnished simply, allowing the quality of the ingredients to shine. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a soft, blurred background maintaining focus on the food.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add minced shallot. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 2 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in chicken stock and Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 2-3 minutes. Do not boil vigorously.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Heat through 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato Salad with Seared Chicken and Dijon Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant composition. A bed of fresh, crisp mixed salad greens forms the base. Artfully arranged on top are warm, slightly burst roasted cherry tomatoes and tender, caramelized red onion wedges. Seared chicken, cut into substantial, golden-brown chunks, is placed among the vegetables, exhibiting a juicy interior. The entire salad is lightly coated with a glossy Dijon vinaigrette, creating a subtle sheen. Finely chopped fresh parsley or basil is scattered as a garnish, adding a pop of green. The colors are natural and inviting, with reds, greens, and golden-browns in harmonious balance. The plate maintains moderate negative space, highlighting each component. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard flatware, and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Cut red onion into 8 wedges.
Toss tomatoes and onion wedges with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tomatoes are slightly burst and onions are tender and caramelized.
While vegetables roast, prepare chicken. Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes. Cut each breast into 2-3 rustic chunks.

Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar, honey, minced garlic (if using), salt, and pepper. Slowly whisk in remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine mixed salad greens, roasted tomatoes, and roasted red onion wedges. Drizzle with most of the dressing. Toss gently to combine.
Divide salad among four plates. Arrange seared chicken chunks artfully on top of each salad. Drizzle with any remaining dressing. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or basil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken Rillette Crostini with Fermented Garlic Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A clean, minimalistic presentation on a light, handcrafted ceramic plate with an organic, slightly irregular rim. The centerpiece is several irregularly shaped, golden-brown sourdough crisps, each generously topped with a dollop of creamy, shredded chicken rillette. The rillette shows rich, natural chicken color and a slightly coarse texture. Bright red halves of fermented cherry tomatoes are carefully placed atop the rillette, their vibrant color contrasting with the chicken. Scattered around the crostini are golden, shard-like pasta crisps, exhibiting a delicate crispness. A few tiny sprigs of fresh thyme or basil provide a subtle green accent. The background is a natural, light-colored reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin subtly draped. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the pure textures and colors of the sustainable ingredients.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, render fat from chicken skin over medium-low heat. Remove skin once crisp.
Add chicken thighs, 4 whole garlic cloves, thyme, and rosemary to the pot. Add olive oil until chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 2-3 hours, until chicken is falling off the bone. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove chicken, herbs, and garlic. Strain fat; reserve.
Shred chicken meat with two forks. Mash confit garlic and mix into shredded chicken. Add enough reserved chicken fat to moisten until spreadable. Season to taste.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Peel and thinly slice 4 garlic cloves.
In a clean jar, combine tomatoes, sliced garlic, white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Stir well.
Seal jar loosely to allow gas release. Leave at room temperature for 24-48 hours until slightly bubbly and tangy. Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Tear or cut day-old sourdough into irregular, rustic pieces (about 5-7 cm).
Arrange on a baking sheet. Drizzle lightly with olive oil. Bake for 10-15 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool.
Break lasagna sheets into irregular, bite-sized shards. Arrange on a separate baking sheet. Drizzle lightly with olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Bake at 160°C for 8-12 minutes until golden brown and very crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Cool.
Spread chicken rillette generously onto each sourdough crisp. Top with a few fermented garlic tomato halves.
Arrange on a large sharing platter with the pasta crisps alongside. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh thyme or basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. The wide, flat pappardelle noodles are thoroughly coated in a rich, dark red-brown ragu, forming an appealing mound. Tender, large chunks of braised beef are visibly nestled within the sauce and pasta, showcasing their fork-shredded texture. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped Italian parsley adds a vibrant color contrast, along with a generous dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese, providing a touch of white and a slightly coarser texture.
