1. If using carrot tops, wash them well.
2. Combine fresh basil leaves (and carrot tops if using) with 30ml olive oil and zest of 1 lemon in a small blender or food processor.
3. Blend until smooth. Season with a pinch of salt.
Part 5: Assembly
1. Arrange roasted potatoes and carrots on individual plates.
2. Place a seared tuna fillet alongside the vegetables.
3. Spoon a generous amount of fermented carrot and onion relish over or next to the tuna.
4. Drizzle with basil-lemon oil.
5. Garnish with fresh basil leaves or finely chopped carrot tops.
6. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.
notes: The fermented relish requires advance preparation.
Adjust fermentation time based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.
Use sustainably caught tuna.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Potato & Chicken Hash with Savory Tomato Relish
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-beige ceramic plate with a natural, slightly textured finish. A generous mound of golden-brown fermented potato hash forms the base, its irregular cubes showing varying shades of crispness. Nestled beside the hash is a whole, deeply seared chicken thigh, its skin a rich, burnished mahogany, exhibiting a crisp, inviting texture. A vibrant, rustic dollop of savory tomato relish, with visible diced tomatoes and onions, provides a striking contrast of color and texture. Scattered artfully around the plate are irregular pieces of dark, pitted black olives, adding depth. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space around the food, emphasizing the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. No ornate garnishes; only a light scattering of fresh, finely chopped green chives offers a subtle, natural accent. The chicken is presented whole, showcasing its natural form.

ingredients.name: mixed spice (smoked paprika, dried oregano, black pepper)
fresh parsley or chives, chopped (for garnish)

instructions: To ferment potatoes: Dissolve 20g salt in 1 litre filtered water to make brine. Place 800g potato cubes (2cm) in a clean glass jar. Pour brine over potatoes, ensuring full submersion. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 3-5 days, until pleasantly tangy. Store in refrigerator once fermented.

To ferment tomato relish: Combine 400g diced tomatoes, 100g finely diced onion, 2 minced garlic cloves, 5g mixed spice, 5g salt, 30ml ketchup, and 15ml olive oil in a clean glass jar. Mix well. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 2-3 days, until desired tanginess. Store in refrigerator.

Prepare chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. In a bowl, combine 2 minced garlic cloves, 30ml soy sauce, 5g mixed spice, 15ml olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Add chicken thighs, coating evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours refrigerated.

Cook chicken: Preheat oven to 190°C. Heat an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

Cook potato hash: While chicken roasts, drain fermented potatoes. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add remaining 15ml olive oil. Add remaining 100g diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add drained fermented potato cubes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until potatoes are tender and browned. Season with salt and pepper.
Optional fried eggs: If desired, fry two eggs sunny-side up or to your preference.

Assemble and serve: Divide potato hash among four plates. Place one chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon generous amounts of savory tomato relish alongside. Scatter chopped black olives. Drizzle with 30ml mayonnaise if desired. Garnish with fresh parsley or chives.
notes: This recipe champions a zero-waste approach. Leftover chicken bones can be used to make a quick stock. Potato peels can be crisped in the oven or added to stock. Onion and garlic peels can be composted or used for vegetable broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Roasted Chicken with Fermented Garlic Aioli and Quick-Pickled Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Roasted Chicken is presented on a cream-colored, handcrafted ceramic plate with a wide rim, placed on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The chicken thigh, roasted to a golden-brown hue, sits as a whole, succulent piece, its surface showing a slight crispness. Beside the chicken, a generous dollop of creamy, off-white Fermented Garlic Aioli is artfully placed, its smooth texture contrasting with the rougher chicken. A vibrant, fresh mound of quick-pickled vegetables, including thinly sliced pink radishes, thin orange carrot batons, and finely shredded purple red cabbage, provides a striking burst of color and crisp texture. The arrangement is natural and unforced, allowing ample negative space on the plate. A few sprigs of fresh green parsley or dill are scattered over the aioli and vegetables as a simple, natural garnish. The setting is minimalist, with an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone subtly folded beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting from the side highlights the textures and colors of the food. The background is clean and unobtrusive, hinting at a sustainable, organic environment with subtle natural elements.

ingredients.name: Egg (for aioli if homemade, otherwise omit)
Fresh parsley or dill, chopped (for garnish)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Roast 4 garlic cloves with 15 ml olive oil until soft and golden, about 15-20 minutes. Set aside.
For quick-pickled vegetables: Thinly slice radishes and carrots into thin batons. Finely shred red cabbage. Place all vegetables in a clean jar or heatproof bowl.

Combine white vinegar, water, 15g salt, and 15g sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, stirring until salt and sugar dissolve. Pour hot brine over vegetables. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. (Can be made ahead and stored for up to 2 weeks).

Prepare chicken marinade: In a bowl, combine 30 ml soy sauce, 10g mixed spice blend, and 15 ml olive oil. Add chicken thighs. Ensure chicken is fully coated. Marinate for at least 15 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Roast marinated chicken thighs on a baking sheet for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and chicken is cooked through and lightly browned.

While chicken roasts, prepare Fermented Garlic Aioli: In a small bowl, mash roasted garlic cloves with a fork. Stir in 150g mayonnaise, 15 ml ketchup, and 15 ml soy sauce. Mix until smooth. (For homemade aioli, whisk 1 egg yolk with mashed roasted garlic, then slowly drizzle in 150 ml olive oil until emulsified, then add ketchup and soy sauce).
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Drain pickled vegetables.

Plate individual chicken thighs. Spoon a generous dollop of Fermented Garlic Aioli alongside. Arrange a mound of quick-pickled vegetables next to the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or dill. Serve immediately.
notes: To make lacto-fermented garlic for a deeper flavor profile: Peel garlic cloves. Place in a clean jar. Cover with a 2% brine (20g non-iodized salt per 1 litre filtered water). Seal with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 7-14 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate. Use this fermented garlic, mashed, in the aioli for an authentic fermented element.
Zero-waste tip: Save chicken bones for homemade stock. Use vegetable trimmings (carrot tops, radish greens) in a green smoothie or vegetable stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Spicy Sausage and Broccolini
recipes.visual_description: Orecchiette with Spicy Sausage and Broccolini is plated on a clean, round white porcelain dish. The pasta forms a natural mound, coated in a light, emulsified sauce. Golden-brown chunks of spicy Italian sausage are interspersed, alongside vibrant green broccolini florets and stalks. Visible sliced garlic and red pepper flakes add detail. The dish features warm cream, rich brown, and bright green hues. Textures include chewy pasta, crisp sausage, and tender-crisp broccolini, all with a light sheen. Freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano and scattered fresh parsley leaves garnish the top. The plate sits on a simple wooden surface, with a white cotton napkin and European flatware. Natural, even lighting creates soft shadows. The background is clean, suggesting a casual bistro. This is a single, refined restaurant portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add sausage, breaking it apart. Cook until browned and cooked through, 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes to the pan with the sausage. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer until wine is mostly evaporated, 2-3 minutes.
Add broccolini to the pan. Add stock. Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes, until broccolini is tender-crisp.
Meanwhile, cook orecchiette according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add pasta to the pan with the sausage and broccolini.
Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano and Pecorino Romano. Add half of the reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously to combine, creating a creamy sauce. Add more pasta water as needed.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust spiciness by increasing or decreasing red pepper flakes.
Ensure pasta is al dente for best texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Olives and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Olives and Tomatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two whole, seared chicken thighs, skin-on and bone-in, are arranged centrally. Scattered around the chicken are vibrant red, roasted cherry tomatoes, some gently burst, and whole, glossy black Kalamata olives. Thinly sliced garlic cloves are visible amongst the ingredients. A light, savory pan sauce pools subtly at the base. Fresh sprigs of green rosemary and thyme leaves are placed over and beside the chicken, adding a fragrant, natural garnish. The overall presentation is balanced, showcasing rich golden-brown chicken, bright reds, deep blacks, and fresh greens. The plate rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface, typical of a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting textures and colors, creating an approachable, professional appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread to soak up the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken thighs completely dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side down, in the hot pan. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken.
Add whole cherry tomatoes, whole Kalamata olives, and thinly sliced garlic cloves to the pan around the chicken. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Braise for 25-30 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Remove pan from oven. Grate lemon zest over the dish. Squeeze fresh lemon juice into the pan.
Serve hot, directly from the pan or plated individually.
notes: Ensure chicken skin is very dry before searing for maximum crispiness.
Adjust seasoning to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Apricot-Thyme Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared duck breast is presented on a clean white round porcelain plate. The duck, with its deeply golden-brown, crispy skin and rosy medium-rare interior, is sliced into thick, substantial chunks and arranged neatly but not rigidly on one side of the plate. A glossy, amber-hued apricot-thyme glaze is generously spooned over the duck and pools gently around its base. Alongside the duck, vibrant green roasted asparagus spears are arranged, and a small cluster of golden-brown roasted potato wedges completes the composition. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the duck and sauce for garnish. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a neatly folded light-colored cotton napkin. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures against a clean, unobtrusive background, creating an approachable yet refined bistro aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Small potatoes (e.g., fingerling or baby potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Toss asparagus and potato wedges with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in oven for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.
Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into meat. Season skin and flesh with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe skillet. Render fat over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Pour off excess fat periodically.
Flip duck breasts. Sear flesh side for 2 minutes.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 6-8 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 57-60°C). Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove duck from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 10 minutes.
While duck rests, make the sauce. Pour off most duck fat from skillet, leaving 15 ml. Add shallots to skillet. Sauté over medium heat until softened, about 3 minutes. Add garlic. Sauté 1 minute.
Deglaze skillet with apricot liqueur. Scrape up browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Pour in chicken stock. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer until sauce thickens slightly, about 5-7 minutes. Remove thyme sprigs.
Whisk in cold butter cubes until sauce is glossy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice rested duck breasts crosswise into thick chunks. Do not fan.
Plate duck. Spoon sauce over. Serve with roasted asparagus and potato wedges. Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Baked Chicken Macaroni with Broccoli and Corn
recipes.visual_description: A generous, home-style portion of Cheesy Baked Chicken Macaroni with Broccoli and Corn is served on a simple, round off-white ceramic plate, showcasing its golden-brown, bubbly top crust. The dish reveals tender, diced chicken chunks (approximately 2 cm), vibrant green broccoli florets, and bright yellow corn kernels, all enveloped in a creamy, rich cheese sauce. The macaroni is soft and coated. The textures are comforting and inviting. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A single, sturdy silver fork rests beside the plate. The background is minimal, suggesting a relaxed family dining area with a lived-in atmosphere, emphasizing the dish as the centerpiece of a comforting meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 7-8 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove chicken from skillet.
In the same skillet or a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded cheddar cheese, hot sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth.
Steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp, about 3-4 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooked macaroni, cooked chicken, steamed broccoli, corn kernels, and cheese sauce. Mix well to coat all ingredients.
Pour mixture into a 2.5-3 liter baking dish.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and top is golden. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Adjust hot sauce to preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Turkey Medallions with Broccoli Puree, Parmesan Tuile, and Calabrian Chili Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single seared turkey medallion, golden-crusted and tender, centers a pristine white bone china plate. A vibrant, emerald-green broccoli puree sweeps curvilinearly across one side. A delicate, golden Parmesan tuile stands upright, leaning subtly against the turkey. A deep ruby-red Calabrian chili and shallot gastrique forms a glossy pool beside it. A single, perfectly round, herb-infused pasta disc rests nearby. Abundant negative space highlights the minimalist elegance. Tiny, vibrant green micro basil leaves provide a final touch. The dish rests on luxurious white Carrara marble, illuminated by dramatic, focused lighting, with a precisely folded white linen napkin and elegant modern flatware completing the sophisticated setting.
instructions: Trim turkey breast. Cut into 4 equal medallions (approx 150g each).
Season medallions with sea salt and black pepper.
Vacuum seal turkey medallions. Cook sous vide at 63°C for 1.5 hours.
Remove turkey from bag. Pat very dry. Sear medallions in hot olive oil in a non-stick pan. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crusty. Rest 5 minutes.
Bring salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp (approx 3-4 minutes).
Immediately transfer blanched broccoli to ice bath. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water.
Blend broccoli with 30g butter, heavy cream, pinch of salt. Blend until perfectly smooth. Pass through fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grate Parmesan cheese finely.
Arrange small, thin circles (approx 5cm diameter) of grated cheese on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Remove from oven. Let cool completely on parchment paper.
Finely mince shallots. In a small saucepan, combine red wine vinegar, sugar, and minced shallots.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce until syrupy. Add vegetable stock and Calabrian chili paste. Simmer gently.
Reduce until gastrique coats the back of a spoon. Stir in 20g cold butter. Whisk until emulsified and glossy. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Roll fresh pasta sheets very thin (approx 1mm). Cut out 4 perfect circles (approx 4-5cm diameter) using a round cutter.
Bring salted water to a gentle boil. Cook pasta discs for 1-2 minutes until al dente.
Drain immediately. Toss lightly with a tiny bit of olive oil and finely chopped thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Sausage Risotto with Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy, golden-white risotto fills a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl. Visible within and atop the risotto are tender, browned chicken chunks (2-3 cm) and slightly crisp, seared Italian sausage slices (1 cm thick rounds). Bright green, roasted broccoli florets are thoughtfully arranged around the edges and nestled into the risotto, adding a vibrant color contrast. The risotto maintains a fluid, flowing consistency, not dry or molded. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese covers the top, along with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley for a touch of green. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space around the dish. It is set on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and spoon, and a folded white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto is best enjoyed fresh off the stove.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly browned.
Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm chunks. Remove sausage from casings; break into small pieces.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add sausage pieces to the same pot. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 30 g butter to the pot. Add diced onion. Cook, stirring, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes, toasting the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.

Add one ladle (about 250 ml) of hot chicken broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is almost fully absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 20-25 minutes.
Halfway through broth addition, return cooked chicken and sausage to the pot.

When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente (firm to the bite but not hard), remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30 g butter and 60 g grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes; this is 'mantecatura' for creaminess. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Gently fold in most of the roasted broccoli. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish each serving with remaining roasted broccoli, a sprinkle of fresh Parmesan, and chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Ballotine, Wild Rice Pilaf, Onion Soubise
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of elegant French cuisine is presented on a pristine white bone china plate. A velvety, pale ivory Onion Soubise forms a graceful, fluid sweep across the plate's base. Beside it, a compact, textural mound of dark, nutty Wild Rice Pilaf, its grains distinct and plump, rises subtly. Two thick, golden-skinned medallions of Chicken Ballotine, revealing a delicate, creamy mushroom-herb farce within, are artfully placed atop the pilaf, showcasing their perfectly seared exterior and moist interior. A scattering of vibrant green microgreens provides a precise, fresh accent. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space. The dish sits on a premium grey veined marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows. A crisp white linen napkin, folded precisely, and elegant silver flatware are positioned nearby, enhancing the luxurious, refined ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served as a main course in a multi-course French meal.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Ballotine:
Trim chicken thighs. Lay skin-side down. Pound lightly to even thickness. Season with salt, pepper.
Finely dice mushrooms, shallots, garlic.
Melt 30g butter in pan. Sauté shallots until translucent. Add garlic, mushrooms. Cook until moisture evaporates.
Deglaze with white wine. Reduce completely. Add 100ml chicken stock, 50ml cream. Simmer until thickened. Season. Cool completely.
Spread mushroom mixture onto each chicken thigh. Roll tightly into a cylindrical shape. Tie with butcher's twine.
Sear ballotines in olive oil until golden brown on all sides.
Transfer to oven. Roast at 180°C for 20-25 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
Cook Wild Rice Pilaf:
Rinse wild rice.
In saucepan, melt 20g butter. Sauté finely diced shallot until translucent.
Add wild rice, 600ml chicken stock, bay leaf, thyme sprig. Bring to boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 40-50 minutes until rice is tender and liquid absorbed.
Remove bay leaf, thyme. Fluff with fork. Season.
Make Onion Soubise:
Peel, thinly slice onions.
Melt 40g butter in heavy-bottomed pot. Add sliced onions. Cook over very low heat, covered, 30-40 minutes until very soft and translucent, not browned. Stir occasionally.
Add heavy cream, milk. Simmer 5 minutes.
Transfer mixture to blender. Blend until perfectly smooth. Pass through fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Season with salt, white pepper. Keep warm.
Plating:
Slice each rested chicken ballotine into 2-3 thick medallions.
Spoon a generous dollop of onion soubise onto the plate, spreading it subtly.
Arrange a mound of wild rice pilaf next to the soubise.
Place 2-3 chicken ballotine medallions elegantly on top or beside the pilaf.
Garnish with a few microgreens or finely snipped chives.
notes: Ensure the chicken is fully cooked to 75°C.
The soubise must be extremely smooth; sieving is crucial.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Cheesy Rice with Pan-Seared Chicken and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, showcasing a single individual portion. A generous mound of creamy, off-white cheesy rice forms the base, its soft texture visible. Resting atop the rice are two thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast chunks, their seared crust contrasting with the tender interior. Alongside the chicken, vibrant green roasted broccoli florets, slightly charred at the edges, are artfully arranged, adding a pop of color and texture. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley garnishes the dish, providing a fresh aromatic accent. The arrangement is balanced and professional, with ample negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery, under soft, natural lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (392°F).
Cut broccoli into bite-sized florets. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread broccoli on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Set aside.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 1 minute to toast the grains.
Heat chicken broth in a separate saucepan until simmering.
Add one ladle of hot broth to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is creamy and al dente. This takes about 20-25 minutes.
While rice cooks, prepare chicken. Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 15ml olive oil.
Sear chicken breasts for 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes. Cut each breast into 2-3 thick chunks.
Stir grated Parmesan cheese and remaining 15g butter into the creamy rice. Stir until melted and well combined.
Taste and adjust seasoning for salt and pepper.
To plate, spoon a generous portion of creamy cheesy rice onto each plate.
Arrange pan-seared chicken chunks and roasted broccoli florets on top of the rice.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For creamier rice, add a splash more broth or a knob of butter at the end.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Apple Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic apple crumble served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with subtle rim imperfections. The topping is a rugged, golden-brown crust featuring coarse flour crumbs and toasted rolled oats. Soft, 2cm chunks of stewed Granny Smith apples are visible beneath the topping, with thick, caramelized amber juices bubbling slightly at the dish's edges. A single, generous pour of thick, pale yellow vanilla custard pools naturally on one side, partially melting into the warm crumble. The bowl sits on a dark, weathered oak table beside a folded linen napkin and a tarnished silver spoon. Soft, warm kitchen light emphasizes the crunchy textures and steam rising from the fruit.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with hot vanilla custard
Accompany with a dollop of clotted cream
Pair with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 2cm chunks.
Toss apples with 50g sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Transfer apple mixture to a 20cm baking dish.
Cut cold butter into small cubes.
Rub butter into flour using fingertips until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Stir in remaining 100g sugar and rolled oats.
Spread crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden brown and fruit is bubbling.
Remove from oven and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use cold butter to ensure a crisp, crumbly texture.
Do not overwork the dough or it will become tough.
Granny Smith apples provide the best tart balance to the sweet topping.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken with Crispy Potato & Fermented Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Slow-Cooked Chicken with Crispy Potato & Fermented Garlic Rice is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream or beige tone. The plating is minimalistic, allowing ample white space to highlight each ingredient. Fluffy, slightly green rice forms the base, topped with rustic, tender chunks of slow-cooked chicken. Alongside, golden-brown, 2cm roasted potato cubes are artfully arranged. A drizzle of rich braising liquid adds moisture and depth. The dish is finished with delicate shavings of aged hard cheese and a scattering of golden, crisp chicken skin for texture. The composition is natural and unforced, emphasizing the inherent beauty of the ingredients. The scene is set on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, with a clean, minimalist background featuring subtle greenery to enhance the eco-conscious aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Aged hard cheese (e.g., Parmesan, aged cheddar)

instructions: Remove skin from chicken thighs. Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Place chicken skin, fat-side down, in a cold pan. Cook over medium-low heat until crispy and golden brown (10-15 minutes). Drain on paper towel. Crumble when cool.
In the same pan with rendered chicken fat (or a little olive oil), sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken.
Add onion to the pan. Sauté until translucent. Add fermented garlic. Cook for 1 minute.

Return chicken to pan. Add stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over low heat for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and is tender. Remove chicken. Shred or cut into rustic chunks. Reduce braising liquid slightly if desired.
Rinse rice. Cook according to package instructions for firm, separate grains.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into 2cm cubes. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden.
Combine cooked rice with chopped parsley and a spoonful of the braising liquid for flavor.

Spoon rice onto plates. Arrange roasted potato cubes alongside. Place rustic chunks of slow-cooked chicken on top. Drizzle with remaining braising liquid. Grate or shave aged cheese over the dish. Sprinkle with crispy chicken skin.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Hake with Savory Almond-Cocoa Crust, Creamy Mustard Tatsoi, and Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, everyday ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A single pan-seared hake fillet, coated in a golden-brown, subtly textured almond-cocoa crust, is the centerpiece. The hake is a thick, whole chunk, not sliced, resting naturally on a bed of vibrant green, creamy mustard tatsoi. Its crust shows hints of the dark chocolate's deep hue against the toasted almonds. The roughly chopped tatsoi is softly wilted, its leaves retaining their natural shape and rich green color, lightly coated in a creamy, pale yellow sauce. Beside the hake, a perfectly poached egg sits, its delicate white encasing a promise of a golden, runny yolk. A light scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley or chives adds a final touch of color and freshness. The plating is modest and approachable, filling the plate adequately without overcrowding, resembling a comforting meal served in a family kitchen. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting textures and colors. A simple cloth napkin and standard flatware are casually placed nearby, completing the homely atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Dijon mustard
ingredients.quantity: 2 tablespoons (for tatsoi sauce) + 1 teaspoon (for crust binder)

instructions: Prepare the crust mixture: In a shallow dish, combine almond meal, breadcrumbs, finely grated dark chocolate, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.

Prepare the hake: Pat hake fillets dry with paper towels. In another shallow dish, whisk 1 egg with 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard. Dip each hake fillet into the egg mixture. Dredge thoroughly in the almond-chocolate crust mixture. Press to coat evenly.

Cook the hake: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil and 10g butter in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place the crusted hake fillets in the pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side. Cook until golden brown and flaky.

Prepare the creamy tatsoi: In a separate pan, melt 20g butter with 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add finely minced shallot and cook until softened, about 2 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard. Pour in chicken or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Add roughly chopped tatsoi. Cook, stirring, until wilted, about 3-4 minutes. Stir in cream. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.

Poach the eggs: Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of vinegar (optional). Carefully crack each egg into a small bowl. Gently slide into the simmering water. Poach for 3-4 minutes for soft yolks. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.

Plate the dish: Place a generous portion of creamy mustard tatsoi on each plate. Top with a pan-seared hake fillet. Gently place a poached egg alongside or on top of the hake. Drizzle with fresh lemon juice. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Coconut Egg Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Coconut Egg Curry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, resting on a simple wooden table. A neat mound of fluffy white jasmine rice forms the base. Over the rice, a vibrant, creamy yellow-orange coconut curry sauce is generously ladled. Two perfectly halved boiled eggs, with firm, bright yellow yolks and smooth white exteriors, are nestled into the curry, showcasing their distinct shapes. The smooth curry sauce has a glossy sheen. Fresh, vibrant green chopped coriander leaves are scattered over the eggs and curry for color contrast. A few thin, bright red slices of fresh chili are artfully placed. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. A set of chopsticks and a small white ceramic bowl are beside the plate, enhancing the Southeast Asian aesthetic. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional steamed jasmine rice on the side.
Offer a small dish of fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies for extra spice.
Provide a side of fresh cucumber slices to refresh the palate.
instructions: Place eggs in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 8 minutes. Drain. Cool in ice water. Peel. Set aside.
Melt margarine in a large pan or pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in red curry paste. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, to toast paste.
Pour in coconut milk and coconut liqueur. Stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fish sauce and palm sugar. Stir to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Gently add peeled boiled eggs to the simmering curry. Cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing eggs to absorb flavors.
Remove from heat. Stir in lime juice.
Ladle curry with eggs over cooked jasmine rice. Garnish with fresh coriander and sliced red chili.
notes: For a thicker curry, simmer longer. For a thinner curry, add a splash of water or coconut milk.
Adjust red curry paste quantity based on desired spice level.
traditional_techniques: Toasting curry paste to deepen flavor
Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Sous-Vide Chicken Breast, Black Garlic Jus, Blanched Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared sous-vide chicken breast, golden-brown and glistening, rests off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. The breast is presented whole, showcasing its elegant form and crispy skin. A delicate, glossy black garlic jus is artfully drizzled in a natural, flowing curve beside the chicken, its deep, rich hue providing a sophisticated contrast. Three to four vibrant green blanched asparagus spears, cut into uniform batons, are meticulously arranged parallel to the chicken, adding a touch of fresh color and architectural precision. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the minimalist aesthetic. The plating is clean and intentional, highlighting the quality of ingredients and precision of execution. The scene is set on a superpremium white Carrara marble surface with subtle grey veining, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that casts soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits beside the plate. A single, elegant silver fork and knife are positioned to the side.
instructions: Season chicken breasts generously with sea salt and black pepper. Place each breast in a vacuum-sealable bag with one thyme sprig and a drizzle of olive oil. Vacuum seal bags.
Preheat a water bath to 63°C (145.4°F). Cook chicken breasts for 1.5 hours.
While chicken cooks, prepare black garlic jus. Finely mince the shallot.
In a small saucepan, melt 10g butter with 5ml olive oil over medium heat. Sauté minced shallot until translucent, about 2 minutes.
Add white wine. Reduce by half.
Add chicken stock and black garlic cloves. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and gently simmer for 15 minutes, allowing black garlic to soften and dissolve into the stock.
Strain the jus through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Return strained jus to a clean saucepan.

Reduce the jus over medium heat until it coats the back of a spoon, about 5-7 minutes. Whisk in 20g cold unsalted butter, off heat, to emulsify and create a glossy finish. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Prepare an ice bath.
Blanch asparagus spears in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until vibrant green and crisp-tender. Immediately transfer to ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Once chicken is cooked, remove from water bath. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Heat remaining 20g butter and 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Sear chicken breasts, presentation side down, for 3-4 minutes until deeply golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 1-2 minutes to finish cooking. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Rest chicken breasts on a wire rack for 5 minutes before plating.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared King Oyster Mushroom, Dark Beer Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine white bone china plate holds two thick, pan-seared King Oyster mushroom medallions, artfully overlapped. Their golden-brown, caramelized crust contrasts with the tender interior. A glossy, dark amber dark beer glaze is elegantly drizzled over and around the mushrooms, creating organic lines. Adjacent, a small, shimmering pool of clear, pale green thyme-infused garlic oil adds a delicate sheen. A few vibrant red chili threads are precisely placed on one mushroom, with a small fresh thyme sprig nearby. The minimalist plating emphasizes natural beauty and perfect execution, leaving abundant negative space. Presented on a cool grey marble surface, bathed in dramatic professional lighting with subtle shadows. A crisp, white linen napkin, folded precisely, completes the ultra-minimalist, luxurious setting.
instructions: Prepare mushrooms. Wipe clean. Trim ends. Cut each mushroom into 2 cm thick medallions. Score one side of each medallion lightly in a crosshatch pattern.

Make thyme-garlic oil. Heat 30 ml olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add sliced garlic and 4 thyme sprigs. Gently infuse for 10 minutes. Do not brown garlic. Strain oil; discard solids. Set aside.

Prepare dark beer glaze. In a small saucepan, combine dark beer and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Whisk in Dijon mustard. Simmer gently until liquid reduces to a glossy, syrupy glaze, about 10-15 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Sear mushrooms. Heat a cast iron pan over medium-high heat. Add a thin layer of olive oil. Sear mushroom medallions, scored side down first, until golden brown and caramelized, about 3-4 minutes per side. Season with salt and pepper during searing.
Prepare chili threads. Slice red chili very thinly into fine threads.

Plate. Arrange 1-2 seared mushroom medallions per plate, slightly overlapping or in a natural cluster. Drizzle generously with dark beer glaze. Spoon a few drops of thyme-garlic oil around the mushrooms. Garnish with a few chili threads and a small fresh thyme sprig. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chicken with Parsnip Puree and Crispy Skin
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken thigh, its skin a rich golden-brown, rests atop a generous swirl of creamy, pale beige parsnip puree. The chicken is presented whole, showcasing its natural form. Alongside, vibrant green vegetables, like blanched asparagus spears or broccolini florets, are neatly arranged, adding a pop of fresh color. A scattering of finely chopped, golden-brown crispy chicken skin provides textural contrast and a zero-waste element. The dish is centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone, leaving ample white space. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle textures of light wood or stone. The presentation is simple, organic, and focused on the inherent beauty of the ingredients.
instructions: Prepare the lacto-fermented brine: Combine water, sea salt, bay leaves, peppercorns, and smashed garlic in a large jar. Stir until salt dissolves.
Submerge chicken thighs in the brine. Ensure chicken is fully covered. Place a weight if needed. Seal the jar.
Ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours. Transfer to refrigerator for an additional 1-2 days. The total brining time is 3-4 days.
Remove chicken from brine. Pat very dry with paper towels. Carefully remove chicken skin; set aside.
Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Place chicken skin in a cold pan. Render over medium-low heat until crisp and golden. This takes 10-15 minutes. Remove skin; chop into small pieces. Season lightly with salt. Set aside.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes.
While chicken roasts, prepare parsnip puree. Peel parsnips; dice into 2 cm pieces. Boil until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well.
Transfer parsnips to a blender. Add vegetable stock and butter. Blend until very smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Blanch or steam green vegetables until tender-crisp. Season lightly.
Spoon parsnip puree onto plates. Place a rested chicken thigh on top. Arrange green vegetables beside the chicken.
Garnish with chopped crispy chicken skin and fresh parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: The parsnip peels can be added to your vegetable scrap bin for future stock.
Ensure chicken is completely submerged in brine to prevent spoilage.
Adjust brining time based on desired fermentation flavor. Longer brining yields more tang.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Ballotine with Artichoke Velouté and Smoked Bacon Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken ballotine medallion, showcasing its golden-brown, crispy skin and the tender, succulent interior with a hint of the sausage farce, is positioned off-center on a pristine, large white bone china plate. Beneath and slightly to the side of the chicken, a luminous, pale green Artichoke Velouté forms an organic, flowing pool, its velvety texture evident. A delicate scattering of dark, crispy smoked bacon crumble, interspersed with finely chopped green chives, is precisely placed around the chicken and on the velouté, offering a textural contrast and visual depth. A single, irregularly shaped shard of toasted sourdough crisp stands artfully beside the chicken, adding a subtle architectural element. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the sophisticated simplicity and flawless execution of each component. The plate rests on a premium grey veined marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin and minimalist silver flatware, under dramatic, focused lighting that creates subtle shadows. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined restaurant portion.

ingredients.name: artichoke hearts (canned or jarred in water, drained)

instructions: Prepare the Chicken Ballotine: Carefully butterfly each chicken breast. Pound to an even 1 cm thickness. In a bowl, combine sausage meat, one minced shallot, one minced garlic clove, chopped parsley, and chopped thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well. Divide sausage mixture into 4 equal portions. Place one portion onto each butterflied chicken breast. Roll each chicken breast tightly into a cylinder. Secure with butcher's twine. Season the exterior with salt and pepper.

Cook the Chicken Ballotine: Heat 20ml olive oil in an oven-safe, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken ballotines, turning occasionally, until golden-brown and crispy on all sides (8-10 minutes total). Add 30g butter to the pan. Baste chicken with melted butter. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Rest chicken for 5-10 minutes.

Make the Artichoke Velouté: Melt 10g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Sauté remaining minced shallot until translucent (2-3 minutes). Add drained artichoke hearts and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Blend mixture with an immersion blender until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Return velouté to the saucepan. Stir in heavy cream. Gently heat through. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare the Smoked Bacon Crumble: In a dry pan, render finely diced bacon over medium heat until very crispy and golden-brown. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Once cool, finely chop or crush crispy bacon into a crumble. Stir in chopped chives.

Make the Sourdough Crisp: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Brush both sides of the sourdough slice with 5ml olive oil. Bake on a baking sheet until golden-brown and very crisp (8-12 minutes). Break into small, irregular shards.

Assemble and Serve: Remove twine from rested chicken ballotines. Slice each ballotine into 2-3 thick, elegant medallions (approximately 3-4 cm thick). Spoon a generous pool or elegant swoosh of Artichoke Velouté onto the center of each plate, leaving abundant white space. Carefully place one or two chicken ballotine medallions onto the velouté. Sprinkle Smoked Bacon Crumble sparingly around the chicken. Lean a Sourdough Crisp artfully against the chicken or velouté. Garnish with a few micro herbs, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Butter and Roasted Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, sliced into thick, diagonal medallions, rests slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken boasts a rich golden-brown crust with tender, white interior visible on the cuts. Beside it, a neat cluster of vibrant green roasted asparagus spears. A glossy, pale yellow lemon-herb butter sauce pools beneath the chicken and glistens on the asparagus. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and clean presentation in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Trim woody ends from asparagus. Toss asparagus with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 8-12 minutes until tender-crisp. Set aside.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board to rest.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Once melted, add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook for 3-5 minutes until sauce slightly reduces.
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Slice each chicken breast into thick, diagonal medallions (not fanned). Arrange chicken and roasted asparagus on individual plates. Spoon lemon-herb butter sauce generously over chicken and asparagus. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato Basil Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of vibrant Tomato Basil Risotto is presented in a shallow, clean white porcelain bowl. The risotto appears creamy and free-flowing, showcasing its characteristic fluid consistency. The rice grains are plump and al dente, coated in a rich reddish-orange sauce from the cooked tomatoes. Interspersed throughout are small, softened pieces of diced onion and minced garlic, with bright green, torn fresh basil leaves providing a striking color contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the top, and a delicate drizzle of golden extra virgin olive oil adds a subtle sheen. The bowl is centered on a simple, rustic wooden table surface. Beside it, a folded cotton napkin and standard silver fork and spoon are neatly arranged. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto does not hold well.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up any extra sauce.
instructions: Heat chicken stock in a saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.
Dice the onion finely. Mince the garlic. Roughly chop the tomatoes.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Do not brown.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until rice edges are translucent (Tostatura).
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed (Sfumatura).
Add chopped tomatoes. Stir for 2 minutes.
Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly.
Wait for each ladleful to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding stock and stirring for 18-20 minutes. Rice should be creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy (Mantecatura).
Stir in most of the fresh basil leaves, torn or roughly chopped.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with a little more stock if needed.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use a good quality chicken stock for best flavour.
Constant stirring is key to achieving a creamy risotto texture.
Taste the rice often to ensure it cooks to your preferred al dente consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Duck Breast with Savory Chocolate-Almond Crumble and Mustard Tatsoi
recipes.visual_description: A modern bistro setting features a clean white porcelain plate on a simple wooden table. A single portion of seared duck breast, sliced into thick medallions, is presented on one side of the plate. The duck skin is crisp and golden-brown, contrasting with the tender, pink interior. Beside the duck, a vibrant pile of mustard-glazed tatsoi, its dark green leaves slightly wilted and glistening, forms a soft bed. A perfectly poached egg with a bright yellow yolk sits atop the tatsoi, ready to burst. A coarse, savory crumble of toasted almond and dark chocolate is sprinkled generously over the duck and egg, providing visual texture and a deep, earthy color. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the textures and colors.
instructions: Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season duck generously with salt and pepper.
Place duck skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe pan. Render fat over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip duck. Sear flesh side for 3-4 minutes.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast for 6-8 minutes until internal temperature reaches 60-63°C for medium-rare. Rest duck for 5-10 minutes before slicing.
For the savory crumble: Toast almonds in a dry pan until fragrant. Let cool. Roughly chop almonds and dark chocolate. Combine with a pinch of salt and chopped thyme.
For the mustard tatsoi: Heat butter in a pan. Add finely minced shallot and minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant.
Add tatsoi. Cook briefly until just wilted. Stir in Dijon mustard, chicken stock, and apple cider vinegar. Cook until liquid reduces slightly and coats tatsoi. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Poach eggs: Bring a pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of vinegar. Carefully crack each egg into the simmering water. Poach for 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are runny. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Slice rested duck breast into thick medallions.
Plate immediately: Arrange a bed of mustard tatsoi. Place sliced duck medallions beside tatsoi. Top with a poached egg. Sprinkle savory chocolate-almond crumble over the duck and egg.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb and Potato Curry (Aloo Gosht)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lamb and Potato Curry (Aloo Gosht) is presented in a clean, white, deep porcelain bowl. The dish features tender, succulent lamb cut into substantial 3-4 cm chunks and soft 3 cm potato cubes, both generously coated in a rich, reddish-brown gravy. The gravy has a smooth consistency with visible flecks of green from the fresh coriander and subtle spice textures. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped coriander leaves garnishes the top, adding a pop of green against the deep tones of the curry. The lamb chunks and potato cubes are arranged naturally within the bowl, allowing the flavorful sauce to pool invitingly. The entire bowl is centered on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. Beside the bowl, a small side plate holds a piece of warm, fluffy naan bread. A simple, folded cotton napkin rests nearby. The scene is illuminated by natural, even overhead lighting, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style ambiance with a subtly blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm naan bread or basmati rice
Offer a side of raita (yogurt dip) or pickled onions

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium (about 600g), peeled, cut into 3 cm cubes

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add lamb chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove lamb, set aside.
Add chopped onions to the same pot. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and slit green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and red chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add tomato puree. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until oil separates.
Reduce heat to low. Whisk yogurt until smooth. Gradually add yogurt to the pot, stirring constantly to prevent curdling. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return seared lamb to the pot. Add salt. Pour in enough water or stock to just cover the lamb.
Bring to a simmer. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 60-90 minutes, or until lamb is tender.
Add potato cubes. Cook for another 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Stir in Garam Masala. Cook for 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Vegetable Korma
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Indian Vegetable Korma, served in a clean, white, round porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The korma features a rich, creamy, golden-orange sauce, with tender, distinct pieces of medium-cubed potatoes, thick-sliced carrots, small broccoli florets, and quartered mushrooms. Professional knife work is evident in the vegetable cuts. A light scattering of fresh, bright green coriander leaves garnishes the top. The curry is fluid, filling the bowl with moderate negative space. Beside the bowl, a portion of fluffy white basmati rice is neatly mounded on a separate white side plate, and a folded piece of golden-brown naan bread. A simple cotton napkin and traditional flatware complete the setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, against a blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Basmati rice
Naan bread
Raita
Mango pickle

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (approx. 150g), peeled, cut into 1 cm thick rounds

ingredients.name: Cashews
ingredients.quantity: 50g, unsalted, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Cook until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric, cumin, coriander, and red chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add pureed tomato. Cook until oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
Drain soaked cashews. Blend with a little water to form a smooth paste. Add cashew paste to the pot. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add potato cubes and carrot rounds. Stir to coat with the masala. Add water or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, or until potatoes are almost tender.
Add broccoli florets and quartered mushrooms. Stir gently. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Reduce heat to low. Whisk plain yogurt until smooth. Slowly stir yogurt into the curry. Do not boil after adding yogurt.
Stir in heavy cream and garam masala. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Season with salt to taste.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper and Mediterranean Chicken Pasta Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mediterranean pasta salad is artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Golden farfalle pasta forms the base, interspersed with generous chunks of roasted red, yellow, and orange bell peppers (cut into 2cm pieces) and tender roasted zucchini slices (1.5cm thick). Diced grilled chicken breast (1.5cm cubes) is distributed throughout, a supporting protein. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced red onion, and glistening black Kalamata olives are mixed in. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered over the top, along with fresh, chopped green parsley and oregano. The salad is lightly coated in a clear, zesty lemon-herb vinaigrette, reflecting light. The presentation is organized yet naturally flowing, leaving moderate negative space. The setting is a simple light wooden table with a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or crusty artisanal bread.
Offer small bowls of extra olives or feta on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Cut red and yellow bell peppers into 2 cm chunks. Slice zucchini into 1.5 cm thick rounds.
Toss bell peppers and zucchini with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add farfalle pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to stop cooking. Drain thoroughly.

Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Grill or pan-sear chicken over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes per side, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Let rest 5 minutes, then dice into 1.5 cm cubes. Let cool.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion. Halve pitted Kalamata olives.
In a small bowl, whisk together 60 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, dried oregano, minced garlic, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine cooled pasta, roasted bell peppers, roasted zucchini, diced chicken, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and Kalamata olives.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine. Add crumbled feta cheese and chopped fresh parsley and oregano.
Toss again lightly. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Serve chilled or at room temperature.
notes: This salad can be prepared up to a day in advance. Store dressing separately and toss just before serving for best texture.
For a vegetarian option, omit chicken and increase other vegetables or add chickpeas.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A deep, white porcelain bowl holds a generous individual portion of Pork Ragu with Pappardelle. The wide, flat pappardelle noodles are thoroughly coated in a rich, dark reddish-brown ragu. Tender, shredded pork chunks are visible throughout the sauce, integrated seamlessly. Finely diced vegetables like onion, carrot, and celery have cooked down into the thick, flavorful sauce. A few small, vibrant red chili slices peek through, hinting at a gentle warmth. The dish is garnished with a scattering of freshly chopped bright green flat-leaf parsley and a generous dusting of finely grated white Pecorino Romano cheese. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl, along with standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows and highlighting its inviting textures and colors. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a clean, casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the rich sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Accompany with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 3-4 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks in batches until well-browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thinly sliced deseeded red chilies. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, bay leaves, and rosemary sprig. Stir to combine.
Bring the ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 2.5 to 3 hours. Cook until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaves and rosemary stem from the pot. Use two forks to shred the pork directly in the sauce. Mix well.
Cook pappardelle pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly. Add reserved pasta water as needed to achieve desired consistency.
Serve hot. Garnish with freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley and grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
notes: The ragu can be made a day in advance; its flavor often improves overnight.
Adjust the amount of red chilies based on desired spice level. For less heat, remove all seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Sheet Pan Mustard Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sheet Pan Mustard Chicken and Potatoes is presented on an everyday round ceramic plate with natural imperfections. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, crispy-skinned and not fanned, sits centrally. Around it are rustic, golden-brown roasted potato wedges, some with slightly charred edges. Vibrant red, burst cherry tomatoes and golden-brown, soft smashed garlic cloves are scattered naturally among the chicken and potatoes. A few fresh green sprigs of rosemary are casually placed on top. The plate is set on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and a casually placed cloth napkin are beside the plate. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, comforting atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing natural portions.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the sheet pan for a family-style meal.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread to soak up pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Smash garlic cloves with the side of a knife.
In a large bowl, combine Dijon mustard, olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Whisk well.
Add chicken thighs and potato wedges to the bowl. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken and potatoes in a single layer on a large sheet pan. Place rosemary sprigs among them.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Remove pan from oven. Add cherry tomatoes and smashed garlic cloves to the pan. Toss gently with potatoes.
Return to oven. Roast for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest on the pan for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: This recipe is high in protein, providing a hearty and satisfying main course.
The sheet pan method makes for easy cleanup.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Cheesy Chicken & Tomato Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: The dish is a rustic, individual portion of baked pasta, served in a small ceramic ramekin. A golden-brown crust of melted mozzarella and Parmesan cheese covers the top, showing bubbly edges. Below, tender elbow macaroni is coated in a rich, savory red tomato sauce. Small, irregular chunks of cooked chicken, diced bright red tomatoes, and tiny flecks of green fresh thyme are visible. Specks of red chili hint at spice. The texture is hearty and comforting. The ramekin rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, showing natural grain. A crumpled, off-white linen napkin is casually placed beside it. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing the homely atmosphere. The scene is uncluttered, focusing on the inviting, comforting dish.

ingredients.name: Small pasta (e.g., ditalini or elbow macaroni)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped chili to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and chopped fresh thyme. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Season with salt and black pepper.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce mixture. Stir to combine thoroughly.
Divide the pasta mixture evenly among four individual oven-safe ramekins or small baking dishes.
Top each ramekin generously with shredded mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden brown.
Let cool slightly before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Bourguignon
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef Bourguignon is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The centerpiece features four to five large, succulent chunks of braised beef chuck, glistening with a deep, mahogany-colored glossy sauce. Interspersed among the meat are whole, tender pearl onions and golden-brown sautéed button mushroom halves. Bright orange carrot rounds provide a pop of color. The stew is finished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley. The sauce has a rich, velvety consistency, pooling slightly around the base. The dish sits on a dark wood bistro table. A side of crusty baguette slices and a simple silver spoon rest on a white cotton napkin nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette
Pair with a glass of Pinot Noir or red Burgundy
Traditionally served with buttery mashed potatoes or boiled potatoes
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Sauté bacon lardons in a heavy pot until crisp. Remove and set aside.
Sear beef chunks in the bacon fat over high heat until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add sliced carrots and onions to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef and bacon to the pot. Add beef stock and bouquet garni.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 hours until meat is tender.
Sauté mushrooms and pearl onions in butter in a separate pan until golden.
Add mushrooms and pearl onions to the stew. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove bouquet garni. Season to taste.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the beef is patted dry before searing to achieve a deep crust.
Use a high-quality dry red wine for the most authentic flavor profile.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Mustard Chicken with Roasted Garlic Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared golden-brown chicken cutlet rests centrally on a round ceramic plate, its surface lightly textured from searing. Beside it, a generous pile of rustic roasted potato wedges, their skins golden and crisp, interiors fluffy. Interspersed among the potatoes are vibrant red cherry tomatoes, some gently burst and caramelized from roasting. A glossy, savory mustard-garlic pan sauce is drizzled lightly over the chicken. Fresh, roughly chopped green parsley is scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color. The plate is white with subtle, natural imperfections, set on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and basic flatware are placed beside the plate. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in family meal atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. Place on a baking sheet.
Toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil, 3 minced garlic cloves, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Roast potatoes for 25 minutes.
While potatoes roast, halve cherry tomatoes.
After 25 minutes, add halved cherry tomatoes to the baking sheet with potatoes. Toss gently.
Return to oven. Roast for another 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and golden, and tomatoes are blistered.
While vegetables finish roasting, prepare chicken. Pat chicken cutlets dry. Season both sides with 5g salt and 2g black pepper.
In a large skillet, heat 30ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cutlets to the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm.
In the same skillet (off heat), add Dijon mustard and remaining 3 minced garlic cloves. Stir to combine with any pan drippings.
To serve, place one chicken cutlet on each plate. Spoon roasted potatoes and tomatoes alongside. Drizzle chicken with the mustard-garlic pan sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Pork Shoulder with Roasted Vegetables and Fresh Corn Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single, inviting portion of Beer-Braised Pork Shoulder is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. The deeply browned pork is served in a large, irregular chunk, revealing its tender, fall-apart texture. A rich, glossy dark brown braising liquid, infused with kidney beans, pools around the pork. Alongside, golden-brown roasted potato wedges and thick roasted onion segments are neatly arranged, their edges slightly caramelized. A vibrant fresh salad of bright yellow corn kernels and diced red tomatoes, lightly dressed, sits beside the main components, atop a small bed of crisp green salad leaves. The overall composition is balanced and appealing, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface and a clean cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the varied textures and warm, inviting colors of the dish, creating an approachable yet refined presentation.

ingredients.name: Onions
ingredients.quantity: 2 large (1 diced, 1 cut into thick wedges)

ingredients.name: Canned Kidney Beans, drained and rinsed
Salad Greens (e.g., mixed greens or butter lettuce)

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season pork chunks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork from pot.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Pour in beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return pork to the pot. Add broth and bay leaves. Liquid should mostly cover the pork. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily pulls apart.

While pork braises, prepare roasted vegetables: Toss potato wedges and onion wedges with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast in the same oven as the pork for the last 45-60 minutes of braising, or until tender and golden brown.
Prepare corn and tomato salad: In a bowl, combine corn kernels and diced tomatoes. Whisk together red wine vinegar, a splash of olive oil, salt, and pepper for dressing. Toss with corn and tomatoes.
Remove pork from oven. Carefully transfer pork chunks to a cutting board. Rest for 10 minutes.
Skim excess fat from braising liquid if desired. Stir in drained kidney beans. Simmer braising liquid on stovetop for 5-10 minutes to slightly reduce and heat beans.

To serve: Place one large pork chunk on each plate. Spoon some braising liquid and kidney beans over the pork. Arrange roasted potato and onion wedges alongside. Place a small mound of salad greens and a portion of the corn and tomato salad on the plate. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Cutlets with Smashed Potatoes and Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion is presented on a rustic, round ceramic plate with subtle imperfections. Two golden-brown, pan-seared chicken cutlets are arranged slightly overlapping, showcasing their crispy exterior and tender interior. Beside the chicken, a generous mound of irregularly smashed potatoes reveals a fluffy, comforting texture, with some skin visible for a homely feel. Scattered around the plate are vibrant, roasted cherry tomato halves, some beautifully burst, displaying their rich red and orange hues. A creamy, pale yellow Dijon mustard sauce is generously drizzled over the chicken and pools naturally on the plate. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is simple and uncluttered, allowing the comfort food to be the focal point.
