Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
While beef cooks, prepare parmesan crisps. Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Create 8-12 small mounds of grated parmesan cheese, spaced apart. Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Let cool on the baking sheet, then carefully remove.

For the kidney bean ragout: Drain and rinse kidney beans. In a separate saucepan, combine 300g of kidney beans with 50ml of beef broth (from the braising liquid or fresh). Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some beans whole for texture. Stir in 1 clove minced garlic and a pinch of dried chili flakes. Heat gently.
Once beef is tender, taste and adjust seasoning of the beef and ragout.
To serve: Ladle a portion of the spicy kidney bean ragout onto the center of each plate. Arrange 2-3 tender beef chunks on top of or alongside the ragout.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and 2-3 parmesan crisps.
notes: This dish benefits from slow cooking, allowing the beef to become exceptionally tender and the flavors to meld. The spiciness can be adjusted by varying the amount of dried chili flakes.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Estilo Español
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Spanish Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown, seared thick chunks of chicken are nestled within a bed of saffron-infused rice. The rice is a rich yellow-orange, with individual grains visible and a tender, slightly moist texture. Diced red bell pepper and bright green peas are evenly distributed, adding vivid color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley provides a final touch of green. The dish is centrally composed, leaving moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and even natural lighting, creating an inviting, authentic Spanish bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine or a pitcher of sangria.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into thick chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or paella pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion and diced red bell pepper to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, smoked paprika, and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in hot chicken broth and saffron threads. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken to the pan.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice absorbs most liquid and is tender. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in green peas. Cover and let rest off heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Allowing the rice to rest off heat helps it absorb remaining liquid and become fluffy.

recipes.recipe_name: Cured Beef, Fermented Potato & Mushroom Starter
recipes.visual_description: A single, small starter portion is elegantly presented on a round, matte, handcrafted ceramic plate in a light cream or beige tone. A small, organic mound of the mixed tartare is positioned slightly off-center, showcasing the natural textures and colors. Diced cured beef pieces, with their deep reddish-brown hue, are interspersed with creamy white small fermented potato cubes, pale brown/grey thinly sliced pickled mushrooms, and delicate light pink/purple pickled red onion slices. The composition is clean and ingredient-focused, with ample negative space on the plate highlighting the minimalistic aesthetic. A very sparse scattering of finely chopped fresh green chives provides a subtle, natural color accent. The plate rests on a light-colored, natural wood or stone surface. A neatly folded, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is placed beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing textures. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle, out-of-focus hint of natural elements like a green plant.

ingredients.name: Fresh chives or dill, finely chopped

instructions: Prepare beef for curing. Pat beef sirloin completely dry.
Mix curing blend: combine 50g coarse salt, 25g granulated sugar, 5g crushed black peppercorns, and 1 bay leaf.
Rub beef entirely with the curing blend. Ensure full coverage.
Place beef in an airtight container. Refrigerate for 24-48 hours. Turn beef once during curing.
Remove cured beef from container. Rinse thoroughly under cold water. Pat completely dry with paper towels.
Thinly slice cured beef against the grain. Dice slices into small 5mm cubes. Set aside.
Prepare potatoes for fermentation. Peel potatoes. Dice into small 5mm cubes.
Prepare potato brine: Dissolve 20g coarse salt in 500ml filtered water.
Place potato cubes in a clean jar. Pour brine over potatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged.
Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Ferment until desired tanginess is achieved.
Drain fermented potatoes. Set aside.
Prepare mushrooms and red onion for pickling. Clean mushrooms; slice thinly. Thinly slice red onion.
Prepare pickling brine: In a saucepan, combine 250ml white wine vinegar, 250ml water, 10g coarse salt, and 10g granulated sugar. Bring to a boil.
Add sliced mushrooms and red onion to the hot pickling brine. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Let mushrooms and onion cool completely in the brine.
Drain pickled mushrooms and red onion. Set aside.
Assemble the starter: In a bowl, gently combine diced cured beef, fermented potato cubes, pickled mushrooms, and pickled red onion.
Drizzle with 5ml olive oil. Add 5g finely chopped fresh chives or dill. Mix gently.
Plate immediately. Serve as a cold starter.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-yellow bomba rice, infused with saffron, is mounded slightly in the center, appearing moist and flavorful, not dry. Scattered throughout the rice are vibrant orange diced carrots and bright green peas. Nestled naturally within and on top of the rice are golden-brown, tender chunks of boneless chicken thigh, showcasing their seared exterior. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green and freshness. A lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft, casual restaurant-style background that remains unobtrusive.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or shallow pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion and carrots to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced.
Add bomba rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan, nestling it into the rice. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice has absorbed most of the liquid and is tender. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pineapple & Coconut Delight
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the dessert is elegantly presented in a small, handcrafted ceramic bowl in a soft cream hue, resting on a light reclaimed wood table surface. The pale, creamy coconut pudding has a smooth, delicate texture, with a subtle translucency. It is topped with vibrant yellow, small diced fresh pineapple chunks, offering a bright, natural contrast. A light drizzle of golden, clear pineapple core syrup glistens over the fruit. Scattered sparingly are delicate, toasted coconut flakes and a fresh mint sprig, adding subtle color and freshness. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. A natural beige linen napkin is folded nearby, and soft natural light bathes the scene.
instructions: Dice 200g pineapple flesh into small cubes. Place in a clean glass jar.
Add 100ml water and 15ml maple syrup to the jar. Stir well.
Loosely cover the jar. Ferment at room temperature (20-25°C) for 2-3 days. Look for slight bubbling and a tangy aroma. Skim any surface mold.
Cut remaining pineapple flesh (approx. 200g) into small cubes. Set aside for garnish.
Simmer remaining pineapple core and rind with 200ml water and 30ml maple syrup for 15 minutes. Strain the syrup; discard solids.
In a saucepan, combine coconut milk, strained liquid from the fermented pineapple jar, agar-agar powder, and remaining 15ml maple syrup.
Bring mixture to a gentle boil over medium heat. Whisk constantly for 2 minutes until agar-agar fully dissolves.
Remove from heat. Stir in lime juice.
Pour pudding mixture into 4 individual serving bowls or molds.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until fully set.
Serve each pudding topped with fresh diced pineapple cubes, a drizzle of the pineapple core/rind syrup, toasted coconut flakes, and a fresh mint sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Lemon Herb Chicken with Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken and potatoes rests on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, its skin crisp and taut, is the focal point. Beside it, several irregular wedges of golden-roasted Yukon Gold potatoes display crispy edges and a fluffy interior. Interspersed are soft, caramelized red onion wedges and tender, roasted garlic cloves. Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs, vibrant green, are thoughtfully placed for color and aroma. A light, glistening pan sauce, infused with lemon and herbs, is artfully drizzled over the chicken and potatoes. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing elements to breathe. The background is a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin to the side. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich, earthy tones and varied textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty artisan bread for dipping in the pan sauce.

ingredients.name: Whole Chicken
ingredients.quantity: 1.5 kg, cut into 8 pieces (2 breasts, 2 thighs, 2 drumsticks, 2 wings)

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 1 kg, scrubbed, cut into 2 cm wedges

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1 large, half thinly sliced, half for juice

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken pieces very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
In a large bowl, toss potato wedges, red onion wedges, smashed garlic, rosemary, thyme, oregano, and half of the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange chicken pieces and potato mixture in a single layer on a large baking tray or roasting pan.
Place lemon slices among the chicken and potatoes.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden brown. Flip potatoes halfway through.
Carefully remove chicken and potatoes to a warm platter. Tent with foil.
Place roasting pan on stovetop over medium heat. Add white wine (if using) and chicken broth to the pan. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Bring to a simmer and reduce sauce by half, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in fresh lemon juice from the remaining half lemon. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve chicken and potatoes immediately, drizzled with the pan sauce.
notes: Ensure chicken is thoroughly patted dry for maximum crispiness.
Do not overcrowd the baking sheet; use two if necessary for even roasting.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Stuffed Chicken with Potato Rosti and Spicy Cheese Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared stuffed chicken breast, sliced into three thick, juicy medallions, anchors the white porcelain plate. The golden-brown crust of the chicken contrasts with the creamy, light-colored stuffing peeking out, revealing hints of diced red pimento and green herbs. Beside the chicken, a perfectly round, golden-crisp potato rosti sits, its shredded potato strands visibly textured. A generous drizzle of vibrant, creamy orange-hued spicy cheese sauce flows over both the chicken and the rosti, creating a natural, inviting pattern. Two bright yellow and white soft-boiled egg quarters are placed neatly beside the chicken, adding a rich visual element. Freshly chopped green parsley is scattered lightly over the dish for a pop of color. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: A crisp green salad
instructions: Prepare Stuffing: Dice 150g mushrooms, 50g pimento, 1 shallot, 2 cloves garlic finely. Sauté in 15g butter until softened. Cool. Dice 50g cheddar cheese. Mix sautéed vegetables with diced cheddar. Season with salt and pepper.
Stuff Chicken: Butterfly 4 chicken breasts. Pound gently to even thickness. Divide stuffing among breasts. Roll tightly. Secure with toothpicks.

Cook Chicken: Preheat oven to 180°C. Heat 15ml olive oil in oven-safe pan. Sear stuffed chicken until golden brown on all sides. Transfer pan to oven. Bake 15-20 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove toothpicks. Rest chicken 5 minutes.
Prepare Potato Rosti: Grate 800g potatoes. Squeeze out all moisture. Mix with 2 beaten eggs, 5g salt, 2g black pepper. Form into 4 round patties, 1.5 cm thick.
Cook Rosti: Heat 20g butter and 15ml olive oil in non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook rosti patties 8-10 minutes per side until golden and crispy. Keep warm.

Make Cheese Sauce: In small saucepan, melt 50g cheddar and 4 slices American cheese with 100ml heavy cream over low heat. Whisk until smooth. Stir in 30g Dijon mustard and 15ml hot sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare Garnish Eggs: Soft-boil 4 eggs for 6-7 minutes. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Peel. Quarter each egg.

Plate Dish: Place one potato rosti on each plate. Slice each stuffed chicken breast into 3-4 thick medallions. Arrange chicken medallions next to rosti. Drizzle cheese sauce over chicken and rosti. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and 2 soft-boiled egg quarters.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: Golden pan-seared chicken breast, whole or in two thick pieces, positioned on a pristine white round plate. Earthy brown sautéed cremini mushroom slices are artfully scattered around. A rich, glossy Marsala wine sauce, deep amber, pools around the chicken, lightly coating it. Vibrant green fresh chopped Italian parsley garnishes the dish. Presented on a light wooden table with a crisp white linen napkin and silver flatware. A subtle glass of red wine in the background. Natural, even lighting highlights textures: crisp chicken surface, tender mushrooms, smooth shimmering sauce. Balanced composition with negative space, focusing on the refined single serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple buttered pasta or creamy polenta.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a dry red wine, such as a Chianti or Merlot.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter, cold, cut into cubes

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Pound each breast to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Dredge chicken breasts lightly in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the same skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with Marsala wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Reduce heat to low. Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Allow chicken to warm through in the sauce.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in cold butter until melted and incorporated (mantecare).
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use a good quality dry Marsala wine for best flavor, not cooking Marsala.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beef and Pineapple Flatbread
recipes.visual_description: The Savory Beef and Pineapple Flatbread sits on a well-used wooden dining table, centered on a rustic, round ceramic plate with a slightly chipped rim. The golden-brown flatbread crust peeks out from under a generous layer of bubbly, melted mozzarella cheese, which is golden in spots. Visible through the cheese are hearty, irregular chunks of browned ground beef and golden pineapple pieces, scattered evenly across the surface. The beef is finely crumbled and cooked through, while the pineapple maintains its distinct shape and vibrant yellow color. A few specks of dried oregano are visible on the melted cheese. The portions are substantial, filling the plate without overcrowding. The lighting is warm and cozy, mimicking natural kitchen light. A simple cloth napkin is casually draped beside the plate.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add beef mince. Break it apart. Cook until browned, about 8 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pan. Cook until softened, 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, water, salt, pepper, and oregano. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in pineapple chunks. Remove from heat.
Place flatbreads on a baking tray.
Divide beef mixture evenly over each flatbread. Spread to edges.
Top each flatbread generously with shredded mozzarella.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and crust is golden.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper, Pineapple, Black Bean, and Mozzarella Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl, showcasing its vibrant array of colors. Diced red, yellow, and orange bell peppers create a bright base, interspersed with golden pineapple cubes, dark black beans, and pale yellow corn kernels. Halved white mozzarella bocconcini add creamy contrast. The ingredients are loosely tossed, creating a natural, slightly mounded composition with ample negative space around the edges of the bowl. A light sheen from the chili-lime dressing coats each component. Freshly chopped green cilantro is generously sprinkled over the top, adding a final pop of color and texture. The overall presentation is clean, organized, and inviting, emphasizing the freshness and diversity of the chopped ingredients.
instructions: Dice pineapple, red bell pepper, yellow bell pepper, and red onion into uniform small pieces.
Rinse black beans and corn under cold water; drain well. Halve mozzarella balls.
Combine diced pineapple, bell peppers, red onion, black beans, corn, and mozzarella in a large mixing bowl.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, chili powder, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper to create the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Add chopped cilantro.
Gently toss all ingredients until well combined and coated with dressing.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.
notes: Chilling the salad before serving enhances the flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Confit and Tomato Crostini with Crispy Vermicelli
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white rectangular plate, showcasing three elegantly arranged crostini. Each golden-brown toasted baguette slice is topped generously with tender, shredded chicken confit. Vibrant ruby-red cherry tomato confit, glistening with olive oil, contrasts beautifully. Delicate, bright green basil chiffonade is scattered across, adding freshness. A sprinkle of golden-brown, finely crushed crispy vermicelli pasta provides unique texture. A dark, glossy balsamic glaze artfully zigzags across the crostini and plate, adding depth. The composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and natural, even lighting, creating a refined bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C.
Place cherry tomatoes, sliced garlic, 100 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper in a small oven-safe dish. Toss gently.
Bake for 45-60 minutes, or until tomatoes are soft and slightly wrinkled. Set aside to cool.
Season chicken breast with salt and pepper.
In a small saucepan, cover chicken breast with water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken. Shred or finely dice when cool enough to handle.
Cook vermicelli pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain very well. Spread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake pasta at 180°C for 15-20 minutes, or until completely dry and crispy. Alternatively, shallow fry in a small amount of olive oil until golden and crisp. Break into small pieces.
Slice baguette into 1 cm thick rounds. Brush lightly with remaining olive oil.
Toast baguette slices in a pan or oven until golden brown and crisp.
To assemble: Spoon tomato confit onto each toasted baguette slice.
Top with shredded chicken.
Finely chiffonade half of the fresh basil. Sprinkle over crostini.
Sprinkle crispy vermicelli pieces over the basil.
Drizzle with balsamic glaze. Garnish with remaining whole basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sausages with Rum-Glazed Pineapple and Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Pan-Seared Sausages with Rum-Glazed Pineapple and Creamy Polenta. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a light wooden table in a modern bistro setting. Creamy, golden-yellow polenta forms a smooth base. Two pan-seared pork sausages, cooked to a rich golden-brown, are placed as whole pieces or thick medallions beside the polenta. Vibrant yellow pineapple wedges, lightly caramelized and glistening with a dark rum glaze, are arranged neatly. A light drizzle of pan sauce coats the elements. The dish is garnished with fresh chopped parsley. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing textures and colors. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting creates a professional and inviting appearance.

ingredients.name: Fresh Pineapple
ingredients.quantity: 300g (peeled, cored, cut into 1.5 cm thick wedges)

instructions: Bring chicken stock to a boil in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, stirring frequently, until thickened and creamy, about 10-15 minutes.
Stir in milk and 15g butter into polenta. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausages. Cook, turning occasionally, until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 12-15 minutes. Remove sausages from skillet. Keep warm.
In the same skillet, add remaining 15g butter. Add finely diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pineapple wedges to skillet. Cook for 3-5 minutes, turning once, until lightly caramelized.
Pour rum into the skillet with pineapple. Deglaze, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, allowing alcohol to evaporate and sauce to slightly thicken.

Spoon creamy polenta onto the center of each plate. Place 1-2 sausages beside or on top of the polenta. Arrange rum-glazed pineapple wedges next to the sausage. Spoon any remaining pan sauce over the dish. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato Chicken with Potato Cream and Sourdough Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a clean, light beige handcrafted ceramic plate, emphasizing negative space. A generous, organically shaped dollop of smooth, creamy potato cream forms the base. A whole, pan-seared chicken thigh, with its golden-brown, crispy skin facing upwards, rests centrally on the potato cream. The chicken is plump and unsliced. Scattered around the chicken are irregular, rustic pieces of golden-brown sourdough crisp, along with thin, translucent slivers of baked onion, adding texture and subtle color. A small, vibrant green sprig of fresh thyme is placed gently on the plate, providing a natural accent. The overall color palette is earthy and natural, featuring creamy whites, rich golden-browns, and soft greens. The composition is clean and minimalist, highlighting the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. The plate sits on a light-colored, natural wood surface, accompanied by a simple, undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its textures and warmth. The background is clean and unfussy, with a hint of a natural plant, maintaining an eco-conscious, serene aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (onion skins, potato peels, carrot ends)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato-Garlic Paste (3-5 days in advance): Roughly chop tomatoes, 3 garlic cloves, and a quarter of the onion. Blend with 10g sea salt until smooth. Transfer to a clean glass jar. Loosely cover. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Stir daily. It should become tangy and slightly bubbly. Refrigerate once fermented.
Make Vegetable Stock: Combine vegetable scraps with 500 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes. Strain, discard solids. Set stock aside.

Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. In a bowl, combine chicken with 60 ml (4 tablespoons) of the fermented tomato-garlic paste. Mix well to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours refrigerated.

Cook Chicken: Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Make Potato Cream: Peel potatoes. Cut into 3 cm chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Pass potatoes through a ricer or mash thoroughly. Gradually whisk in 15 ml olive oil and 100 ml of warm vegetable stock until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Adjust consistency with more stock if needed.

Prepare Sourdough Crisp: Tear day-old sourdough bread into irregular 2-3 cm pieces. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a quarter of the remaining onion, thinly sliced. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake at 190°C for 8-12 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Crush lightly after cooling if desired.
Serve: Spoon a generous portion of potato cream onto each plate. Place one chicken thigh on top. Scatter sourdough crisps around the chicken. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Italian Chicken and Potato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Italian Chicken and Potato Skillet is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, seared chicken thighs, their exteriors slightly crisp, are the focal point. They are nestled among tender, quartered baby potatoes, earthy quartered cremini mushrooms, and vibrant diced tomatoes. Melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese generously covers the chicken and vegetables, with some strands stretching invitingly. The dish boasts a rich color palette of golden chicken, red tomatoes, brown mushrooms, and creamy white cheese. A sprinkle of fresh green basil leaves adds a pop of color and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro: the plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by traditional silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the inviting textures and colors of the food. A small, elegant bowl of freshly grated Parmesan cheese sits subtly in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette makes a good accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in quartered baby potatoes and quartered mushrooms. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Add dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet. Nestle them into the vegetables.
Cover the skillet. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Uncover skillet. Sprinkle shredded mozzarella over the chicken and vegetables. Cover briefly until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh basil. Serve directly from the skillet or plate individually.
notes: For extra flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and crisp the skin during searing.

recipes.recipe_name: Maple-Roasted Cherry and Citrus Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, resting on a light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. The composition is clean and balanced, featuring a vibrant array of fresh and roasted fruits with creamy accents. A base layer of glistening, segmented citrus supremes, including bright orange and pink grapefruit, is artfully arranged. Scattered over this base are whole, plump roasted cherries, some slightly caramelized, showcasing their deep ruby-red color. Strategically placed among the fruits are smooth, creamy white dollops of vanilla mascarpone cream, adding a luxurious texture contrast. A few small, fresh green mint leaves are delicately placed on top of the cream and fruit, providing a pop of fresh color and natural elegance. The elements are well-proportioned with moderate negative space, creating a professional yet inviting appearance. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the fresh textures and vibrant colors of the fruit and cream.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Place pitted cherries on the prepared tray. Drizzle with 40ml maple syrup and zest from half the lemon. Toss gently to coat.
Roast cherries for 15-20 minutes, or until slightly softened and caramelized. Remove from oven. Let cool completely.
Split vanilla bean lengthwise. Scrape seeds into a medium bowl. Add mascarpone cheese, heavy cream, powdered sugar, and remaining 20ml maple syrup to the bowl.
Whip the mixture with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Do not overmix.

Segment oranges and grapefruit: Cut off the top and bottom of each citrus fruit. Stand fruit on a cutting board. Slice off the peel and white pith following the curve of the fruit. Working over a bowl, carefully cut along the membranes to release individual segments (supremes). Squeeze remaining juice from membranes into the bowl. Discard membranes.
To assemble, place a small amount of citrus juice from the bowl on the bottom of each of four individual dessert plates. Arrange a base layer of mixed citrus segments on each plate.
Evenly distribute the cooled roasted cherries over the citrus segments on each plate.
Place 2-3 generous dollops of vanilla mascarpone cream among the fruit on each plate.
Garnish each serving with 3-4 fresh mint leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Tea Crémeux, Sweet Wine Pear, Brown Butter Sable
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented on a pristine, oversized white bone china plate, allowing for abundant negative space that highlights the minimalist composition. A single, perfectly formed quenelle of pale, creamy black tea crémeux rests slightly off-center, its surface smooth and inviting. Beside it, two or three precisely cut 1cm diced sweet wine-poached pear pieces, their translucent golden hue glistening, are artfully arranged. Small, glossy droplets of amber brandy fluid gel are strategically placed around the crémeux and pear, catching the light. A delicate, sandy sprinkle of golden-brown butter sable crumble provides textural contrast and visual warmth. The entire composition is restrained yet impactful, embodying sophisticated simplicity. A single, tiny purple edible viola flower or a vibrant green micro mint sprig serves as the sole, precise garnish, adding a subtle touch of color. The plate sits on a luxurious, lightly veined grey marble surface. Professional, dramatic lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and the architectural precision of the plating. The scene is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing the artistry of the dish.
instructions: Prepare Black Tea Crémeux:
Heat cream and tea leaves in a saucepan until simmering. Remove from heat. Steep 10 minutes. Strain, pressing tea leaves. Reheat cream gently.
Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a bowl until pale.
Slowly pour hot cream into egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until thickened (82-84°C). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter cubes and vanilla until melted and smooth.
Pass crémeux through a fine-mesh sieve. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill 4 hours minimum.
Prepare Sweet Wine Poached Pear:
Peel, core, and cut pears into 1 cm dice or small, elegant segments.
Combine sweet wine, water, sugar, and vanilla bean in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Add pear pieces. Gently poach 5-7 minutes until tender but firm. Do not overcook.
Carefully remove pears with a slotted spoon. Chill immediately.
Reserve 100 mL of the poaching liquid for the fluid gel.
Prepare Brandy Fluid Gel:
In a small saucepan, combine reserved pear poaching liquid, brandy, and agar-agar.
Bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Boil 1 minute.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until firm, about 30 minutes.
Once firm, cut into small pieces. Blend in a high-speed blender until completely smooth and gel-like.
Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Transfer to a squeeze bottle or small piping bag. Chill until ready to use.
Prepare Brown Butter Sable Crumble:

Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Continue cooking until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. Strain brown butter into a bowl, discarding solids. Chill slightly until semi-solid.
In a bowl, combine flour, powdered sugar, and salt.
Add the cooled brown butter. Rub with fingertips until a fine, sandy crumble forms.
Spread crumble on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake at 160°C (325°F) for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Stir halfway through. Let cool completely.
Assemble and Plate (Serves 4):
On each chilled dessert plate, place a single elegant quenelle of black tea crémeux.
Artfully arrange three to five 1cm diced poached pear pieces next to the crémeux.
Dot the plate with small, precise drops of the brandy fluid gel.
Sprinkle a small amount of brown butter sable crumble next to the other elements for texture.
Garnish with a single, tiny edible flower or a micro mint sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown roasted chicken thigh is centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Surrounding the chicken are vibrant halved cherry tomatoes, deep purple red onion wedges, and shiny black Kalamata olives, all glistening with savory pan juices. The roasted vegetables are tender with slightly caramelized edges. Fresh green sprigs of oregano and thyme are artfully placed on top of the chicken and among the vegetables, adding a pop of color and freshness. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests beside the chicken, ready for squeezing. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver fork and knife beside the plate. The background features a softly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a relaxed yet refined dining atmosphere, illuminated by natural, even lighting. The composition is balanced, showcasing the natural textures and rich colors of the Mediterranean ingredients with appropriate negative space, emphasizing the rustic elegance of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in pan juices.
Serve with a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with 3g salt and 1g black pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil, red onion wedges, smashed garlic, halved cherry tomatoes, and Kalamata olives to the pan. Sauté 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in 2g salt and 1g black pepper. Add chicken broth and fresh oregano and thyme sprigs.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them among the vegetables.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 20-25 minutes, until internal chicken temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove pan from oven. Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and vegetables with pan juices. Garnish with fresh lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to taste.
Chicken breasts can be substituted; adjust cooking time as needed to prevent drying.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Gochujang Pork Belly Bites
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve crispy Gochujang pork belly bites are arranged artfully on a light reclaimed wood serving board. Each bite-sized piece of pork belly, approximately 2.5 cm cubes, exhibits a rich, caramelized reddish-brown exterior from searing, with visible crispy skin. A vibrant red-orange dollop of finely chopped kimchi relish sits atop each pork cube, providing a striking color contrast. The kimchi's texture is slightly coarse, showcasing its fermented nature. Thinly sliced bright green scallions and a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds are scattered over the bites as a natural garnish. The composition is minimalistic, featuring ample white space on the board. The setting includes a natural beige undyed linen napkin subtly folded to one side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the ingredients. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural plant greenery, creating an eco-conscious and serene aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an appetizer or canapé.
Offer small individual perilla or lettuce leaves for optional wrapping (ssam style).
instructions: Cut pork belly into 2.5 cm cubes. Score the skin lightly.
In a large pot, cover pork belly cubes with water. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 30 minutes until tender. Drain well. Pat dry thoroughly.
In a bowl, combine gochujang, soy sauce, minced garlic, minced ginger, sesame oil, brown sugar, and black pepper. Mix well to create the marinade.
Toss the cooked pork belly cubes with the marinade. Ensure all sides are coated.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated pork belly cubes, skin-side down first.
Sear pork belly cubes for 5-7 minutes per side, turning frequently, until all sides are golden brown and crispy. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove from heat. Drain excess oil.
Finely chop kimchi to create a relish texture.
Thinly slice scallions for garnish.
Arrange crispy pork belly cubes on a serving platter. Top each cube with a small dollop of chopped kimchi. Garnish with sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds.
notes: This recipe utilizes pork belly, ensuring a flavorful and crispy bite while minimizing food waste by using the skin.
The use of fermented kimchi aligns with sustainable food practices and adds a complex flavor profile.
Focus on fresh, seasonal ingredients where possible to enhance sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Parmesan Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, is the focal point on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. It is generously coated with a creamy, pale ivory garlic Parmesan sauce, which pools invitingly around its base. The chicken displays a crisp, caramelized exterior from searing. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is scattered over the chicken and sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a light, natural wood table surface, with a folded off-white cotton napkin beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware is placed neatly alongside. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and warm tones. The arrangement is professional, balanced, and approachable, with moderate negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pasta, polenta, or crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt, pepper, and Italian herbs.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add shallot to skillet. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in heavy cream and Parmesan cheese. Whisk until smooth. Simmer 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty chicken and vegetable stew is served on a round, rustic ceramic plate. A generous scoop of fluffy brown rice anchors the dish. Tender, golden-brown chicken thighs, braised to perfection, rest beside and slightly atop the rice. Soft, coin-cut carrots and diced red tomatoes are nestled within the rich, savory broth, which pools gently on the plate. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley adds a vibrant green contrast. The dish has a natural, unpretentious appearance, showcasing comforting textures and warm colors. It is placed on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, inviting kitchen light, with a simple cloth napkin and everyday cutlery nearby. The presentation is homely and inviting.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down first, until deeply golden brown, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and coin-cut carrots to the pot. Sauté, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom, until vegetables soften, about 7-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add canned diced tomatoes, chicken stock, bay leaf, and fresh thyme sprigs to the pot. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the liquid.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is fork-tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While the stew simmers, prepare brown rice according to package instructions.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs from the stew before serving.
Serve hot stew over individual portions of cooked brown rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Miso Salmon with Blanched Bok Choy
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single individual portion. A thick, pan-seared salmon fillet, golden-brown and crisp on the skin side, rests centrally. Its flesh is moist and flaky, brushed with a glossy, rich brown miso glaze that shimmers under natural light. Beside the salmon, vibrant green bok choy leaves, blanched to tender-crisp perfection, are arranged neatly. The bok choy retains its natural shape, some larger leaves, some smaller, showing a gentle sauté with minced garlic and grated ginger. A scattering of toasted white sesame seeds adorns the salmon and bok choy, adding a textural contrast and nutty aroma. The plate has ample negative space, allowing the colors of the salmon and bok choy to stand out. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks and a small white rice bowl are placed to the side, completing the authentic Japanese-inspired dining experience. A folded cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a side of steamed white rice
Can be accompanied by a small bowl of clear dashi soup
instructions: Prepare Miso Glaze: Combine miso paste, mirin, sake, soy sauce, sugar, and toasted sesame oil in a small saucepan. Whisk thoroughly. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Cook for 2-3 minutes, whisking occasionally, until the glaze slightly thickens. Remove from heat.
Prepare Salmon: Pat salmon fillets dry completely with paper towels. Season the skin side generously with salt and black pepper.

Sear Salmon: Heat neutral oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 5-7 minutes until the skin is crispy and golden brown. Flip the salmon fillets.

Glaze Salmon: Brush the cooked side of each salmon fillet liberally with the prepared miso glaze. Continue cooking for 1-2 minutes, brushing occasionally, until the salmon reaches desired doneness. Internal temperature should be at least 63°C (145°F).
Prepare Bok Choy: Separate bok choy leaves. Wash them thoroughly under cold water. Mince garlic. Grate fresh ginger.

Blanch Bok Choy: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a rolling boil. Add the bok choy leaves. Blanch for 1-2 minutes until tender-crisp and vibrant green. Immediately drain and transfer to an ice bath or rinse under cold water to stop cooking. Drain again thoroughly.

Sauté Bok Choy: Heat a small amount of sesame oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the blanched bok choy. Toss gently to coat. Season with a pinch of salt.

Plate Dish: Place one seared miso-glazed salmon fillet on each clean plate. Arrange the sautéed bok choy neatly beside the salmon. Drizzle any remaining miso glaze over the salmon. Garnish generously with toasted white sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon, Olives, and Capers
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and tender, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. It is nestled amidst a vibrant, glistening sauce composed of halved bright red cherry tomatoes, dark, pitted Kalamata olives, and small green capers. The sauce lightly coats the chicken and pools around it, showcasing its rich, savory texture. A generous sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley and a hint of grated lemon zest add a pop of green and yellow, enhancing the fresh aroma. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's inviting colors and textures, with ample negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and lemon juice. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Add halved cherry tomatoes, pitted Kalamata olives, and drained capers to the skillet. Simmer for 5 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Garnish with fresh lemon zest and chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Manzo Brasato al Aglio Nero con Farro e Verdure di Scarto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous, dark mahogany chunk of fork-tender braised beef sits prominently on a creamy, unglazed ceramic plate. Beside it, a rustic mound of earthy beige farro. A vibrant pile of dark green cavolo nero, sautéed until tender-crisp, adds a pop of color. A glossy, rich brown reduction of the braising liquid pools around the beef, catching the light. A few soft, deep black garlic cloves are nestled near the beef, adding a unique visual and textural element. A single fresh rosemary sprig garnishes the dish naturally. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin and simple, elegant Italian flatware are subtly present. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic textures and natural colors of the sustainable ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty, rustic bread to sop up the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed lightly with olive oil and red wine vinegar.

ingredients.name: Beef or vegetable stock (made from scrap vegetables)
Cavolo nero or kale
ingredients.quantity: 200 g, tough stems removed, leaves roughly chopped

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced fresh garlic and crushed black garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef or vegetable stock, rosemary sprigs, and bay leaf. Liquid should almost cover the beef. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F). Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While beef braises, cook farro according to package directions. Typically, boil 3 parts water to 1 part farro. Simmer until tender but still chewy, about 20-25 minutes. Drain excess water.
In the last 15 minutes of braising, heat a small amount of olive oil in a pan. Sauté chopped cavolo nero until tender-crisp. Season with salt.

Remove beef from pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids and herbs. Skim off excess fat. Reduce liquid over medium heat until slightly thickened and glossy.
Serve each beef chunk with a portion of farro and sautéed cavolo nero. Drizzle with the reduced braising liquid. Garnish with a fresh rosemary sprig.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by encouraging the use of vegetable trimmings (onion ends, carrot peels, celery leaves) to make a flavorful stock for braising.
Black garlic is a fermented ingredient that adds a unique, umami-rich sweetness and depth to the dish, aligning with eco-conscious cooking methods.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Beer Risotto, Smoked Chili Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, precisely cut into two or three thick, tender pieces, rests elegantly atop a naturally mounded, fluid beer-infused risotto. The creamy risotto flows gently outward, showcasing its luxurious texture without constraint. A vibrant crimson smoked chili oil is artfully drizzled around the chicken and risotto, creating an organic, abstract pattern on the pristine white plate. A delicate, golden-brown shard of crispy chicken skin stands upright, providing a textural counterpoint and height. A scattering of bright green micro-cilantro or finely snipped chives provides a final, precise touch of fresh color and aroma. The composition is deliberately minimalist, with abundant negative space on a large, round, premium bone china plate. The dish is presented on a polished dark grey marble surface. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and elegant, minimalist silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Dramatic, soft overhead lighting creates subtle shadows, highlighting the dish's textures and forms. The background is completely out of focus, maintaining an ultra-minimalist aesthetic with maximum negative space.

ingredients.name: High-quality pale ale or pilsner beer
Red chilies (e.g., Fresno or bird's eye)

instructions: Prepare chicken: Sous vide chicken breasts to 63°C for 1.5 hours. This ensures tenderness and pasteurization. Remove from bath, pat very dry. Reserve skin for crisping.

Crisp chicken skin: Place reserved chicken skin between two sheets of parchment paper. Place between two baking sheets. Bake at 180°C until golden and crisp, about 15-20 minutes. Season lightly with salt. Break into shards.

Make chili oil: Finely chop red chilies. Gently heat 50ml olive oil in a small saucepan. Add chopped chilies and smoked paprika. Infuse slowly over very low heat for 15 minutes. Do not brown. Strain oil through a fine-mesh sieve into a small bowl. Discard solids.
Start risotto: Melt 20g butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Toast rice: Add Carnaroli rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Deglaze rice: Pour in beer. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.

Cook risotto: Begin adding warm chicken stock, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each addition to be nearly absorbed before adding the next. Continue until rice is creamy and al dente, about 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be fluid.
Finish risotto: Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 20g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Risotto should be fluid and flowing.

Sear chicken: Heat a large, oven-safe pan with a drizzle of olive oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear until skin is golden, crispy, and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F), about 5-7 minutes. Flip. Cook briefly, 1-2 minutes, to finish. Rest chicken 5 minutes.

Plate: Spoon a generous portion of fluid risotto onto the center of each warm plate, allowing it to spread naturally. Slice each chicken breast into two or three thick, diagonal pieces. Arrange chicken pieces artfully on top of the risotto. Drizzle smoked chili oil around the chicken and risotto. Garnish with a shard of crispy chicken skin and a scattering of micro-cilantro or finely snipped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: The quality of beer significantly impacts the risotto's flavor. Choose a high-quality pale ale or pilsner that you enjoy drinking.
Ensure the risotto remains fluid and creamy; add a little more warm stock if it becomes too thick.
Adjust the amount of red chilies in the oil to control the spice level according to preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Shredded Chicken Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A homely serving of Simple Shredded Chicken Crostini rests on a well-used wooden dining table. Several crostini pieces are arranged casually on a simple, round ceramic platter. Each crostini features a golden-brown, crispy toasted baguette slice, generously topped with a mound of creamy, off-white shredded chicken mixture. The chicken mixture is chunky with visible finely diced celery and small flecks of red onion. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast on top. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, as if served directly from a family kitchen. The lighting is warm and cozy, suggesting a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. A casually placed cloth napkin is visible nearby. The scene is clean and uncluttered, focusing on the comforting appeal of the dish.
instructions: Poach chicken breasts. Place chicken in a saucepan. Cover with water. Bring to a simmer.
Cook 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Let cool slightly.
Shred chicken using two forks or your hands.
Prepare chicken mixture. In a bowl, combine shredded chicken, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, finely diced celery, and minced red onion.
Season chicken mixture. Add salt and black pepper to taste. Stir well.
Prepare crostini. Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Arrange on a baking tray.
Toast crostini. Drizzle bread slices with olive oil. Bake at 180°C for 8-10 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Assemble crostini. Spoon a generous amount of chicken mixture onto each toasted baguette slice.
Garnish. Sprinkle fresh chopped parsley over assembled crostini. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Garlic Chicken Teppanyaki
recipes.visual_description: The Spicy Garlic Chicken Teppanyaki is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant and inviting single portion. Seared golden-brown chicken chunks, each with a slightly irregular yet appealing shape, are nestled alongside bright orange carrot batons. The ingredients are coated in a glossy, dark amber sauce, reflecting the pan-seared technique. A sprinkle of thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds adds fresh color and texture. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, allowing each component to be distinctly visible without overcrowding. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small white bowl of steamed Japanese rice and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its rich colors and appetizing sheen, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a side of steamed Japanese short-grain rice
Accompanied by a small bowl of miso soup
A small dish of pickled ginger (gari) can be offered alongside
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut chicken into 3-4 cm chunks.
Peel and cut carrots into 0.5 cm thick batons. Mince garlic. Mince fresh chili. Grate ginger. Thinly slice green onions for garnish.
In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar. Stir until sugar dissolves. Add minced garlic, minced chili, and grated ginger.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or teppanyaki griddle over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to hot pan. Do not overcrowd. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add carrots to the same pan. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return chicken to the pan with carrots. Pour sauce over chicken and carrots.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until sauce slightly thickens and coats chicken and vegetables.
Remove from heat. Stir in sesame oil.
Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Teppanyaki (griddle cooking for direct heat and even searing)

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents seared boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into generous 5cm chunks, coated in a rich, creamy sauce. The golden-brown chicken pieces are nestled amongst vibrant green wilted spinach and ruby-red sun-dried tomato halves. The sauce, a harmonious blend of cream and Parmesan, gently clings to all components, showcasing a velvety texture. Garnished with fresh chopped Italian parsley, the dish offers a delightful contrast of colors and textures. It is served in a clean, white porcelain dinner plate on a simple wooden table, accompanied by classic Italian flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting, rustic elegance. A single portion is thoughtfully arranged with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Serve alongside a simple green salad.
Serve over pasta, such as tagliatelle or penne.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut each thigh into 2-3 large chunks (approx. 5cm pieces). Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and sliced sun-dried tomatoes to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in heavy cream and dried oregano. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until spinach is wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Return cooked chicken pieces to the pan. Toss to coat them in the creamy sauce. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage and Chicken Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of Cabbage and Chicken Slaw is mounded casually on a simple, round ceramic plate. The finely shredded green and purple cabbage, vibrant orange carrots, and creamy white dressing are prominent. Small, irregular chunks of cooked chicken are visible throughout the slaw, nestled among the vegetables. Thinly sliced green onions are sprinkled on top, adding a pop of fresh green. The components are naturally mixed, showing a wholesome, comforting texture. The plate rests on a well-worn wooden dining table. A simple, folded cotton napkin in a neutral color is casually placed beside the plate. Warm, diffused lighting, as if from an overhead kitchen fixture, creates a cozy, inviting atmosphere. The background is slightly out of focus, showing glimpses of a lived-in family kitchen, like a salt and pepper shaker. The overall presentation is homely and unpretentious.
instructions: Cook chicken breast until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Shred or dice into small chunks. Set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, combine shredded cabbage and shredded carrots.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, granulated sugar, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the cabbage and carrot mixture. Toss well to coat all vegetables evenly.
Add the shredded chicken and thinly sliced green onions to the bowl.
Gently toss all ingredients together until well combined.
Cover the bowl and chill the slaw in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving. This allows flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Roulade, Onion Soubise, Brioche Toast, Cured Egg Yolk
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated sharing platter presents three to four thick, perfectly seared chicken roulade medallions, each displaying a tight, even spiral of tender chicken and delicate stuffing. Each medallion is artfully placed alongside a small, elegant quenelle or swoosh of creamy, pale golden caramelized onion soubise. Interspersed are small, crisp squares of golden-brown toasted brioche. The roulade medallions are delicately grated with vibrant orange cured egg yolk, adding a pop of color and rich umami. A few tiny, fresh thyme leaves are meticulously placed as a precise garnish, enhancing color and aroma. The composition is organic and flowing, with generous negative space on a minimalist, matte black or pristine white designer porcelain platter. The platter rests on a sleek, grey-veined white Carrara marble surface. A crisp, white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, is positioned discreetly to the side. Dramatic, focused professional lighting creates subtle shadows that emphasize texture and depth, with an ultra-minimalist, dark background to draw full attention to the food.
instructions: Begin curing egg yolks: Mix 50g salt and 50g sugar. Create four small depressions in the mixture. Place one egg yolk in each depression. Cover yolks completely with remaining salt-sugar mixture. Refrigerate for 48 hours. Rinse yolks gently under cold water. Pat dry. Dehydrate in a low oven (60°C) for 2-3 hours until firm and grateable.

Prepare caramelized onion soubise: Slice onions thinly. Melt 25g butter in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft, stirring occasionally. Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook 2 minutes. Deglaze with chicken stock. Simmer until liquid reduces slightly. Remove thyme. Transfer onions to a blender. Add heavy cream. Blend until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Keep warm.

Prepare chicken roulade: Pat chicken breasts dry. Place each breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound gently with a meat mallet to an even 0.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper. Spread a thin layer of caramelized onion soubise over each chicken breast. Roll each breast tightly into a cylinder. Secure with butcher's twine.

Cook chicken roulade: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 25g butter in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear roulades on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Rest for 5 minutes. Remove twine.
Prepare brioche toast: Cut brioche slices into small, neat squares or rectangles. Toast in a dry pan or under a broiler until golden and crisp. Alternatively, brush lightly with butter and toast.

Assemble dish: Slice chicken roulades into 2 cm thick medallions. Arrange 2-3 medallions per person on a minimalist sharing platter. Place small, elegant quenelles or swooshes of warm onion soubise beside the chicken. Scatter toasted brioche squares around the plate. Grate a generous amount of cured egg yolk over the chicken roulade medallions. Garnish with a few tiny, fresh thyme leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Chorizo Rice
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Spanish Chicken and Chorizo Rice dish is centrally plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rice, cooked to a tender but not mushy consistency, forms a shallow, even layer, showcasing its rich golden-orange hue from saffron and paprika. Interspersed throughout are generous, irregular chunks of seared chicken, displaying a golden-brown crust, and thick, browned medallions of chorizo sausage, their edges slightly crisped. Bright red bell pepper cubes and golden corn kernels add bursts of color and texture, evenly distributed. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped green parsley provides a final vibrant contrast. The dish is presented with moderate negative space on the plate, allowing each element to be clearly seen without overcrowding. A crisp, simple side salad of mixed greens, lightly dressed, sits in a small, elegant white bowl beside the main plate. A quartered fresh lemon wedge is placed beside the rice for serving. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table surface. A grey linen napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the dish's textures and colors. A rustic, dark-glazed ceramic serving bowl is visible in the soft-focus background, subtly hinting at a shared dining experience without distracting from the individual portion. Traditional flatware is placed beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet or paella pan for family-style dining.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up the flavorful juices.
Accompany with a dry white wine or sangria.
instructions: Prepare ingredients. Dice chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Slice chorizo into 1 cm thick rounds. Dice onion into small cubes. Dice red bell pepper into 1.5 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or paella pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add chorizo slices to the same pan. Cook until browned and crisp. Remove chorizo. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Arborio rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in canned diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-18 minutes, or until rice is almost tender and liquid is mostly absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Stir in frozen corn kernels and cooked chorizo. Cook uncovered for another 5 minutes, or until rice is fully cooked and liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Garnish the dish with chopped parsley. Serve with lemon wedges and a side of mixed salad greens.
notes: The chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C for safety.
Adjust liquid if rice seems too dry or wet during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Fricassée with Creamy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown chicken thigh, skin crispy and glistening, rests on a generous mound of creamy, rustic mashed potatoes. The chicken is a deep golden hue, indicating perfect searing. Around the base of the chicken and nestled into the potatoes are sautéed cremini mushroom halves, their earthy brown caps contrasting with the pale potatoes. A rich, velvety cream sauce, light beige in color, pools around the chicken and potatoes, catching light. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, adding a pop of color. The presentation is clean and professional on a round white porcelain plate. The plate sits on a simple wooden table. A cotton napkin and standard flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (Yukon Gold or similar), peeled, quartered

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat 30ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with white wine, scraping up browned bits from the bottom. Reduce by half, about 3 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken to the pan, skin-side up.
Cover pan and transfer to the preheated oven. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken bakes, cook potatoes. Place quartered potatoes in a pot, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Return drained potatoes to the hot pot. Add 20g butter. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
In a separate pan, melt remaining 20g butter over medium-high heat. Add halved mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Once chicken is cooked, remove from oven. Transfer chicken to a plate. Remove thyme sprigs from the pan sauce.
Stir heavy cream into the pan sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Adjust seasoning to taste.

To serve, spoon creamy mashed potatoes onto individual plates. Place a chicken thigh on top. Spoon generous amount of creamy mushroom sauce over chicken and potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Thigh with Caramelized Onion Purée and Crispy Shallots
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated, minimalist composition presented on a large, elegant, white ceramic sharing platter. The focal point is several irregular, golden-brown seared chicken thigh chunks, their crisp skin glistening, arranged organically. Adjacent to and interwoven with the chicken are elegant, flowing dollops of smooth, deep amber caramelized onion purée. Scattered artfully across the platter are delicate, golden-brown crispy shallot rings and vibrant, translucent pink pickled shallot crescents, providing textural and color contrast. A small, precise drizzle or pool of rich, dark mahogany chicken jus enhances the composition. A few finely chopped fresh chives are precisely sprinkled over the chicken. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing the artistry. The platter rests on a premium light-colored wooden table. Dramatic professional lighting creates distinct shadows, highlighting textures. The background is ultra-minimalist and unobtrusive.
instructions: Trim excess fat from chicken thighs. Season generously with salt and pepper. Place chicken in a vacuum-sealable bag. Seal, removing all air.
Cook chicken sous vide at 64°C for 90 minutes. Alternatively, pan-roast chicken, skin-side down, until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Remove chicken from bag. Pat skin very dry with paper towels. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, until deeply golden and crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear flesh side for 1-2 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken on a wire rack for 5 minutes. Cut into irregular 3-4 cm chunks.

For Caramelized Onion Purée: Peel and thinly slice yellow onions. Melt butter and 15ml olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 45-60 minutes until deeply caramelized and very soft. Do not brown. Blend onions until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For Crispy Shallots: Peel and thinly slice shallots into rings. Heat neutral oil in a small pot to 160°C. Fry shallot rings in batches until golden brown and crisp, about 2-3 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Season with a pinch of salt.

For Pickled Shallots: Peel and thinly slice remaining shallots into crescents. In a small saucepan, combine red wine vinegar, sugar, and 50ml water. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Pour hot liquid over sliced shallots. Let cool to room temperature. Drain before serving.

For Chicken Jus: Pour chicken stock into a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until liquid has reduced by two-thirds and is slightly thickened, about 15-20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate: Spoon generous dollops or create a flowing 'river' of caramelized onion purée across a sharing platter. Artfully arrange the seared chicken chunks on top of and around the purée. Scatter crispy shallot rings and pickled shallot crescents over the chicken and purée. Drizzle reduced chicken jus over the chicken and around the elements. Garnish with finely chopped fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Mushroom Chicken with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single seared chicken breast, cut into three thick, juicy medallions, exhibiting a golden-brown crust. It rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate, partially enrobed in a rich, creamy garlic mushroom sauce. The sauce, speckled with tender, earthy sliced cremini mushrooms and finely diced onion, coats the chicken invitingly. Alongside, a generous portion of roasted potato wedges, golden and slightly crisp on the exterior, with fluffy interiors, are neatly arranged. A sprinkle of vibrant fresh chopped parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of green. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, standard silver flatware, and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, under natural, even lighting for a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into 2cm thick wedges. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Flip halfway through.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Stir in dried thyme.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3-4 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Taste and adjust seasoning.
