Adjust hot sauce quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Arroz Mexicano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo con Arroz Mexicano is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous mound of vibrant, savory long-grain rice, infused with tomato and spices, forms the base. A golden-brown, pan-seared boneless chicken thigh, its surface slightly crisp, rests invitingly atop the rice. Scattered around the chicken and rice are bright yellow roasted corn kernels and deeply red, blistered cherry tomatoes, adding pops of color and texture. A sprinkle of crumbled white Cotija cheese and fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the dish, enhancing its visual appeal. A lime wedge sits beside the rice, ready for squeezing. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and a fork and knife, evoking a casual bistro ambiance with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Salsa roja or verde
Agua fresca
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, 3g cumin, and 3g chili powder.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion and red bell pepper. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Toast 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly golden.
Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, remaining 2g cumin, 2g chili powder, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice. Cover skillet tightly. Reduce heat to low. Cook 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

While rice cooks, preheat oven to 200°C. Toss corn kernels and whole cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 10-15 minutes until corn is slightly charred and tomatoes are blistered.
Remove skillet from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.

Fluff rice gently with a fork. Plate a single chicken thigh atop a generous portion of rice. Garnish with roasted corn, blistered cherry tomatoes, crumbled Cotija cheese, and fresh cilantro. Serve immediately with a lime wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best results, use a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet that can be tightly covered.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons nested in a shallow white porcelain bowl. Large, 3cm tender chunks of braised beef are distributed naturally throughout the pasta, coated in a thick, mahogany-colored tomato sauce. The sauce has a glossy sheen and visible small bits of diced carrots and onions. The dish is topped with a light, airy snowfall of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. A small pinch of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the center. The bowl sits on a rustic light-wood bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural daylight illuminates the textures of the shredded beef fibers and the silkiness of the pasta ribbons.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of full-bodied red wine like Chianti
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread for 'fare la scarpetta'
Present in wide-rimmed pasta bowls
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the same pot. Sauté 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, and herb sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Cook for 2.5 to 3 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Remove herb sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Boil salted water in a large pot. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 60ml of pasta water.
Toss pasta with the ragu and reserved water over low heat for 1 minute.
Serve immediately with grated cheese.
notes: Ensure the beef is seared deeply for maximum flavor development.
If the sauce is too thick, add more pasta water during the finishing stage.
Chuck roast or shin are the best cuts for this long-braising method.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Duck Breast with Daikon Nimono and Umami Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Seared Duck Breast with Daikon Nimono and Umami Glaze is presented on a minimalist, round, matte white ceramic plate. A single, thick, translucent white daikon round, gently simmered to tenderness, forms the base. Two to three thick, unsliced medallions of seared duck breast, displaying a rich, amber-brown, crispy skin and tender, rosy interior, are elegantly arranged beside the daikon. A glossy, dark amber umami glaze is artfully drizzled in an organic sweep across the plate, catching the light. A few delicate, almost translucent, pale green wakame crisps are precisely placed near the duck, adding a textural contrast. A small cluster of vibrant green micro shiso leaves or finely chopped chives provides a fresh, precise accent. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity of the plating. The entire plate is centered on a polished white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Professional, dramatic lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing the depth and texture of the dish. A set of elegant, dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the plate, completing the authentic Japanese fine-dining aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a standalone main course.
Accompany with a small bowl of steamed white rice on the side.
Offer a delicate clear soup (osuimono) as a preceding course.

ingredients.name: Micro shiso leaves or chives (for garnish)

instructions: Prepare Dashi: Combine 1.5 litres water and kombu in a pot. Heat gently, remove kombu just before boiling. Add katsuobushi, simmer 30 seconds. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Reserve dashi.
Prepare Daikon: Peel daikon. Cut into 2 cm thick rounds. Blanch daikon in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain well.

Simmer Daikon: In a separate pot, combine blanched daikon, 300ml dashi, 50ml soy sauce, 50ml mirin, and 10g sugar. Bring to a simmer. Cook 20-25 minutes until daikon is tender and translucent. Keep warm.

Prepare Wakame Crisp: Rehydrate wakame in cold water for 5 minutes. Squeeze out excess water thoroughly. Pat very dry with paper towels. Heat neutral oil to 170°C in a small pot. Fry wakame in small batches for 10-15 seconds until crisp. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
Prepare Duck: Score duck skin in a crosshatch pattern, without cutting into the meat. Season duck breasts generously with salt and pepper.

Sear Duck: Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, dry oven-safe pan. Heat pan over medium-low heat. Render fat slowly for 10-12 minutes until skin is golden brown and crisp. Pour off excess fat.

Finish Duck: Flip duck breasts. Cook meat-side down for 3-4 minutes. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Cook for 5-7 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest duck breasts on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Make Glaze: In a small saucepan, combine remaining dashi (approx. 1.2 litres), 50ml soy sauce, 50ml mirin, sake, and 5g sugar. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until glaze is thickened and syrupy. Skim any foam.

Plate Dish: Place one daikon round centrally on each plate. Slice rested duck breast into thick medallions (2-3 per person). Arrange duck medallions artfully beside or slightly over the daikon. Drizzle the reduced dashi glaze around the duck and daikon. Garnish with a few delicate wakame crisps and micro shiso leaves or finely chopped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the daikon is cooked until very tender but still holds its shape. The blanching step helps remove any raw bitterness.
Rendering the duck fat slowly is crucial for achieving a perfectly crispy skin. Do not rush this step.
The dashi glaze should be reduced to a consistency that coats the back of a spoon, not too thick, not too thin.
traditional_techniques: Precise knife work (for daikon and duck)

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Shiitake Dashi Consommé with Edamame & Wakame
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is presented in a wide, shallow, matte white bone china bowl. At the center, a precise, small mound of finely minced, dark brown shiitake 'caviar' rests, its texture subtly glistening. Around it, two to three vibrant green dots of smooth edamame cream are artfully piped, creating a soft, organic curve. Adjacent to these, one or two delicate, translucent, and slightly curled wakame crisps stand upright, providing an ethereal textural contrast. A crystal-clear, amber dashi consommé is gently poured around the elements, creating abundant negative space and a sense of lightness. The surface of the consommé is dotted with a few drops of bright green shiso oil, adding a final aromatic and visual accent. The overall composition is minimalist, elegant, and balanced, emphasizing purity of form and color. The bowl rests on a polished dark wood table, with a pristine white linen napkin folded precisely to the side. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's refined simplicity.
instructions: Wipe konbu with damp cloth. Do not wash.
Combine konbu and 1 litre cold water in pot. Bring slowly to 60°C. Hold 10 minutes.
Remove konbu. Increase heat. Just before boiling, add katsuobushi.
Remove from heat immediately. Let katsuobushi sink, about 1 minute.
Strain dashi through fine mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Do not press.
Season dashi with 5ml light soy sauce, 5ml mirin, and pinch of salt. Keep warm.
Clean shiitake. Remove stems. Finely mince caps into uniform 'caviar' size.
Heat 5ml neutral oil in small pan over medium heat.
Add minced shiitake. Sauté until tender and slightly caramelized, about 5 minutes.
Season with 2ml light soy sauce and 2ml mirin. Set aside.
Bring water to boil. Add edamame. Blanch 2 minutes.
Drain edamame. Transfer to ice water bath. Cool immediately.
Drain edamame. Remove any remaining skins. Blend edamame with 30ml vegetable stock or dashi until very smooth.
Pass mixture through fine mesh sieve to remove any fibrous bits. Season with salt.
Transfer to small squeeze bottle or piping bag.
Hydrate dried wakame in cold water 5 minutes. Drain wakame. Squeeze out excess water. Pat very dry with paper towels.
Heat 200ml neutral oil to 170°C in small pot.
Carefully fry small pieces of wakame until crisp, about 10-15 seconds. They will puff up.
Remove with slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Lightly salt.
Blanch shiso leaves 10 seconds in boiling water. Immediately transfer to ice bath.
Drain shiso. Squeeze out all water. Combine shiso and 50ml neutral oil in small blender. Blend until very smooth.
Strain oil through fine mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth or coffee filter for clear oil.
Place small amount of shiitake 'caviar' in center of each shallow bowl.
Pipe 2-3 small dots or a delicate swoosh of edamame cream around the shiitake.
Carefully place 1-2 wakame crisps next to the shiitake.
Gently pour warm dashi consommé around the arranged elements.
Finish with a few drops of shiso oil around the consommé.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang Chicken & Kimchi Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Korean Kimchi Fried Rice is centrally mounded on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rice, infused with the rich red hue of kimchi and gochujang, has visible chunks of sautéed kimchi and golden grains. On top of the rice, three to four substantial, irregular chunks of pan-seared gochujang chicken, approximately 3 cm, are artfully placed, showcasing their caramelized, deep red-brown exterior. A perfectly fried sunny-side up egg with a glistening, runny yolk crowns the dish. The plate is garnished with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced green onion batons for freshness and contrast. The setting features a simple wooden table, a grey cotton napkin, and a pair of traditional Korean metal chopsticks and a spoon beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of danmuji (yellow pickled radish) for a refreshing counterpoint.
Accompany with a simple clear soup like Kongnamul Guk (soybean sprout soup) or Doenjang Jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew).
Eat with traditional Korean metal chopsticks and a metal spoon.
instructions: Prepare chicken marinade. In a bowl, combine chicken chunks, 30 g gochujang, 15 ml soy sauce, 5 ml sesame oil, 10 g minced garlic, and all grated ginger. Mix well. Marinate chicken for at least 30 minutes.
Cook rice according to package instructions if not already cooked. Set aside.

Sear chicken. Heat 15 ml cooking oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken chunks in a single layer. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.

Prepare kimchi fried rice base. Add remaining 15 ml cooking oil to the same pan. Add chopped kimchi and remaining 5 g minced garlic. Stir-fry for 3 minutes. Add kimchi juice and gochugaru (if using). Stir-fry for another 2 minutes.
Add cooked rice. Add cooked short-grain rice to the pan with kimchi. Break up any clumps. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes, ensuring rice is well coated and heated through.

Combine and finish. Return seared chicken chunks to the pan with the rice. Add remaining 30 g gochujang, 15 ml soy sauce, and 10 ml sesame oil. Toss everything together until well combined and heated through.
Fry eggs. In a separate small pan, fry 4 sunny-side up eggs to your desired doneness, ideally with a runny yolk.

Plate and serve. Divide kimchi fried rice among 4 individual white porcelain dinner plates. Arrange seared chicken chunks on top of the rice. Place one fried egg on each serving. Garnish generously with thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best fried rice texture, use day-old cooked rice.
traditional_techniques: Wok hei (achieved through high heat stir-frying for the fried rice)

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Cheeks with Taleggio Polenta, Green Peas, and Kidney Beans
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed with ample negative space. A generous, free-flowing pool of creamy, golden-yellow Taleggio polenta forms the base, its surface smooth and inviting. Nestled beside the polenta are two substantial, dark mahogany-brown braised beef cheek pieces, their surfaces glistening with richness and showing the tender, pull-apart texture. A glossy, dark brown reduction sauce, thick enough to cling, is generously spooned over the beef and partially over the polenta. Around the perimeter of the beef and polenta, a scattering of vibrant emerald green peas and deep reddish-brown kidney beans adds pops of contrasting color and texture. The peas are plump and round, the beans whole and distinct. A light sprinkle of freshly chopped bright green parsley provides a final touch of freshness and color. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cream-colored cotton napkin lies beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual, professional restaurant atmosphere. The portion is a single, refined individual serving.
instructions: Pat beef cheeks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef cheeks until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes. Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cover tightly.
Transfer pot to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F). Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from pot. Cover loosely with foil. Keep warm.

Strain braising liquid into a saucepan. Discard solids. Skim fat if necessary. Bring liquid to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce until slightly thickened to a saucy consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring water or milk to a simmer in a separate pot. Gradually whisk in polenta. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened and creamy.
Remove polenta from heat. Stir in butter and diced Taleggio cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt.
Briefly blanch green peas in boiling water for 1-2 minutes. Drain. Gently warm drained kidney beans.

Place a generous dollop of creamy Taleggio polenta on each plate. Arrange 1-2 substantial pieces of braised beef cheek beside the polenta. Spoon reduced braising sauce over beef and polenta. Scatter green peas and kidney beans around the dish. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Taleggio is a soft, pungent Italian cheese. Its creamy texture and mild, fruity tang complement the rich beef.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Rice and Cashew Kheer
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Indian Rice and Cashew Kheer is presented in a small, rustic ceramic bowl with an earthy glaze. The kheer is thick and luscious, showing soft, distinct rice grains suspended in a rich, pale ivory base. The surface is garnished with a scattering of lightly fried, golden-brown cashews, some whole, some halved, providing a textural contrast. A few delicate strands of deep orange saffron are visible, adding subtle color. The bowl sits on a well-used dark wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple, small metal Indian dessert spoon rests casually beside the bowl. Lighting is warm and inviting, evoking a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, perhaps a soft blur of a traditional Indian spice box, keeping the focus entirely on the comforting dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve Kheer warm or chilled as a dessert.
Often prepared for festivals, special occasions, or as a comforting family treat.
Can be enjoyed on its own or with a light flatbread like puri.
instructions: Rinse basmati rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Soak rice in 100 ml water for 30 minutes. Drain well.
Crush cardamom pods lightly to expose seeds.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add cashews to the pot. Fry until light golden brown. Remove cashews and set aside.
Pour milk into the same pot. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Add drained rice and crushed cardamom pods to the milk.
Simmer gently, stirring every few minutes, for 45-60 minutes.
Cook until rice is fully tender and the milk has thickened to a creamy consistency.
Stir in granulated sugar. Cook for another 5 minutes, stirring until sugar dissolves completely.
If using, dissolve saffron strands in a tablespoon of warm milk. Stir into the kheer.
Remove from heat. Discard cardamom pods.
Stir in most of the fried cashews. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve warm or chilled in individual dessert bowls, garnished with remaining cashews.
notes: Stirring frequently is crucial to prevent milk from sticking to the bottom and burning.
The kheer will thicken further as it cools. Adjust consistency with a little warm milk if serving chilled.
traditional_techniques: Slow simmering (dum cooking principle for rice)
Frying nuts in ghee for flavor and texture (similar to tadka technique)

recipes.recipe_name: Linguine with Garlic Shrimp and Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Linguine with Garlic Shrimp and Sun-Dried Tomatoes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden bistro table. The pasta is neatly swirled, forming a modest mound, lightly coated in a glistening, savory sauce. Pink, plump, whole shrimp are artfully arranged on top and around the pasta, showcasing their perfectly cooked texture. Julienne-cut sun-dried tomatoes, vibrant deep red, are distributed throughout the dish, adding pops of color. A generous sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top, providing a fresh contrast. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a crisp white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and standard European-style flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes in oil, drained and julienned

instructions: Cook linguine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta water before draining.
Pat shrimp dry. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add shrimp. Cook 1-2 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sun-dried tomatoes. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce by half.
Add chicken or vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.
Add cooked linguine to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat.
Return shrimp to the skillet. Add chopped fresh parsley. Toss gently to combine.
If needed, add reserved pasta water gradually to achieve desired sauce consistency. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with White Beans and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of braised chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two succulent, golden-brown braised chicken thighs are nestled amidst a rich, rustic stew of plump white cannellini beans and tender diced onions. The deep red, herb-infused tomato sauce coats the beans and chicken, creating a comforting visual. Vibrant green specks of fresh chopped parsley are sprinkled over the top, providing a fresh contrast. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, set against a subtle, casual restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
A light green salad with a simple vinaigrette.
A glass of dry white wine.
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine (if using) and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until liquid is reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, ensuring they are partially submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F).
Braise for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven. Stir in rinsed cannellini beans.
Return to oven and braise for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Discard rosemary, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Chicken thighs are ideal for braising as they remain moist and tender.
Adjust seasoning to taste after braising.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Risotto and Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy mushroom risotto occupies the center of a clean, white round dinner plate, flowing naturally. The risotto is a warm ivory color with visible specks of sautéed brown mushrooms. Nestled atop the risotto are two thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast medallions, their surfaces showing a rich, caramelized crust. Beside the chicken, a cluster of vibrant red roasted cherry tomatoes adds a pop of color and glossy texture. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge, placed invitingly to the side. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the elements. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately for best texture.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Toss cherry tomatoes with 15ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Roast in oven at 200°C for 10-15 minutes until softened. Set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil and 30g butter. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until translucent. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir 2 minutes until rice edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add 250ml warm chicken broth to the rice. Stir constantly until absorbed. Continue adding broth, 250ml at a time, stirring until absorbed before each addition. This process takes 20-25 minutes.
While risotto cooks, slice mushrooms. In a separate small pan, sauté mushrooms in 15g butter until tender and browned. Add sautéed mushrooms to the risotto during the final 10 minutes of cooking.
Risotto is done when creamy and al dente. Stir in remaining 15g butter, grated Parmesan cheese, and whole milk. Season with salt and pepper. Add a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.
Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions. Do not fan out slices.
Plate a portion of creamy mushroom risotto. Top with sliced chicken. Garnish with roasted cherry tomatoes, fresh chopped parsley, and a lemon wedge.
notes: For best results, always use warm chicken broth when adding to the risotto. This helps maintain the cooking temperature and ensures consistent absorption for a creamy texture.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (creaming the risotto with butter and cheese at the end)

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: The soup is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl, generously filled with a clear, golden chicken broth. Tender chunks of poached chicken breast, about 2-3 cm in size, are visible throughout. Fluffy white rice grains, fully cooked, are suspended in the broth. Diced carrots and celery, along with finely minced onion, add subtle color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley leaves garnishes the top, providing a vibrant contrast. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden kitchen table, alongside a simple cloth napkin and a standard metal spoon. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting steam rising from the hot soup.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread for dipping.
Offer a simple green salad as a side.
instructions: Dice the onion, carrots, and celery into small cubes, approximately 0.5 cm.
Cut chicken breast into 2-3 cm chunks. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) during cooking.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the white rice. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender.
Remove from heat. Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half into the soup. Reserve the rest for garnish.
Ladle soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: For richer flavor, use bone-in chicken thighs and remove bones after cooking.
Adjust liquid amount for desired soup consistency.
Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mozzarella Chicken Roulade with Beef & Pineapple Relish and Pan-Seared Salmon
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of Creamy Mozzarella Chicken Roulade with Beef & Pineapple Relish and Pan-Seared Salmon on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two to three thick-cut medallions of golden-brown seared chicken roulade are neatly arranged over a pool of luscious, off-white creamy mozzarella sauce. Beside the chicken, a vibrant mound of beef and pineapple relish showcases finely diced red tomatoes, yellow pineapple chunks, and browned ground beef, offering textural contrast. A perfectly pan-seared salmon fillet, with a slightly crisp, golden-brown exterior and flaky interior, rests adjacent to the chicken and relish. Garnishes of small, fresh green basil leaves are artfully placed for a pop of color. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting each component. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table surface in a modern bistro style. A folded white cotton napkin and a minimalist fork and knife are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.

ingredients.name: canned pineapple chunks, drained, finely diced
salmon fillets, skin on or off

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Place each between two sheets of cling film. Pound to 0.5 cm thickness using a meat mallet.
Season inside of each chicken breast with salt, pepper, chopped parsley, and basil.
Roll each chicken breast tightly into a cylinder. Secure with kitchen twine if needed.
Heat 30ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear roulades 3-4 minutes per side until golden.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Bake 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add beef mince. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Stir in diced pineapple, diced tomatoes, sugar, and vinegar. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cook 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid reduces and relish thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
In a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour to form a roux. Cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in cream and chicken stock. Cook, whisking constantly, until sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in shredded mozzarella until melted and smooth. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.
Pat salmon fillets dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon skin-side down (if applicable). Sear 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy.
Flip and cook 2-3 minutes more, until cooked through. Adjust cooking time for desired doneness.
Slice each chicken roulade into 2-3 thick medallions. Spoon a bed of creamy mozzarella sauce onto the center of each plate.
Arrange the chicken roulade medallions on top of the sauce. Place a generous spoonful of the beef & pineapple relish beside the chicken.
Carefully place one pan-seared salmon fillet on the other side of the chicken. Garnish with fresh basil leaves or parsley sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple & Sweet Potato Leather with Spiced Almond Crumble
recipes.visual_description: The finished dish presents a natural, organic composition of Fermented Apple & Sweet Potato Leather, arranged artfully on a cream-toned handcrafted ceramic plate. Several rustic, free-form strips of the deep amber-orange leather are gently overlapped, showcasing their smooth, pliable texture. A small, inviting pile of Spiced Almond Crumble rests alongside, its rough, golden-brown texture providing a pleasing contrast. The natural colors of the ingredients dominate, with earthy tones of sweet potato and cinnamon, and the lighter beige of the almonds. The plating is clean and minimalist, with generous negative space highlighting the inherent beauty of each component. The scene is set on a light reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin subtly placed. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its simple, wholesome elegance.

ingredients.name: Maple Syrup
ingredients.quantity: 75 ml (60 ml for leather, 15 ml for crumble)

ingredients.name: Ground Cinnamon
ingredients.quantity: 7.5 ml (5 ml for leather, 2.5 ml for crumble)

instructions: Ferment Apples: Grate apples, skin on. Place in clean jar. Add 0.5 teaspoon sea salt, 50 ml water. Mix well. Press down. Cover loosely. Ferment 2-3 days at room temperature until tangy. Strain liquid; reserve. Use apple pulp.
Prepare Sweet Potato: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pierce sweet potato. Roast 45-60 minutes until very tender. Cool. Peel. Mash until smooth.
Make Leather Base: Combine mashed sweet potato, fermented apple pulp, 60 ml maple syrup, 5 ml vanilla, 5 ml cinnamon. Mix thoroughly until smooth.
Dehydrate Leather: Line dehydrator tray or baking sheet with parchment paper. Spread mixture thinly and evenly, 3 mm thick.
Dehydrate: Dehydrate at 50°C for 6-8 hours, or bake at 70-80°C with oven door slightly ajar, until pliable and no longer sticky.

Prepare Almond Crumble: Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread almonds on baking sheet. Toast 8-10 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Cool. Roughly chop toasted almonds. Combine chopped almonds with 15 ml maple syrup, 2.5 ml cinnamon. Mix well.
Assemble: Once leather is cool, peel from parchment. Cut into rustic strips or squares. Serve with spiced almond crumble.
notes: The strained liquid from apple fermentation can be used in salad dressings or beverages.
Sweet potato peels can be composted or repurposed for vegetable stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Reclaimed Chicken Bone Broth with Fermented Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of clear, golden chicken broth fills a handcrafted ceramic bowl in an earthy cream tone. Shredded chicken pieces rest at the bottom, visible through the translucent liquid. Thinly sliced, pale green fermented vegetable strands are gently arranged within the soup, adding a subtle textural contrast. A small, artful cluster of vibrant green fresh parsley leaves and finely sliced scallion greens floats on the surface, providing a fresh pop of color. The bowl sits on a light, natural-textured bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually draped beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the soup's warmth and clarity. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of out-of-focus green foliage from a potted plant.

ingredients.name: Fermented green vegetable pieces, thinly sliced

instructions: Combine chicken carcass, bones, water, onion peels, carrot peels, celery ends, garlic skins, ginger peel, bay leaves, peppercorns, and parsley stems in a large pot.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 4-6 hours. Skim foam as needed.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Season broth with salt.
Add chicken thighs to the strained broth. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove chicken thighs. Let cool slightly. Shred chicken meat into bite-sized pieces.
Return shredded chicken to broth.
Stir in fermented green vegetable brine.
Divide soup into bowls. Add thinly sliced fermented green vegetable pieces to each bowl.
Garnish with fresh parsley leaves and thinly sliced scallion greens.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken, Dauphinoise, Carrot Puree, Crispy Rice
recipes.visual_description: A meticulously composed, minimalist plate features a golden, crispy-skinned pan-seared chicken breast as the focal point, resting elegantly on a small, golden-brown crispy rice cake. Beside it, a perfectly formed, individual Dauphinoise potato, showcasing delicate layers and a gratinéed golden-brown top. A vibrant, silky smooth carrot puree forms an artistic swoosh across the plate, providing a striking color contrast. A few glossy, slow-roasted cherry tomatoes, slightly blistered, are artfully placed to add bursts of ruby red. The chicken, cooked to tender perfection, reveals its juicy interior where a thick medallion is presented. The plate is pristine white bone china, offering abundant negative space that emphasizes the architectural precision of each element. A delicate sprig of fresh chervil or a sprinkle of microgreens provides a final touch of verdant freshness. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and creating an ultra-sophisticated, clean aesthetic. The setting is a premium grey veined marble surface with a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, signifying luxury and refined dining.

ingredients.name: Large potatoes (e.g., Russet or Maris Piper)

instructions: Prepare Dauphinoise: Preheat oven to 160°C. Thinly slice potatoes (1-2mm) using a mandoline. Heat cream with minced garlic, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Arrange potato slices in buttered individual gratin dishes or a small baking dish. Pour hot cream over potatoes. Bake 45-55 minutes until tender and golden. Top with grated Parmesan for last 10 minutes. Let rest 10 minutes before serving.

Prepare Crispy Rice Cakes: Cook Arborio rice according to package directions until tender but slightly al dente. Drain well. Press cooked rice into a thin, compact layer on a parchment-lined tray. Chill thoroughly for at least 30 minutes. Cut into small, neat rectangles or circles (approx. 4x4cm). Pan-fry in a thin layer of olive oil until golden and crisp on both sides. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Carrot Puree: Peel and chop carrots. Steam or boil until very tender. Drain well. Blend carrots with 15g butter, a splash of hot chicken stock, salt, and pepper until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Keep warm.

Prepare Slow-Roasted Cherry Tomatoes: Toss cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in the same 160°C oven for 15-20 minutes until slightly softened and blistered. Do not overcook.

Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken breasts very dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15g butter and 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Flip chicken. Add thyme sprigs. Continue cooking 8-10 minutes, basting with pan juices, until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from pan. Rest 5 minutes before slicing into thick medallions or serving whole.

Assemble Plates: Place a crispy rice cake on each plate. Top with a thick slice or whole chicken breast. Arrange a portion of Dauphinoise next to the chicken. Create a swoosh or quenelle of carrot puree. Scatter a few slow-roasted cherry tomatoes. Drizzle with pan juices from chicken. Garnish with microgreens or chervil. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken breasts are of uniform thickness for even cooking. Pound gently if needed.
For ultra-smooth carrot puree, blend hot and pass through a fine-mesh sieve.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Beef Liver Stew
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of hearty Chicken and Beef Liver Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew features robust, browned chicken chunks and beef liver chunks, approximately 3-4 cm. Diced carrots and onions, cut into 1 cm cubes, are interspersed. Bright green broccoli florets and creamy white cauliflower florets, broken into 2-3 cm pieces, add color and texture. Cooked buckwheat and barley are visible, forming a comforting base. The stew is topped with thinly sliced green onion. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, off-white ceramic plate and a casually folded linen napkin are nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, evoking a homely family meal.
instructions: Prepare ingredients: Cut 500g chicken and 250g beef liver into 3-4 cm chunks. Dice 1 large onion and 2 medium carrots into 1 cm cubes. Mince 4 cloves garlic. Break 200g broccoli and 200g cauliflower into 2-3 cm florets. Drain and rinse 400g canned kidney beans. Thinly slice 2 stalks green onion for garnish.

Sear meats: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Sear liver chunks until browned on all sides. Remove liver from pot.
Sauté aromatics: Add diced onion and carrot to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and 1 tsp dried chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Simmer chicken: Return chicken to the pot. Pour in 750ml water or broth. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Add grains, vegetables, and liver: Add 100g buckwheat groats, 100g barley, broccoli florets, cauliflower florets, and kidney beans to the pot. Stir well. Add seared liver chunks.
Continue cooking: Cover and cook for another 15-20 minutes, or until grains are tender and vegetables are cooked through. Add more water or broth if needed for desired consistency.
Season and serve: Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. Ladle hot stew into deep bowls. Garnish with thinly sliced green onion.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of tender chicken thigh pieces, cut into large, irregular chunks, rests in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce on a white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken shows hints of its golden-brown seared crust. The sauce is rich and slightly chunky, flecked with finely diced aromatics. Fresh, roughly torn basil leaves are scattered over the dish, adding contrasting green. A light drizzle of extra virgin olive oil provides a subtle sheen. The plate sits on a simple wooden table. Beside it, a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. In the background, a small bowl of grated Pecorino Romano cheese and crusty Italian bread. Natural, even light highlights the dish against a clean background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese at the table.
Can be served alongside pasta, polenta, or roasted potatoes.

ingredients.name: Parmesan or Pecorino Romano cheese, grated

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until skin is golden and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly reduced, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring sauce to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Remove chicken from the pot. Carefully remove skin and bones. Cut chicken meat into large, irregular chunks. Set aside.
Increase heat to medium. Simmer sauce, uncovered, for 5-10 minutes, or until slightly thickened. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Stir most of the fresh basil into the sauce. Return chicken chunks to the sauce. Gently toss to coat.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil. Offer grated cheese and crusty bread on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Saffron Risotto, Roasted Cherry Tomato, Carrot Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated portion on a large, round bone china plate with a subtle grey rim. A generous, fluid quenelle of vibrant saffron risotto anchors the composition slightly off-center. Perched gracefully atop the risotto is a thick, golden-skinned pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a tender finish. A delicate, silken swirl of bright orange carrot and ginger puree artfully sweeps across a portion of the plate, providing a contrasting color and texture. Scattered with precision around the chicken and risotto are a few glossy, slow-roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly burst. A single, ethereal, golden potato crisp stands upright, providing architectural height and a whisper of texture. The abundant white space of the plate emphasizes the minimalist design. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle is placed beside the plate on a premium light grey marble surface.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Slice potatoes paper-thin using a mandoline. Arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Lightly brush with olive oil and season with salt. Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, sliced garlic, and thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.

Steam or boil carrot chunks and ginger slices until very tender. Drain well. Transfer to a high-speed blender. Add a small knob of butter (10g) and a splash of hot chicken stock (50ml). Blend until perfectly smooth and silky. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Season with salt. Keep warm.

In a wide, heavy-bottomed pan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced shallots and cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add Arborio rice and toast for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent. Pour in white wine and stir until fully absorbed. Add a ladle of hot chicken stock, stir until absorbed. Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring frequently, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. After 10 minutes, dissolve saffron threads in a small amount of hot stock and add to the risotto. Continue adding stock for 15-18 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy. Remove from heat. Stir in remaining cold butter (50g) and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and incorporated. The risotto should be fluid and flowing. Adjust seasoning.

Pat chicken breasts very dry. Season skin generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp. Flip chicken. Transfer pan to preheated oven (180°C) and cook for another 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes before slicing.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic French Beef Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A crystal-clear, golden-amber beef consommé is presented in a pristine white porcelain soup bowl. Submerged within the transparent broth are several substantial, dark brown 4-5 cm braised beef cubes, their irregular, tender surfaces visible. Complementing the beef are small, precisely cut 1 cm diced vibrant orange carrots and pale green celery, maintaining their distinct shapes. A delicate scattering of finely chopped bright green chives and parsley floats on the consommé's surface, providing a fresh, aromatic accent. The bowl is centered on a simple, light wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the clarity of the broth and the rich, natural colors of the ingredients, set against a subtle, uncluttered modern bistro background.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.quantity: 100 g, white and light green parts

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Roast beef bones at 200°C for 20 minutes if using. Roughly chop 150g carrots, 100g celery, and 150g onion for the initial broth. Dice remaining 100g carrots and 100g celery into 1 cm cubes for garnish.
In a large pot, sear beef cubes over high heat until well browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add roughly chopped carrots, celery, and onion to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add garlic, bay leaves, thyme, and peppercorns. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef and roasted bones (if using) to pot. Add cold water. Bring to a boil. Skim foam. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently 3-4 hours, until beef is very tender. Skim surface periodically.
Carefully strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids. Reserve cooked beef cubes. Let broth cool. Refrigerate until fat solidifies. Skim fat.
In a bowl, combine lean ground beef, egg whites, tomato paste, and ice cubes. Mix well.
Place defatted broth in a clean pot. Add clarification mixture. Stir constantly over medium heat until raft forms on top. Stop stirring. Create a small hole in raft for steam to escape.
Reduce heat to very low. Simmer gently 30-45 minutes. Do not disturb raft.
Carefully ladle clarified consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with damp cheesecloth. Do not press raft. Discard raft. Season consommé with salt.
Blanch 1 cm diced carrots and celery in boiling salted water until tender-crisp. Drain.
Gently reheat consommé. Place several braised beef cubes and blanched diced vegetables in each serving bowl. Ladle hot consommé over. Garnish with chopped chives and parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Tomato Rice is presented in a shallow, wide ceramic bowl. A golden-brown, seared bone-in chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is nestled prominently on top of a vibrant orange-red bed of short-grain rice. The rice is tender, studded with soft, diced tomato pieces and flecks of minced garlic and onion. The grains are separate yet moist. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is generously scattered over the chicken and rice, providing a contrasting color and fresh aroma. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests on the rim of the bowl, ready to be squeezed. The overall composition is rustic yet refined, showcasing the rich colors and textures of the dish. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pan if serving family style, or in individual wide, shallow bowls.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the flavorful juices.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide, shallow pan or paella pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crisp. Flip and sear for another 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Stir in diced tomatoes and saffron threads. Cook for 5 minutes, mashing tomatoes slightly, to form a sofrito.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 1-2 minutes to coat rice grains evenly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan loosely or leave uncovered if using a traditional paella pan. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively.
Remove from heat. Cover tightly with foil or a lid. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Avoid stirring the rice too much once the broth is added to allow the rice to cook evenly and prevent it from becoming sticky.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Chorizo Paella
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of Chicken and Chorizo Paella is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rice, vibrant golden-yellow from saffron, forms a cohesive base with visible, distinct grains. Interspersed are tender, browned 3 cm chicken chunks and rich red 1 cm chorizo rounds. Diced red bell pepper and finely diced onion pieces add color and texture. Fresh green chopped parsley is sprinkled generously over the top, and a bright yellow lemon wedge rests at the plate's edge. The presentation is organized but natural. The background features a rustic wooden table, with simple, elegant flatware and a small ceramic bowl for discarded lemon rind, all under soft, natural lighting, creating an authentic Spanish bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, offering extra lemon wedges for squeezing.
Traditionally enjoyed communally from a large paella pan, but individual portions are common in restaurant settings.
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine or sangria.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: 0.5 g, steeped in 60 ml hot water

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add chorizo to the pan. Cook until slightly crispy and fat is rendered. Remove chorizo. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat rice in the tomato mixture. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan. Pour in hot chicken stock and saffron water. Stir gently once.
Bring to a simmer. Distribute ingredients evenly. Do not stir further.
Cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is al dente.
Reduce heat to low. Continue cooking for 5-7 minutes, listening for a crackling sound to form the socarrat.
Remove from heat. Arrange cooked chorizo on top of the paella.
Cover pan with foil or a lid. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Braised Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening, rests on a bed of fork-tender, rustic potato chunks on an everyday, off-white ceramic plate. A rich, dark reddish-brown sauce pools around them, reflecting the warm kitchen light. The chicken skin is crisp; potatoes are irregular, homely chunks. Beside the main dish, a small, vibrant mound of fresh mixed salad greens is casually arranged. Interspersed within are bright red halved cherry tomatoes and thin, pale apple slices, lightly dressed. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife, and a casually folded linen napkin, complete the homely scene. Soft, inviting kitchen lighting evokes a comfortable family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family-style, allowing guests to serve themselves from a central pot or platter.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the rich sauce.
Pair with a glass of the red wine used in the braise.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deep golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine and brewed coffee. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid reduces by half, about 5-7 minutes.
Add chicken stock to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in liquid.
Cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Add potato chunks around the chicken in the pot.

Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Potatoes should be fork-tender.

While chicken braises, prepare the salad. Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice the apple. In a small bowl, whisk together 15 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, and Dijon mustard for vinaigrette. Season with salt and pepper.
Toss salad greens with halved cherry tomatoes and thinly sliced apple. Dress with vinaigrette just before serving.
Carefully remove pot from oven. Transfer chicken and potatoes to a serving platter. If sauce is too thin, simmer on stovetop briefly to reduce. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve chicken and potatoes with a generous spoon of sauce. Serve fresh salad on the side. Garnish chicken with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For extra flavor, you can brown 100g of diced bacon or pancetta before searing the chicken. Remove bacon, then proceed with chicken searing. Add bacon back with chicken stock.
The braising liquid can be strained and puréed with some of the cooked vegetables for a thicker, smoother sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Bourguignon
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef Bourguignon is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The centerpiece features four to five large, succulent chunks of braised beef chuck, glistening with a deep, mahogany-colored glossy sauce. Interspersed among the meat are whole, tender pearl onions and golden-brown sautéed button mushroom halves. Bright orange carrot rounds provide a pop of color. The stew is finished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley. The sauce has a rich, velvety consistency, pooling slightly around the base. The dish sits on a dark wood bistro table. A side of crusty baguette slices and a simple silver spoon rest on a white cotton napkin nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty French baguette
Pair with a glass of Pinot Noir or red Burgundy
Traditionally served with buttery mashed potatoes or boiled potatoes
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Sauté bacon lardons in a heavy pot until crisp. Remove and set aside.
Sear beef chunks in the bacon fat over high heat until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add sliced carrots and onions to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef and bacon to the pot. Add beef stock and bouquet garni.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 2.5 hours until meat is tender.
Sauté mushrooms and pearl onions in butter in a separate pan until golden.
Add mushrooms and pearl onions to the stew. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove bouquet garni. Season to taste.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the beef is patted dry before searing to achieve a deep crust.
Use a high-quality dry red wine for the most authentic flavor profile.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Garlic Shrimp Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The Lemon Garlic Shrimp Pasta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, embodying a simple restaurant-style elegance. Al dente linguine is twirled naturally and centrally, forming a golden-yellow nest. Plump, seared pink shrimp, left whole, are arranged artfully atop and around the pasta, showcasing their vibrant color. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes are scattered throughout, adding pops of color and juicy texture. Dark green, wilted spinach leaves are interspersed, providing depth. A light drizzle of golden garlic-lemon sauce glistens over the dish. The pasta is generously garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley and fine lemon zest, adding freshness and aroma. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, set on a simple light wooden table. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin rest beside the plate, under natural, even lighting, against a softly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with grated Parmesan cheese
Offer crusty bread for dipping the sauce
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add linguine pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml of the pasta water. Drain pasta.
Pat shrimp dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet or pan over medium-high heat. Add thinly sliced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Add seasoned shrimp to the skillet in a single layer. Sear for 1-2 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Remove shrimp from skillet. Set aside.

Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add halved cherry tomatoes. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. If using, deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce the liquid by half.
Add fresh spinach to the skillet. Cook for 1-2 minutes until wilted.

Return the cooked shrimp to the skillet. Add the drained pasta, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and butter. Add 125ml of the reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously to combine, adding more pasta water as needed to achieve a silky sauce consistency.
Stir in the chopped fresh parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Coffee-Tomato Jus and Savory Cottage Cheese Fritters
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. A perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, its golden-brown crust contrasting with the pale interior, is the focal point. Alongside, two golden-hued, slightly crisp savory cottage cheese fritters are neatly arranged. A small, vibrant dollop of deep crimson caramelized red onion jam sits near the chicken, providing a rich color accent. Scattered around are a few plump, roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly burst and revealing juicy interiors. A rich, glossy coffee-tomato jus is artfully drizzled over the chicken and around the plate, its deep brown color adding depth. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley, providing a final touch of color and freshness. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard flatware beside the plate, all bathed in natural, even lighting within a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Prepare Red Onion Jam: Thinly slice red onion. Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add red onion. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes until very soft. Add sugar and red wine vinegar. Cook for another 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until caramelized and jam-like. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Prepare Cottage Cheese Fritters: In a bowl, combine cottage cheese, egg, 30g flour, 10g chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Drop spoonfuls of the mixture (about 2 tablespoons each) into the hot oil. Flatten slightly with the back of a spoon. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towel. Keep warm.

Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board.

Prepare Coffee-Tomato Jus: Return the same skillet to medium heat. Add finely diced yellow onion and minced garlic. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Deglaze with brewed coffee, scraping up any browned bits. Add chicken stock and any juices from the resting chicken. Bring to a simmer. In a small bowl, whisk remaining 30g flour with 30ml cold water to create a slurry. Gradually whisk slurry into simmering sauce until desired consistency is reached. Stir in 15g butter. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Roast Cherry Tomatoes: While chicken roasts, toss cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a small baking sheet. Roast in the same oven as chicken for 10-12 minutes, until softened and slightly burst.

Assemble and Serve: Slice chicken breasts diagonally into two pieces if desired, or serve whole. Place one chicken piece or whole breast on each plate. Arrange 2-3 cottage cheese fritters beside the chicken. Add a small dollop of red onion jam and a few roasted cherry tomatoes. Drizzle generously with coffee-tomato jus. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Lamb & Lobster Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Lamb & Lobster Tagliatelle rests on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente tagliatelle forms a gentle swirl at the plate's center, glistening with a light, glossy garlic-herb butter sauce. Nestled within and beside the pasta are two pan-seared lamb medallions, each displaying a golden-brown crust and a tender, slightly pink interior. Alongside, generous chunks of succulent, pearly-white lobster meat are interspersed, catching the light. The dish is vibrant with flecks of bright green chopped parsley and chives, and delicate strands of yellow lemon zest are scattered throughout. The composition is balanced, leaving appropriate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and classic silver cutlery, illuminated by natural, even light, creating a professional yet approachable bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for pasta.
Prepare lobster: Blanch lobster tails in boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Remove, cool slightly. Extract meat from shells. Cut lobster meat into 2-3 cm chunks.
Cook tagliatelle according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, pat lamb medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear lamb medallions for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness. Remove lamb from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the skillet. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Add cooked tagliatelle to the skillet. Toss to coat in the sauce. Add stock if using.
Add lobster chunks, chopped parsley, and chopped chives to the pasta. Toss gently to combine.
Squeeze in lemon juice and add lemon zest. Add 60-120ml reserved pasta water if needed to create a glossy sauce. Toss again.
Return seared lamb medallions to the skillet with the pasta. Briefly toss to warm through.
Serve immediately. Garnish with additional fresh herbs and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mushroom and Wild Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant serving of Creamy Mushroom and Wild Rice Soup is presented in a pristine white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The soup exhibits a rich, inviting light brown hue, showcasing visible, irregularly sliced sautéed mushrooms and dark, firm wild rice grains. The texture is a harmonious blend of creamy broth and distinct, chewy solids. A light, precise sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh chives garnishes the center. A clean white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl, holding a sleek silver soup spoon. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating an understated yet refined culinary scene.

ingredients.name: Unsweetened plant-based milk (e.g., oat or cashew)

instructions: Rinse wild rice blend under cold water.
Cook wild rice blend according to package directions. Use vegetable broth or water. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, thyme sprigs, and rosemary sprig. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pot. Increase heat slightly. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 8-10 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring soup to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Remove thyme and rosemary sprigs from the soup.
Ladle about 500 ml of the soup (mostly broth and some mushrooms) into a blender. Add plant-based milk. Blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour blended soup back into the pot. Stir well to combine.
Add cooked wild rice to the soup. Heat gently until warmed through. Do not boil after adding milk.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Roasted Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Chicken and Roasted Tomato Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a refined casual dining aesthetic. The risotto is free-flowing, not mounded, displaying its rich, unctuous texture. Golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, cut into approximately 2cm pieces, are nestled throughout the creamy Arborio rice. Vibrant roasted cherry tomato halves, with their slightly caramelized skins, add pops of deep red. The dish is garnished with fresh, bright green basil leaves scattered artfully on top and a generous sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan cheese. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with contrasting textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork and spoon, and a neatly folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the food's inviting appearance, set against a blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the creamy sauce.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine like Pinot Grigio.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until slightly softened and caramelized. Set aside.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, deep pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken, let rest 5 minutes. Cut into 2cm chunks.

Finely dice the yellow onion. Mince the garlic cloves. In the same pan, melt 30g butter with a splash of olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the grains. Ensure all grains are coated and slightly translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.

Add one ladle of hot chicken broth to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Stir in the cooked chicken chunks, roasted cherry tomatoes, remaining 30g butter, and 100g grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute. This is 'mantecatura' to create a creamy texture.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper. If too thick, add a splash more hot broth. The risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls or plates. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and additional shaved Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken broth is hot when adding to the risotto to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is crucial for releasing starch from the rice, creating a creamy risotto.
Risotto should be served immediately as it continues to cook and thicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Frittata di Verdure
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown Frittata di Verdure wedge is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The frittata features a slightly puffed, golden top with visible specks of vibrant green herbs and colorful, tender-crisp vegetables, including red bell pepper, green zucchini, yellow onion, and halved cherry tomatoes. The interior reveals a fluffy, tender texture. A small fresh basil leaf garnishes the top. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, capturing a modern bistro aesthetic. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable presentation with moderate negative space. Traditional flatware accompanies the dish, emphasizing an authentic Italian dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Enjoy as a light lunch or a casual dinner.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Dice zucchini, red bell pepper, and yellow onion into small cubes. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Heat olive oil in a 24 cm oven-safe non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion, bell pepper, and zucchini to the skillet. Sauté 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add halved cherry tomatoes. Cook 2 minutes more.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs with salt and black pepper.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese, chopped basil, and chopped parsley into the egg mixture.
Pour egg mixture evenly over sautéed vegetables in the skillet.
Cook on stovetop 5-7 minutes until edges are set and bottom is golden.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake 15-20 minutes until frittata is puffed and golden brown, and eggs are fully set.
Remove from oven. Let cool 5 minutes. Slide frittata onto a cutting board.
Cut into 4 equal wedges. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Feel free to substitute other seasonal vegetables like asparagus, spinach, or mushrooms.
Pecorino Romano can be used instead of Parmesan for a sharper flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Roulade, Smoked Gouda, Crispy Tortilla, Onion Jus
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented with sophisticated minimalism on a pristine white bone china plate. A lustrous pool of rich, amber-hued caramelized onion jus forms the base. Two thick, perfectly seared chicken roulade medallions, golden-brown with a creamy hint of melted smoked Gouda, are centered elegantly within the jus. The chicken is precisely cut, revealing the spiral. Standing artfully alongside are two delicate, irregularly shaped crispy corn tortilla tuiles, their light golden color providing an architectural counterpoint. Finely sliced vibrant green chive batons are scattered precisely over the chicken and jus, adding fresh color. Abundant negative space emphasizes refined elegance. The plate rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface. A perfectly folded white linen napkin sits adjacent. Lighting is dramatic, casting soft, intentional shadows. The background is clean and uncluttered, focusing all attention on the culinary artistry.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Butterfly each chicken breast. Place between plastic wrap. Pound to 5mm thickness.
Season chicken lightly with salt and pepper.
Distribute diced Gouda evenly over each pounded chicken breast.
Roll chicken tightly into a cylinder. Secure with butcher's twine.
Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear roulades 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
