At the center, a neat mound of glistening, buttered egg noodles (kluski) is arranged, their pale yellow contrasting softly with the other elements. Beside the noodles, a smooth, creamy dollop of bright white Twaróg cream sits elegantly. Scattered over the cream and around the noodles are golden, irregular shards of crispy rye bread crumble, providing textural contrast. Delicately placed on the Twaróg cream are a few translucent, thinly sliced candied mushrooms, their subtle earthy tones complementing the creamy white. A vibrant green spinach coulis is artfully drizzled across the plate, forming organic lines that add a fresh color pop. The plate has moderate negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The setting includes a simple wooden table, a cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and traditional flatware, all illuminated by natural, even lighting to create an approachable, professional ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as a satisfying end to a meal, often accompanied by black tea or coffee.
instructions: Prepare Candied Mushrooms: Wash mushrooms. Slice thinly (1-2mm). Blanch slices in boiling water for 1 minute. Drain. In a small saucepan, combine 100g sugar and 100ml water. Bring to a simmer. Add mushroom slices. Cook gently for 15-20 minutes until translucent. Remove mushrooms with a slotted spoon. Place on parchment paper to dry slightly. Reserve syrup.

Prepare Crispy Rye Crumble: Preheat oven to 160°C. Break rye bread into small pieces. Pulse in a food processor to coarse crumbs. In a bowl, combine crumbs, 20g melted butter, and 20g sugar. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake for 10-15 minutes until golden and crisp. Let cool.

Prepare Spinach Coulis: Blanch spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice water. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water. Blend spinach with 20g sugar, 30ml water, and lemon juice until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a refined coulis.
Prepare Twaróg Cream: In a bowl, combine Twaróg, 100g sugar, heavy cream, vanilla extract, and lemon zest. Beat with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy.
Cook Kluski: Cook noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Toss immediately with 20g butter and 30g sugar.

Assemble Dish: Plate a portion of sweet kluski. Spoon a generous dollop of Twaróg cream beside the kluski. Arrange a few candied mushroom slices on top of the Twaróg cream. Drizzle spinach coulis artistically around the plate. Sprinkle crispy rye crumble over the Twaróg cream and kluski. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe creatively transforms typically savory ingredients like mushrooms and spinach into sweet components, offering a unique yet balanced dessert experience.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper and Black Bean Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, hearty individual portion of Roasted Bell Pepper and Black Bean Salad is presented in an everyday ceramic bowl, showcasing a medley of natural colors and textures. Roasted red, yellow, and orange bell pepper strips, slightly charred at the edges, are interspersed with glossy black beans, bright red cherry tomato halves, thinly sliced crimson red onion, and verdant chopped cilantro. Cubes of creamy green avocado are gently mixed throughout. The salad is generously coated in a light, zesty, and spicy dressing, visible as a glistening sheen on the vegetables. The components are arranged naturally, overlapping and touching, as if served directly from a family bowl onto a plate. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a casual cloth napkin. The setting evokes a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, illuminated by warm, natural light from a nearby window, with a relaxed, unpretentious atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained
Fresh jalapeño, deseeded and finely diced

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Slice bell peppers into 2 cm wide strips. Place on a baking sheet.
Roast bell pepper strips for 15-20 minutes. Peppers should be tender with slight charring. Let cool.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled roasted bell peppers, rinsed black beans, halved cherry tomatoes, thinly sliced red onion, finely diced jalapeño, and chopped cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lime juice, hot sauce, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper for the dressing.
Pour dressing over the vegetable and bean mixture. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Just before serving, gently fold in the diced avocado. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Baked Cod with Roasted Carrots and Halloumi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Baked Cod is centrally plated on a round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, flaky cod fillet, cooked whole, anchors the dish. Beside it, several vibrant orange roasted carrot batons are arranged organically, some showing slight caramelization. Thick, seared slices of Halloumi cheese, golden-brown on the exterior with a creamy white interior, are nestled among the cod and carrots. Scattered around are a few halved bright red cherry tomatoes and dark, briny Kalamata olives. A small sprig of fresh dill or parsley garnishes the fish. A quarter lemon wedge sits near the edge of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and knife and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and natural colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
Serve with a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and peel carrots. Cut into 1cm thick batons.
In a large bowl, toss carrots with 30ml olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast carrots for 15 minutes.
While carrots roast, slice Halloumi cheese into 1cm thick pieces. Pat dry.
Season cod fillets generously with salt and pepper.

After 15 minutes, remove carrots from oven. Add cod fillets, halved cherry tomatoes, and Kalamata olives to the baking sheet with the carrots. Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over cod and vegetables. Place lemon slices over cod.
Place Halloumi slices directly on the baking sheet beside the fish and vegetables.
Return baking sheet to oven. Bake for another 12-15 minutes, or until cod is opaque and flakes easily, and Halloumi is golden.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and dill. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Chicken Breast with Prosciutto, Mozzarella, and Sage Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated portion of Stuffed Chicken Breast with Prosciutto, Mozzarella, and Sage Butter Sauce rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken breast, cut diagonally in half to reveal its luscious prosciutto and melted mozzarella core, is golden-brown from searing, with a tender interior. It sits atop a generous, free-flowing mound of creamy, pale yellow Parmesan polenta. A rich, golden-brown sage butter sauce is drizzled generously over the chicken, pooling slightly around the polenta. Several fresh, vibrant green sage leaves are artfully placed on and around the dish as garnish. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the remaining sauce and polenta.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Butterfly each chicken breast. Place between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1 cm thickness.
Season chicken lightly with salt and pepper.
Place 2 slices of prosciutto on one half of each chicken breast. Top with 35-40 grams of mozzarella.
Fold the other half of the chicken breast over the filling. Secure edges with toothpicks.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm.
Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. Add butter and minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken stock and 8-10 sage leaves to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, reducing sauce by half. Season with salt and pepper.

While sauce reduces, prepare polenta. Bring 750 ml water or stock to a boil in a saucepan. Whisk in polenta slowly. Reduce heat to low. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently, until creamy and thickened.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and 30 grams of butter into the polenta. Season with salt.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of creamy polenta onto each plate. Remove toothpicks from chicken. Cut each stuffed breast diagonally in half. Arrange two halves on top of the polenta.
Spoon the sage butter sauce over the chicken. Garnish with fresh sage leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Stuffed Mushrooms with Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single generously sized, baked Portobello mushroom cap is centrally placed on a warm-toned, slightly imperfect ceramic plate. The mushroom cap is golden-brown and tender from baking, with a slight char on the edges. Its savory filling, a hearty mix of finely diced chicken, fluffy rice, small cubes of ripe red tomato, and finely chopped mushrooms, spills slightly from the top, showing varied textures. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adorns the top, adding a fresh color contrast. The plate rests on a well-worn, light wooden kitchen table, bathed in soft, natural light from a nearby window. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard fork are casually placed beside the plate. The scene evokes a comforting, homely meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Gently clean mushrooms. Carefully remove stems. Finely chop mushroom stems.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and mushroom stems. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Dice chicken thighs into small cubes.
Add chicken cubes to the pan. Cook 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Break apart any large pieces.
Remove chicken mixture from heat. Transfer to a mixing bowl.
Add cooked rice, diced tomato, chicken broth, grated Parmesan cheese, dried oregano, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Mix well to combine.
Place mushroom caps gill-side up on a baking sheet.
Generously spoon the chicken and rice mixture into each mushroom cap.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until mushrooms are tender and filling is lightly golden.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Bavette with Fermented Cabbage & Mushroom Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared beef bavette is presented on a clean, round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The beef, cut into thick, irregular chunks, reveals a rosy, medium-rare interior and a dark, caramelized crust. It rests atop a generous pool of rich, glossy mushroom and beef reduction. Adjacent to the beef is a compact, vibrant mound of pale golden fermented cabbage, its strands distinct and glistening. The plating is minimalistic, allowing significant negative space on the plate. Textures are key: the beef's crisp exterior contrasts with its tender interior; the cabbage is slightly yielding; the sauce is smooth and viscous. The scene is set on a light, reclaimed wood surface with an undyed linen napkin, illuminated by soft, natural light, creating an eco-conscious, clean aesthetic.
instructions: Separate mushroom caps from stems. Slice mushroom caps. Roughly chop mushroom stems.
Peel and thinly slice shallots. Peel and mince garlic.
In a saucepan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped mushroom stems, sliced shallots, and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Deglaze pan with red wine. Reduce by half.
Add beef stock and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes, or until liquid reduces by half and flavors concentrate.
Strain the reduction through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids. Keep warm.
Gently warm the fermented cabbage in a small pot over low heat. Do not boil.
Pat beef bavette dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat remaining olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or cast iron skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place bavette in hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until internal temperature reaches 60°C (140°F).
Remove beef from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes. Internal temperature will rise to 75°C (167°F) for safe consumption.
While beef rests, add sliced mushroom caps to the hot pan. Sauté until golden and tender, about 3-4 minutes.
Stir butter into the warm mushroom reduction until melted and glossy.
Slice rested beef bavette against the grain into thick chunks or medallions.

To plate, spoon a generous pool of mushroom reduction onto a clean white plate. Arrange a small mound of warm fermented cabbage beside the sauce. Place beef chunks on top of the sauce, next to the cabbage. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cashew Verjus Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Fermented Cashew Verjus Cake is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The cake slice stands upright, revealing its tender, slightly dense crumb. Its color is a warm, natural beige from the whole wheat flour and cashews. A glossy, translucent verjus glaze with naturally plump, diced seasonal fruit, such as deep purple grapes or amber figs, generously coats the top, dripping slightly down the sides. The texture contrasts between the soft cake, the softened fruit, and the subtle sheen of the glaze. A few fresh, vibrant green mint leaves are placed artfully beside the slice, adding a touch of natural color. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The background is minimalist, with a hint of soft, natural light and a draped, undyed linen napkin. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. The presentation emphasizes simplicity, natural textures, and the inherent beauty of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh seasonal fruit.
A small dollop of additional fermented cashew cream can be served on the side.

ingredients.name: natural sweetener (e.g., date sugar, maple syrup)

instructions: Soak raw cashews overnight, or in hot water for 2 hours. Drain.
Prepare Fermented Cashew Cream: Blend 150g soaked cashews with 100ml plant-based milk and 15ml verjus until very smooth. Add probiotic capsule content if using.
Pour cashew cream into a clean jar. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 12-24 hours until tangy. Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease and flour a small cake pan (approx. 15cm diameter).
Mix Dry Ingredients: In a bowl, whisk whole wheat flour, 50g natural sweetener, baking powder, and salt.
Combine Wet Ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk 100ml fermented cashew cream, olive oil, 50ml water, and lemon zest.
Combine Batter: Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Bake Cake: Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cool in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Prepare Verjus Glaze/Compote: In a small saucepan, combine 50ml verjus, 20g natural sweetener, and diced seasonal fruit.
Simmer over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until fruit softens slightly and liquid thickens to a light syrup.
Assemble: Once cake is cool, pour the verjus glaze/compote over the top.
Garnish: Garnish with fresh mint leaves or thyme.
notes: This recipe emphasizes local, seasonal, and zero-waste ingredients.
Sourcing high-quality, organic ingredients is recommended for best flavor and sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo con Patatas (Spanish Garlic Chicken with Potatoes)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo con Patatas is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, seared chicken thighs, skin-on, are the focal point, positioned slightly overlapping. Around the chicken, roasted potato chunks, approximately 2-3 cm, are artfully arranged, some with their skins on. A rich, savory sauce, infused with garlic and smoked paprika, coats the chicken and potatoes, pooling subtly on the plate. The sauce exhibits a warm, reddish-brown hue. Thinly sliced, caramelized onion pieces are visible within the sauce. The dish is generously garnished with vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley, scattered over the chicken and potatoes, adding a pop of color and freshness. The textures are varied: crispy chicken skin, tender chicken meat, and soft, comforting potato. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface. Beside the plate, a clean white cotton napkin is neatly folded. Traditional flatware is positioned for dining. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style image. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, allowing the dish to remain the primary subject.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the flavorful sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 8-10 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2-3 cm rustic chunks. Peel and thinly slice onion. Peel and thinly slice garlic.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add sliced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes until wine slightly reduces.
Add chicken broth and bay leaves to the pan. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Add potato chunks around the chicken.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover the pan. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaves. Taste sauce and adjust seasoning if needed. Chop fresh parsley.
Serve chicken and potatoes immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken skin is very dry before searing for maximum crispiness.
Adjust the amount of garlic to personal preference.
traditional_techniques: Sofrito (aromatic base of onion and garlic)

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Lamb Sausage and Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rigatoni with Lamb Sausage and Sun-Dried Tomatoes sits centrally on a round, clean white porcelain plate. The rigatoni is coated in a rich, rustic tomato-based sauce, flecked with deep red sun-dried tomato pieces. Golden-brown, pan-seared lamb sausage chunks are interspersed throughout, providing a hearty visual anchor. Vibrant green, torn fresh basil leaves and finely chopped parsley are scattered over the top, adding a fresh contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano provides a subtle, lighter hue. The dish has a natural, slightly free-form arrangement, showcasing the al dente pasta, robust sausage, and soft sun-dried tomatoes. The plate is on a simple, light-colored wooden table, with a folded white cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping the sauce.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette complements the richness.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for pasta.
Remove casings from lamb sausage. Crumble sausage.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add crumbled lamb sausage to the skillet. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 2-3 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Add crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and roughly chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked lamb sausage to the skillet. Stir. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook rigatoni in boiling salted water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water before draining.
Add drained rigatoni to the skillet with the sauce. Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Toss to combine.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 50ml at a time, until desired consistency.
Stir in fresh basil and parsley.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Lamb Sausage with Sun-Dried Tomato Polenta and Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated portion rests on a premium bone china plate with subtle patterns, centered on a white Carrara marble surface. Two or three thick, pan-seared lamb sausage medallions, cooked to a rich golden-brown crust, are artfully arranged atop a flowing, creamy mound of vibrant orange-red sun-dried tomato polenta. The polenta maintains a fluid, luxurious consistency. A delicate sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped herb gremolata, featuring fresh parsley, mint, and lemon zest, provides contrasting color and aromatic accent, precisely placed for visual impact. The composition is organic and natural, allowing for abundant negative space. Dramatic professional lighting casts subtle shadows. A pristine white linen napkin folded precisely to the side, with minimalist silver flatware, completes the setting.
instructions: Remove lamb sausage meat from casings. Form into 8 thick medallions, approximately 2 cm thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Drain sun-dried tomatoes. Finely dice 40g for polenta. Set aside 20g for garnish.
Prepare gremolata: Finely chop parsley and mint. Finely mince garlic. Combine herbs, garlic, and lemon zest in a small bowl.
Heat chicken stock in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer.

In a separate heavy-bottomed pot, bring 800ml of the simmering stock to a boil. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Stir constantly for 20-25 minutes, adding more hot stock gradually until polenta is creamy and smooth. Stir in diced sun-dried tomatoes, Parmesan, and butter. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Sear lamb sausage medallions for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.

To plate, spoon a generous, flowing mound of sun-dried tomato polenta onto the center of each plate. Arrange two seared lamb sausage medallions artfully on top of the polenta. Sprinkle a small amount of gremolata over the sausage and polenta. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb Sausage Roulade, Sun-Dried Tomato Consommé, Artichoke Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly cylindrical, thick chunk of golden-brown seared lamb sausage roulade rests slightly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtly textured rim. Beside it, a small, elegant quenelle of pale green-grey artichoke heart puree provides a soft contrast. A clear, deep amber-red sun-dried tomato consommé forms a delicate, inviting pool around the base of the roulade. One or two vibrant green, crispy sage leaves are meticulously placed on the roulade, adding a touch of aromatic freshness. The composition features abundant negative space, highlighting the precision and artistry of each component. The plate sits on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. A polished silver fork and knife are positioned to the side, resting on a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sophisticated simplicity and refined textures. The background is ultra-minimalist, drawing full attention to the culinary masterpiece.

ingredients.name: Lean ground chicken or beef (for consommé raft)

instructions: For the Lamb Sausage Roulade: In a large bowl, mix lamb sausage meat with 100g diced shallots, 50g minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Form into 41 individual cylindrical roulades, approximately 4 cm diameter and 15 cm length. Tightly wrap each roulade in cling film, twisting ends to secure. Poach roulades in simmering water at 80°C for 25 minutes until cooked through. Remove, unwrap, and pat dry. Sear roulades in a hot pan with olive oil until golden brown on all sides. Chill completely. Before serving, slice each chilled roulade into 3-4 thick, even chunks, approximately 4-5 cm long. Warm gently in a low oven or by briefly searing before plating.

For the Sun-Dried Tomato Consommé: In a large pot, combine sun-dried tomatoes, remaining shallots, remaining garlic, chicken stock, and white wine. Simmer gently for 45 minutes. Strain solids through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Allow liquid to cool. In a separate bowl, combine egg whites, lean ground chicken/beef, finely diced carrot, and finely diced celery to form a raft mixture. Gently whisk the raft mixture into the cooled tomato stock. Place pot over medium-low heat. Slowly bring to a bare simmer, allowing the raft to form on top. Do not stir. Simmer very gently for 30 minutes. Carefully ladle the clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve without disturbing the raft. Season consommé with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For the Artichoke Heart Puree: Drain artichoke hearts thoroughly. In a saucepan, melt 300g butter. Add artichoke hearts and cook gently for 5 minutes. Add heavy cream and simmer for 5 minutes. Transfer mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until very smooth. Pass the puree through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For the Crispy Sage: Heat remaining butter and 100ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Fry fresh sage leaves in batches until crisp and vibrant green. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

To Plate: Place one warm lamb sausage roulade chunk slightly off-center on each plate. Create a small, elegant quenelle or a deliberate, artistic smear of artichoke heart puree beside the roulade. Carefully pour a small pool of hot sun-dried tomato consommé around the base of the roulade. Garnish with one or two crispy sage leaves precisely placed on or near the roulade. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato and Chicken Soup with Garlic Croutons
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant reddish-orange Roasted Tomato and Chicken Soup is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The soup has a smooth, creamy consistency, with visible small, tender diced chicken pieces nestled within. Golden, crisp garlic croutons are artfully scattered across the surface of the soup, providing textural contrast. A small sprig of fresh green parsley is placed gently on top of the croutons, adding a pop of color. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich color and inviting texture. The entire bowl is visible, with moderate negative space, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.

Halve tomatoes. Quarter onion. Peel garlic cloves. Toss tomatoes, onion, and 2 cloves garlic with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast 30-35 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.

While vegetables roast, place chicken breast in a pot. Cover with water. Bring to a simmer. Cook 15-20 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, cool slightly, then dice into 1 cm cubes. Reserve.
In a large pot, heat remaining 30 ml olive oil over medium heat. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Add to pot. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Peel and dice potato into 2 cm cubes. Add roasted vegetables, diced potato, and chicken broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Carefully transfer soup mixture to a blender. Blend until smooth. Return soup to the pot. Stir in diced chicken. Heat gently.
Cut rustic bread into 2 cm cubes for croutons. In a large pan, toast bread cubes over medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil until golden and crisp.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with a handful of garlic croutons and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apple and Herb Rice Pilaf and Crispy Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening, rests beside a neat mound of fluffy rice pilaf on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken, presented whole, has a beautifully seared crust. The pilaf is light in color, flecked with small, translucent cubes of apple and vibrant green chopped parsley and thyme. A generous scattering of golden, crispy breadcrumbs adds texture and a warm hue over both the chicken and pilaf. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing the elements to breathe. A simple cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting on a plain wooden table surface, creating a refined yet approachable casual dining aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Firm apple (e.g., Honeycrisp or Granny Smith), diced
Day-old rustic bread (e.g., sourdough or baguette)

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Tear bread into small pieces. Pulse in a food processor until coarse crumbs form. Spread crumbs on a baking sheet. Bake 8-10 minutes, until golden and crisp. Set aside.

Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Continue cooking 3-5 minutes. Transfer skillet to preheated 180°C oven. Bake 10-15 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest 5 minutes.

In the same skillet (or a clean pot), melt butter with remaining 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and diced apple. Sauté 2 minutes. Add rice. Stir 1 minute to coat grains. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15-18 minutes, until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove pilaf from heat. Stir in chopped parsley and thyme. Fluff with a fork. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Spoon a mound of rice pilaf onto each plate. Place a seared chicken thigh beside the pilaf. Sprinkle crispy breadcrumbs generously over the chicken and pilaf. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Spicy Beef Ragu with Pappardelle is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The wide, flat pappardelle noodles are loosely coiled, richly coated in a dark, savory red ragu. Large, irregular chunks of tender, shredded beef are prominently visible throughout the sauce, offering a rustic texture. Vibrant green fresh basil leaves are scattered lightly over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. A small, neat mound of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese rests on the rim of the bowl. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and spoon. A folded cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. The setting is a modern bistro with natural, even lighting, creating an inviting and authentic Italian dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich ragu.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a robust Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into large 5-6 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Do this in batches to avoid overcrowding. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic and red chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Return seared beef to the pot.
Bring ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2.5-3 hours.
Stir occasionally until beef is fork-tender. The ragu should be thick and rich.
Remove beef from the pot. Shred the beef using two forks. Return shredded beef to the ragu. Stir well. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Cook pappardelle according to package instructions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving some pasta water. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
If ragu is too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water to achieve desired consistency.
Serve immediately in deep bowls. Garnish with fresh basil and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Español
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Arroz con Pollo Español rests on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The vibrant saffron-infused rice forms a golden-orange bed, studded with bright green peas and flecks of red tomato and bell pepper. Two golden-brown, seared chicken thighs, skin-on and bone-in, are nestled prominently on top of the rice, their crispy skin contrasting with the tender rice. The chicken is presented as whole pieces. A fresh lemon wedge is placed beside the chicken. Chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a touch of vivid green. The overall presentation is rustic yet refined, showcasing rich colors and inviting textures. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with a crisp white cotton napkin folded to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pan if serving family style.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Always include lemon wedges for a fresh squeeze.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: a pinch (approx. 0.1g), steeped in 30ml hot stock

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pan. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes, scraping up browned bits.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Add rice to the pan. Stir well to coat rice with the sofrito. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Cook until almost evaporated, stirring.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice mixture. Pour in hot chicken stock. Add saffron-infused stock. Stir gently.
Bring to a simmer. Cover the pan. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not stir frequently.
Check chicken internal temperature with a thermometer. It should reach 75°C (167°F).
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Adjust liquid amounts based on rice absorption; different rice types absorb differently.
Do not over-stir the rice once liquid is added to prevent starch release and mushiness.
Chicken can be cooked separately and added back at the end if preferred, but cooking in the rice adds flavor.
traditional_techniques: Socarrat (caramelized rice crust at the bottom of the pan, if achieved)

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Kare Raisu (Japanese Chicken Curry Rice)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Japanese Chicken Kare Raisu is presented on a clean, white porcelain oval plate. Steamed Japanese short-grain rice is neatly mounded on one side of the plate. A generous portion of rich, golden-brown Japanese chicken curry is spooned beside the rice, creating a distinct division. The curry features seared chicken in 3cm cubes, tender 2cm potato and carrot chunks, and softened sliced mushrooms and diced onions, all visibly integrated into the thick, glossy sauce. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped scallions garnishes the curry. Beside the curry, a small mound of bright red/yellow fukujinzuke (pickled relish) offers a traditional accent. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin, and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the warm, comforting appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fukujinzuke (pickled relish) or rakkyo (pickled shallots) on the side.
Offer a side of miso soup.

ingredients.name: Japanese curry roux block
ingredients.quantity: 100g (approx. half a standard pack for 4 servings)

instructions: Prepare vegetables: Dice onion. Cut carrots and potatoes into 2cm chunks. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Cut chicken: Cut chicken into 3cm cubes. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken: Heat oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add vegetables and tomato: Add carrot chunks, potato chunks, and diced tomato (or paste) to the pot. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Deglaze and simmer: Return seared chicken to the pot. Pour in water or dashi. Bring to a boil. Skim any foam. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15-20 minutes, or until vegetables are tender and chicken is cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Add roux and mayonnaise: Turn off heat. Break curry roux blocks into pieces and add to the pot. Stir until completely dissolved. Stir in mayonnaise and soy sauce.
Finish curry: Return to low heat. Simmer gently, stirring constantly, for 5-10 minutes until curry thickens to desired consistency. Do not boil vigorously after adding roux.
Cook rice: While curry simmers, cook Japanese short-grain rice according to package directions.
Serve: Ladle hot curry over steamed rice. Garnish with chopped green onion.
notes: Ensure curry roux is fully dissolved before simmering to avoid lumps.
Adjust curry thickness by adding more water or simmering longer.
Do not boil curry vigorously after adding roux to prevent scorching and maintain consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Malfatti di Ricotta e Spinaci con Salsa al Pomodoro Fresco
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of delicate, irregularly oval-shaped ricotta and spinach malfatti is artfully arranged in a shallow, matte white ceramic bowl. The malfatti, each approximately 4 cm long, exhibit a pale green hue from the spinach, with a tender, slightly dimpled surface. They are generously coated in a vibrant, rustic red fresh tomato sauce, which has a smooth yet slightly chunky texture. A scattering of bright green, torn fresh basil leaves provides a aromatic contrast, alongside a dusting of finely grated golden Parmigiano Reggiano. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a linen napkin and classic silver fork beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and comforting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a 'primo piatto' (first course) in a traditional Italian meal.
Offer fresh, crusty bread on the side for 'scarpetta' (mopping up the sauce).
Serve with an extra bowl of grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
instructions: Wash spinach thoroughly. Steam or blanch spinach until wilted. Squeeze out all excess water using a clean kitchen towel. Chop the spinach finely.

In a large bowl, combine ricotta cheese, finely chopped spinach, egg, 50g of Parmigiano Reggiano, 50g of flour, nutmeg, 1 teaspoon salt, and 0.5 teaspoon black pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.

Lightly flour a baking sheet. Dust your hands with flour. Take small portions of the ricotta mixture (about 20g each) and gently roll them into irregular, oval-shaped dumplings, approximately 4 cm long. Place malfatti on the floured baking sheet.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Gently drop the malfatti into the boiling water, cooking in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 3-4 minutes, or until they float to the surface and are tender. Remove malfatti with a slotted spoon and drain well.

While malfatti cook, prepare the sauce. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add thinly sliced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant, do not brown. Add crushed San Marzano tomatoes. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add the cooked malfatti directly to the tomato sauce. Gently toss to coat the malfatti evenly. Remove from heat.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish each serving with fresh torn basil leaves and the remaining 50g of grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Chicken and Pea Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of creamy, free-flowing risotto is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is off-white with vibrant green peas and golden-brown, irregular chunks of seared chicken. The texture is velvety and fluid. Finely chopped fresh green parsley is lightly sprinkled over, with a few thin Parmesan shavings. Chicken is cut into rustic 2cm chunks. The plate rests on a light wooden table, typical of a modern bistro. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and knife are beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant. This is a single, generous individual portion, filling the plate without overcrowding. Standard Western flatware is used for this Italian-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a light white wine.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken. Let rest 5 minutes. Cut into 2cm chunks.
In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil and 30g butter. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until translucent.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add warm chicken broth, one ladle at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for liquid to absorb before adding next ladle.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Add green peas. Stir 2 minutes until heated through.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Stir in chicken chunks. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Stirring the risotto constantly is key for creaminess.
Use warm broth to maintain cooking temperature.
Ensure chicken is cooked through but not dry.

recipes.recipe_name: Berry Oat Clafoutis
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of Berry Oat Clafoutis rests on a simple, off-white ceramic dessert plate, slightly off-center. The Clafoutis presents a rustic, puffed golden-brown crust, lightly dusted with white icing sugar. Visible within the slice and on the surface are bursts of deep red and purple from cooked mixed berries, some whole, some slightly burst. The interior reveals a creamy, custardy texture with subtle flecks of ground oats, contrasting with the soft, yielding berries. The plate sits on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table, showing natural grain. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a muted tone lies casually beside the plate. A sturdy, silver dessert fork rests nearby. Warm, inviting natural light bathes the scene, highlighting the homely comfort of the dessert. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm.
Optionally serve with a dollop of crème fraîche or plain yogurt.

ingredients.name: Mixed red berries (strawberries halved if large, raspberries, blueberries)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Grease a 22 cm round baking dish generously with softened butter.
Grind rolled oats in a food processor until fine, like flour.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and salt until well combined.
Add ground oats to the wet mixture. Whisk until smooth.
Stir in cottage cheese gently. Do not overmix.
Scatter mixed berries evenly in the prepared baking dish.
Pour the batter slowly over the berries.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. The Clafoutis should be puffed and golden-brown. A knife inserted near the center should come out mostly clean.
Remove from oven. Let cool on a wire rack for 15 minutes.
Dust generously with icing sugar before serving. Serve warm.
notes: This dessert is best served warm, shortly after baking.
Leftovers can be reheated gently.

recipes.recipe_name: Gâteau de Campagne à l'Avoine et Fromage Blanc
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of Gâteau de Campagne à l'Avoine et Fromage Blanc sits on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic dessert plate with a subtle, rustic rim. The cake slice is golden brown on top, with a gently textured, slightly coarse crumb visible from the oats, indicating its homely, comforting nature. It is casually dusted with a light, uneven layer of powdered sugar. In the background, the rest of the whole, round cake rests on a simple wooden cutting board or a plain, low cake stand on a well-used wooden dining table. The scene is bathed in warm, natural light, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. A simple silver dessert fork lies beside the plate on a casually folded linen napkin. The overall presentation is unpretentious and focuses on the cake's homemade appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a cup of strong black coffee or herbal tea.
Offer with a simple fruit compote, such as berry or apricot.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease an 18 cm round cake tin with butter. Dust lightly with flour.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, eggs, granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and lemon zest. Whisk until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together rolled oats, all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared cake tin. Spread evenly.
Bake for 30-35 minutes. Cake is done when golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
Invert cake onto a wire rack. Cool completely.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Pasta with Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy chicken pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente pasta is coated in a rich, blush-pink sauce. Generous chunks of golden-brown seared chicken, cut into 2.5 cm cubes, are interspersed throughout. Thinly sliced, deep red sun-dried tomato pieces provide vibrant color and texture. Bright green specks of fresh oregano and chopped parsley are visible, adding freshness. The overall presentation is natural and flowing, with moderate negative space on the plate. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by traditional flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the inviting textures and warm colors of the dish, creating a modern bistro atmosphere with an authentic Italian feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmesan at the table.
Serve with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes (in oil, drained, thinly sliced)
Parmesan cheese (grated, plus extra for serving)

instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Season chicken cubes with salt and pepper.
Add chicken to pan. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add shallot to pan. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of pan.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and fresh oregano. Simmer 3 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan. Cook 2-3 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens slightly.
Add cooked pasta and cooked chicken to the pan. Toss to coat evenly.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley and extra Parmesan.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Reserved pasta water helps create a smooth, emulsified sauce.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (stirring pasta with sauce and cheese)

recipes.recipe_name: Lengua Estofada con Arroz y Tortillas
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, rustic white ceramic plate or a shallow bowl, showcasing a single, refined individual portion. Centrally placed are several generous, irregularly cut chunks of rich, dark brown beef tongue, approximately 3-4 cm, glistening with a savory, reddish-brown sauce. The sauce, thick enough to coat the tongue but still fluid, shows small specks of red from the tomatoes and chipotle. A neat mound of fluffy white rice sits adjacent to the tongue, slightly touching the sauce. The dish is vibrantly garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green cilantro and a scattering of small, crisp white onion dice over the tongue and sauce. A bright lime wedge rests on the plate's rim. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting. A stack of warm corn tortillas, wrapped in a cloth napkin, is presented in a traditional basket or tortilla warmer beside the plate, completing the authentic Mexican dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the stew and sauce
Offer lime wedges for a fresh citrus squeeze
Accompany with pickled jalapeños or a spicier salsa on the side for added heat
instructions: Place beef tongue in a large pot. Cover with water. Add half a white onion, 2 garlic cloves, and 1 bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 2-3 hours until very tender. Tongue should pierce easily with a fork.

Remove tongue from pot. Reserve cooking liquid. Let tongue cool slightly. Peel off outer skin and discard. Trim any tough connective tissue. Cut tongue into large, irregular chunks (approximately 3-4 cm).
In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat vegetable oil over medium heat. Add remaining half white onion, diced, and 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes, chipotle peppers, dried oregano, and cumin powder. Stir well. Cook for 5-7 minutes, breaking down tomatoes.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Add the cooked beef tongue chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

While tongue simmers, prepare rice. Rinse rice under cold water. In a saucepan, combine rice and 500 ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let rest 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Warm corn tortillas on a comal or dry skillet until soft and pliable.

Serve Lengua Estofada hot. Place a generous portion of stewed tongue chunks and sauce on a plate. Serve alongside a scoop of white rice. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and diced white onion. Serve with lime wedges and warm tortillas.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Smoked Chicken and Crispy Pork Belly Macaroni Bake
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous individual portion of golden-brown macaroni bake. The surface is lightly browned and bubbly from baking, with a crisp panko breadcrumb topping. Visible through the creamy, rich cheese sauce are tender pieces of shredded smoked chicken and small, crispy diced chunks of pork belly, providing textural contrast. Finely diced yellow onion and minced garlic are incorporated into the sauce. A vibrant sprinkle of thinly sliced green onions and a few delicate drizzles of bright red hot sauce adorn the top, adding fresh color and a hint of spice. The macaroni is plump and coated in a thick, savory cheese sauce. The overall presentation is inviting and robust, with a balanced composition and moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Dice pork belly into 1 cm cubes. Cook in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove pork belly. Drain excess fat, leaving 15ml in skillet.
If using raw chicken, cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Shred chicken into bite-sized pieces. If using smoked chicken, shred directly.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Add butter to skillet with pork fat. Melt over medium heat. Add finely diced yellow onion and minced garlic. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until thickened.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated cheddar and Gruyere cheese until melted and smooth. Add hot sauce, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Add cooked macaroni, shredded chicken, and crispy pork belly to the cheese sauce. Stir to combine thoroughly.
Transfer mixture to prepared baking dish. Sprinkle panko breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and golden brown. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and extra hot sauce, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Latin American Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: The Arroz con Pollo is presented in a wide, shallow, rustic ceramic serving dish. Golden-hued rice, infused with saffron, forms the base, its grains distinct and fluffy. Nestled atop the rice are several bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, deeply browned and slightly crisped from searing, their skin glistening. Vibrant pops of color come from bright green peas and thinly sliced pimento-stuffed green olives, scattered artfully across the dish. The dish is garnished generously with fresh, coarsely chopped cilantro leaves, adding a fresh green contrast. A few lime wedges are placed alongside. The overall presentation is abundant and inviting, reflecting a communal, family-style Latin American meal. The chicken pieces are whole, not sliced. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a white porcelain plate, a cotton napkin, and a single fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family-style directly from the cooking pan or a large serving dish.
Accompany with simple side dishes like a green salad or sliced avocado.
Offer extra lime wedges for individual squeezing.
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, shallow, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down first, until deeply golden and crispy, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and bay leaf. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing flavors to meld.
Add rice to the pan. Stir well to coat all grains with the sofrito. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine, if using. Cook until almost completely absorbed, stirring constantly.
Stir in hot chicken broth and saffron (with its soaking liquid). Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pan tightly. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove pan from heat. Stir in frozen peas and sliced olives. Re-cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Remove bay leaf. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro. Serve hot with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Southwestern Chicken and Black Bean Soup
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, hearty bowl of Southwestern Chicken and Black Bean Soup is presented on a well-used wooden dining table. The soup fills a rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, reddish-brown broth. Visible are generous chunks of shredded chicken, plump black beans, and vibrant small cubes of red bell pepper, interspersed with diced onion. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green cilantro leaves is scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. A bright green lime wedge rests casually on the rim of the bowl, ready for a squeeze. The presentation is natural and unpretentious, reflecting a homely family kitchen setting with warm, cozy lighting. The bowl sits on the simple table, with a casually placed cloth napkin nearby. The focus is entirely on the appetizing, comforting qualities of the soup.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced red onion and diced red bell pepper. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, chili powder, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken breasts to the pot. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side.
Pour in diced tomatoes, black beans, and chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred the chicken using two forks.
Return shredded chicken to the pot. Stir well.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Oven-Baked Chicken and Vegetable Medley
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Oven-Baked Chicken and Vegetable Medley is arranged on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight beige tint, placed on a rustic, dark wooden dining table. The golden-brown chicken chunks, each about 3-4cm, are nestled amongst vibrant roasted vegetables. Diced potatoes, roughly 2cm cubes, display a light crisp exterior, alongside tender 1cm carrot rounds and softened, quartered mushrooms. Scattered throughout are softened diced onions and bright red diced tomatoes, adding bursts of color. A mound of fluffy white rice sits beside the medley. The arrangement is casual and natural, with components gently overlapping. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a home kitchen. A plain white cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate, and a standard metal fork and knife are placed, ready for a comforting family meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Slice carrots into 1cm rounds. Quarter mushrooms. Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Cut chicken breasts into 3-4cm chunks.
In a large bowl, combine chicken chunks with low-fat mayonnaise, minced garlic, 1 teaspoon salt, 0.5 teaspoon black pepper, and 1 teaspoon dried oregano. Mix well to coat chicken.

On a large baking tray, toss diced potatoes, sliced carrots, diced onion, and quartered mushrooms with 15ml olive oil, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and 0.25 teaspoon black pepper. Spread vegetables in a single layer.
Add diced tomatoes to the vegetable tray, distributing evenly.
Place chicken chunks among the vegetables on the baking tray. Ensure chicken is not overcrowded.
Bake for 30-35 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C. Stir vegetables halfway through baking.
While baking, cook rice according to package directions.
Remove tray from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and vegetable medley immediately with cooked rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, rustic bowl of Hearty Chicken Vegetable Soup is presented on a well-used wooden dining table. The ceramic bowl, in a natural, earthy tone, holds a generous single portion. Diced chicken chunks, approximately 2 cm, are visible throughout the rich, golden broth. Bright orange diced carrots, pale green diced celery, and creamy white diced potatoes are interspersed, showcasing their distinct textures. The chicken is cooked through, tender, and retains its natural shape. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley sits on top, adding a fresh contrast. The soup fills the bowl appropriately, with some negative space around the rim. The setting includes a simple, slightly worn wooden spoon resting beside the bowl and a casually folded cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, homely atmosphere. The focus remains on the wholesome, unpretentious food.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm diced chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Cook until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Pour in chicken broth. Add dried thyme and bay leaf.
Bring soup to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes.
Add diced potatoes. Continue to simmer for another 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty chicken and vegetable soup is presented in a clean, off-white ceramic bowl. The soup features clearly visible, evenly diced pieces of tender white chicken breast, bright orange carrot cubes, soft, pale yellow potato chunks, and vibrant red tomato pieces. These ingredients are suspended in a rich, reddish-orange broth, indicating a savory, tomato-infused base. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley or oregano garnishes the surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The textures appear inviting and comforting. The bowl is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded cotton napkin and a plain metal spoon rest beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the steam rising gently from the hot soup. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual, contemporary bistro setting without distraction, keeping the focus entirely on the appealing dish.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel and dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel and dice carrots into 1 cm cubes. Set aside.
Peel and dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Dice fresh tomatoes into 1.5 cm pieces.
Melt butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in tomato paste, diced fresh tomatoes, diced potatoes, dried oregano, and black pepper. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes and carrots are tender.
Season the soup with salt to taste.
Ladle the hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or oregano if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Potatoes and Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty braised chicken is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly chipped rim. A whole, bone-in chicken thigh, its skin a rich, burnished golden-brown, sits prominently, surrounded by large, tender chunks of roasted potato and thick, irregular pieces of softened carrot. The chicken is not sliced or fanned. A rich, savory, reddish-brown braising liquid pools at the bottom, lightly coating the ingredients. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast. The setting is a well-worn wooden kitchen table, illuminated by warm, inviting light. A simple, sturdy fork and knife rest beside the bowl on a casually placed linen napkin. The overall impression is comforting and unpretentious.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the braising liquid.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, e.g., Maris Piper or Yukon Gold

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip. Sear other side 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add chopped onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add potato chunks, rosemary sprigs, and thyme. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Cover the pot.
Transfer covered pot to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Discard rosemary sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, presented whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken has a crisp, well-developed crust and a tender appearance. Beside it, a neat arrangement of vibrant green roasted asparagus spears. A glossy, pale yellow lemon-herb pan sauce is elegantly spooned over the chicken and around the plate, showing specks of fresh green parsley. A fresh lemon wedge is placed to the side, and a small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the chicken. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, creating a clean, professional bistro atmosphere with a soft, unobtrusive background. The portion is a single, refined serving.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Trim woody ends from asparagus. Toss asparagus with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast asparagus for 10-12 minutes, or until tender-crisp.
While asparagus roasts, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and a crust forms.
Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits.
Reduce stock by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in cold butter, one cube at a time, until sauce is emulsified and glossy.
Stir in fresh lemon juice from one lemon and chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve chicken breasts whole, alongside roasted asparagus. Spoon lemon-herb sauce generously over chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage and Pasta Salad with Pickled Carrots
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, resting on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. Shredded green cabbage forms the base, interspersed with small, al dente pasta shapes and vibrant orange pickled carrot rounds. A small portion of shredded, golden-brown chicken is delicately placed among the vegetables. Fresh mixed greens add contrasting dark green hues and texture. The entire composition is lightly coated with a clear, herb-flecked vinaigrette, showcasing the natural sheen of the ingredients. Negative space is maintained to highlight each component. The setting features an undyed linen napkin in natural beige and soft, diffused natural lighting, creating a clean, eco-conscious aesthetic. A small potted herb plant sits subtly in the background.
instructions: Prepare quick pickled carrots: Combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, 1/2 teaspoon salt, mustard seeds, and peppercorns in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add sliced carrots. Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside.
Cook chicken: Season chicken breast with salt and pepper. Pan-sear or roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Shred or dice into small pieces.

Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, and a pinch of pepper. Stir in chopped dill and parsley. Add 2 tablespoons of the pickling liquid from the carrots.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, cooked pasta, shredded chicken, mixed salad greens, and drained pickled carrots.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Serve immediately.
notes: For zero-waste, compost all vegetable scraps.
Adjust pickling liquid in dressing to taste for desired tanginess.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Chicken Breast, Tomato Essence, Compressed Basil Tomato
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a sophisticated, minimalist composition on a pristine white bone china plate. A perfectly cooked sous vide chicken breast, sliced into two thick, moist medallions, showcases a pure white interior and a delicate golden-brown sear on its exterior. It rests elegantly on one side of the plate. Adjacent, a vibrant, glossy pool of intensely red tomato essence shimmers, reflecting light. Opposite the chicken, a small, precise mound of jewel-like, translucent compressed tomato cubes, infused with bright green basil flecks, adds a burst of color and textural contrast. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing their architectural placement and refined simplicity. The scene is set on a premium grey veined marble surface, under dramatic professional lighting that creates subtle shadows, enhancing depth and luxury. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded, completes the ultra-minimalist background.

ingredients.name: Firm ripe tomatoes, diced into 1 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss quartered beefsteak tomatoes, shallot, garlic with 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 30 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
Transfer roasted vegetables to a blender. Add white wine and chicken stock. Blend until very smooth.
Pass the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Pour the strained liquid into a saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce by half until intensely flavored and slightly thickened. Stir in balsamic vinegar. Adjust seasoning. Keep warm.
Season chicken breasts generously with sea salt and black pepper. Place each breast in a separate vacuum-sealable bag. Add a small knob of butter to each bag.
Vacuum seal bags. Cook in a preheated water bath at 63°C for 1.5 hours.
Once cooked, remove chicken from bags. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat with a touch of olive oil. Sear chicken breasts for 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown. Rest for 5 minutes.
In a bowl, gently combine diced tomatoes, julienned basil, extra virgin olive oil, and a pinch of salt.
Place tomato mixture in a vacuum-sealable bag. Vacuum seal on high pressure to compress. Keep sealed until plating.
Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick medallions.
Arrange chicken medallions artfully on individual plates, slightly off-center.
Spoon a generous pool of warm tomato essence beside the chicken.
Carefully open the compressed tomato bag. Arrange a small, precise mound of compressed basil tomato cubes near the chicken.
Garnish with a few micro basil leaves, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chipotle Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoky Chipotle Beef Ragu with Pappardelle is presented in a clean, wide white porcelain bowl plate. The golden pappardelle pasta forms a nest, generously topped with large, tender chunks of dark, rich braised beef ragu. The beef, broken into substantial pieces, shows its deep reddish-brown color, coated in the glossy, thickened sauce. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro contrasts against the dark ragu. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's textures and colors, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef.
Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic, rehydrated and minced chipotle chilis, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in diced tomatoes and beef broth. Add bay leaves.
Return seared beef to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from pot. Shred or break into large pieces with a fork. Discard bay leaves.
Reduce sauce over medium-high heat until thickened to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
Return shredded beef to the sauce. Keep warm.
Cook pappardelle according to package instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving some pasta water.
Toss cooked pasta with a generous amount of ragu. Add a splash of pasta water if needed for consistency.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple Cinnamon Cottage Cheese Oat Cake
recipes.visual_description: A generous slice of warm Apple Cinnamon Cottage Cheese Oat Cake sits on a simple, cream-colored ceramic plate. The cake slice reveals a moist, tender crumb with visible flecks of ground and whole oats, and soft, light brown 1cm diced apple cubes throughout. Its top crust is a delicate golden-brown, lightly dusted with white icing sugar. In the background, the remaining whole round cake rests on a rustic wooden cutting board, also lightly dusted, suggesting a freshly baked, homely dessert. The setting is a well-used wooden kitchen table. A casually folded beige linen napkin lies beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20cm round cake tin.
Grind 100g of rolled oats into fine flour. Reserve 50g whole oats.
Peel, core, and dice apples into 1cm cubes.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs and sugar until light and fluffy.
Stir in cottage cheese and vanilla extract. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, combine ground oat flour, whole oats, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt.
