Toss broccoli florets with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly charred.

Rinse basmati rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, combine rice with 500ml water, a pinch of salt, and half the lemon zest. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in remaining lemon zest, lemon juice, and chopped parsley.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board to rest for 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced shallot and minced garlic. Sauté for 2-3 minutes, until fragrant and softened.

Add halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes, gently pressing some tomatoes to release juices, until they begin to burst and soften. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes, allowing sauce to slightly reduce. Stir in chopped fresh basil. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.

To serve, place a mound of lemon herb rice on each plate. Arrange a whole seared chicken breast next to the rice. Spoon the tomato-basil sauce generously over and around the chicken. Arrange roasted broccoli florets alongside. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer for a thicker sauce, or adding a splash more broth for a thinner one.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Dijon Chicken with Herbed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a bed of fluffy white long-grain rice, subtly flecked with green chopped tarragon. A rich, creamy Dijon sauce, pale yellow with hints of the pan's fond, is generously spooned over and around the chicken. The chicken exhibits a tender, moist appearance beneath its crisp exterior. A few fresh tarragon sprigs are placed delicately beside the chicken for garnish, adding a vibrant green contrast. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and standard silver cutlery are neatly placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting from the side, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is a gently blurred, casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Offer crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add minced shallots to the same skillet. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in chicken stock and Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.

While sauce simmers, prepare rice. Rinse rice under cold water. Combine rice and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes, covered. Fluff with a fork. Stir in butter and half of the chopped tarragon.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet with the sauce. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 5 minutes until chicken is heated through and coated.
Stir remaining chopped tarragon into the sauce. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve chicken immediately over a bed of herbed rice. Spoon generous amount of sauce over chicken.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety. Use a meat thermometer.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer for thicker sauce, or adding a splash more stock for thinner.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Fermented Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A single individual portion of al dente linguine forms a natural mound. Glistening lightly, it features golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, cut into rustic 3 cm pieces. Vibrant, burst fermented cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly wrinkled, are interspersed throughout. Thinly sliced, translucent sautéed onions weave through the pasta strands. The color palette is earthy and warm: deep reds, golden chicken, natural beige pasta. Fresh, verdant basil leaves provide a bright green contrast. The plating is minimalistic, allowing ample white space, emphasizing each ingredient's natural beauty. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige rests beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting organic textures against a clean, minimalist background with subtle natural elements.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes (at least 3-5 days in advance): Dissolve sea salt in filtered water to create brine. Place cherry tomatoes, garlic, and basil (if using) in a clean glass jar. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 3-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Store in refrigerator after fermentation.

Prepare Onion-Infused Broth: Combine onion scraps, water, and bay leaf in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Set aside.

Cook Chicken: Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken and sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Sauté Aromatics: In the same pan, add thinly sliced onion. Cook over medium heat until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

Build Sauce: Add the fermented cherry tomatoes (including some of their brine) to the pan with onions and garlic. Crush tomatoes gently with a spoon to release juices. Bring to a simmer. Add 200 ml of the prepared onion-infused broth. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Cook Pasta: While sauce simmers, cook linguine in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.

Combine: Add cooked chicken chunks and drained pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If needed, add a splash of reserved pasta water to achieve desired consistency. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Serve: Divide pasta among four plates. Garnish generously with fresh basil leaves.
notes: The fermentation process for tomatoes can be adjusted based on desired tanginess. Taste daily.
Leftover onion-infused broth can be frozen for future use in soups or sauces.
Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Liver Pâté with Toasted Brioche
recipes.visual_description: A small, individual serving of smooth, light brown chicken liver pâté is elegantly presented on a round white porcelain plate. The pâté, with its velvety texture, is either quenelled artfully or served in a small, rustic ceramic ramekin. Beside it, several perfectly toasted, golden-brown brioche slices are arranged neatly, offering a delicate contrast. A small cluster of bright green cornichons, sliced thinly, provides a sharp, acidic counterpoint. A dollop of deep red fig jam adds a sweet, vibrant accent. A tiny sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the pâté. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin complete the modern bistro setting, bathed in soft, even natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette or brioche slices.
Offer cornichons and fig jam as traditional accompaniments.
instructions: Clean chicken livers. Remove any connective tissue or green spots. Pat dry.
Melt 50 g of butter in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced shallots and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add chicken livers to the pan. Sear livers for 2-3 minutes per side until browned but still slightly pink inside. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Deglaze the pan with cognac. Scrape up any browned bits. Cook for 1 minute until alcohol evaporates.
Stir in heavy cream, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Transfer liver mixture to a food processor.
Add remaining 150 g of cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes, to the food processor. Process until very smooth and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Pass the pâté through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl for extra smoothness, pressing with a spatula.
Pour the pâté into individual ramekins or a terrine dish. Cover surface directly with plastic wrap to prevent a skin from forming.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until firm.
To serve, toast brioche slices until golden. Serve pâté with toasted brioche, cornichons, and fig jam.

recipes.recipe_name: Scallop Consommé, Tomato Confit, Seared Scallop
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a Michelin-starred dish is presented in a deep, pristine white bone china bowl. The clear, golden scallop consommé forms the base, its surface almost reflective. Three perfectly seared, plump scallops, exhibiting a beautiful golden-brown crust and delicate white interior, are nestled organically within the consommé. Alongside, a small, artfully arranged cluster of vibrant red halved cherry tomato confit provides a contrasting pop of color and tender texture. A few precise drops of vivid green thyme oil are strategically placed on the consommé's surface, creating an elegant visual accent. A single, tiny sprig of bright green micro basil or cress delicately rests atop one of the scallops, offering a final, minimalist touch. The plating emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the pristine nature of each component. The entire bowl is centered on a luxurious grey-veined Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing the dish's sculptural quality against an ultra-minimalist background, ensuring the food remains the sole focus.
instructions: Prepare Thyme Oil: Blanch 2 thyme sprigs for 10 seconds. Immediately plunge into ice water. Drain well. Blend blanched thyme with 100 ml neutral oil until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or coffee filter. Set aside.

Prepare Tomato Confit: Halve 200 g cherry tomatoes. Toss with 2 thyme sprigs, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 20 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast at 120°C for 45-60 minutes, or until tender and slightly shriveled. Remove thyme and garlic. Set aside.

Prepare Scallop Consommé: Reserve scallop trimmings. In a pot, sauté 50 g chopped onion, 30 g chopped carrot, 20 g chopped celery, and scallop trimmings until aromatic. Add 5 g tomato paste. Deglaze with a splash of fish stock. Add 1 litre fish stock and 2 remaining thyme sprigs. Simmer gently for 20 minutes. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool completely.

Clarify Consommé: Whisk 3 egg whites until frothy. Gently fold egg whites into the cooled broth. Place pot over medium heat. Stir constantly until egg whites form a 'raft' on the surface. Stop stirring. Simmer gently for 20-30 minutes without disturbing the raft. The consommé will clarify. Carefully ladle the clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.

Sear Scallops: Pat scallops completely dry with paper towel. Season generously with salt. Heat 30 ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over high heat until shimmering. Place scallops in the hot pan without overcrowding. Sear for 1.5-2 minutes per side until a deep golden crust forms and scallops are just opaque through the center. Cook to 75°C internal temperature if desired.

Plate the Dish: Pour a portion of warm consommé into each deep, modern designer bowl. Carefully arrange 3 seared scallops and a small cluster of tomato confit in the center of the consommé. Drizzle a few drops of the vibrant thyme oil around the elements. Garnish with 1-2 tiny micro basil leaves for a final touch of freshness and color. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Bean and Potato Stew with Savory Chocolate
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of Hearty Bean and Potato Stew rests in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The stew is rich, thick, and dark reddish-brown, showcasing tender, 2 cm potato cubes, plump mixed beans, and flecks of diced onion. The potatoes are soft but hold their shape, and the beans are intact. A subtle sheen on the surface hints at the melted chocolate. The stew is topped with a scattering of freshly chopped vibrant green parsley. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Adjacent is a simple fork and a casual, slightly rumpled cloth napkin. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures. The background is a softly blurred glimpse of a lived-in kitchen, suggesting a relaxed family meal.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500g, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.quantity: A few sprigs, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in smoked paprika and dried oregano. Cook 30 seconds.
Add potato cubes, chopped tomatoes, and vegetable stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer 15-20 minutes. Potatoes should be tender.
Stir in drained beans, Dijon mustard, and chopped dark chocolate.
Simmer 5 minutes. Stir until chocolate melts and integrates.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Pork Belly with Creamy Cheddar Grits
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual starter portion of Crispy Pork Belly with Creamy Cheddar Grits is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, pale yellow cheddar grits form a smooth, flowing base in the center of the plate. Scattered artfully on top of the grits are several irregular, golden-brown cubes of roasted pork belly, approximately 2cm in size. Each pork belly piece exhibits a visibly crispy, bubbly crackling skin and tender, succulent meat. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh chives garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast to the rich colors. The overall presentation is inviting and approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, beside a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under soft, natural lighting. A subtly blurred background suggests a casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Can be accompanied by a light, acidic coleslaw to cut through richness.
instructions: Pork Belly:
Score pork belly skin in a crisscross pattern. Do not cut into meat.
Place pork belly in a pot. Cover with cold water. Add apple cider vinegar. Bring to a boil. Boil for 10 minutes.
Drain pork belly. Pat very dry with paper towels.
Season pork belly generously with salt and pepper.
Place pork belly skin-side up on a wire rack over a baking tray.
Roast in a preheated oven at 160°C for 2 hours.
Increase oven temperature to 220°C. Roast for another 20-30 minutes, or until skin is crispy and crackling.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 10 minutes. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Cheddar Grits:
Bring chicken stock to a boil in a saucepan.
Slowly whisk in grits. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes, or until grits are creamy and tender. Add more liquid if needed.
Stir in butter, milk, and grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth.
Stir in minced garlic and half of the chopped chives. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Assembly:
Ladle a portion of creamy cheddar grits onto each plate.
Arrange crispy pork belly cubes on top of the grits.
Garnish with remaining fresh chopped chives.
notes: The apple cider vinegar in the blanching water helps tenderize the pork belly and can contribute to crispier skin.
Ensure grits are stirred frequently to prevent sticking and ensure creaminess.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Bean and Potato Braise
recipes.visual_description: A comforting Hearty Bean and Potato Braise is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, filling it generously. The dish features soft, yielding 2 cm diced potatoes, tender creamy cannellini beans, and well-cooked, translucent chopped onions, all suspended in a rich, earthy brown broth slightly thickened from the potato starch and tomato paste. A few vibrant green flecks of fresh chopped parsley are scattered casually on top, adding a fresh contrast. The components are naturally intermingled, showcasing the hearty textures. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm wooden dining table. A simple, slightly worn metal spoon rests within the bowl. A plain, light-colored linen napkin is casually placed beside it. Warm, natural overhead lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting, home-cooked appeal.
instructions: Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Peel and chop onions.
Mince garlic cloves.
Drain and rinse cannellini beans.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add chopped onions. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add diced potatoes, vegetable broth, dried thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Add rinsed cannellini beans to the pot.
Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 10-15 minutes, until potatoes are tender and broth slightly thickened.
Remove bay leaf.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Dijon Sauce and Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white ceramic plate, showcasing a golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast as the centerpiece. The chicken, cooked to perfection, is either left whole or cut into two thick, inviting pieces, never fanned. Adjacent to the chicken are several rustic, garlic-herb smashed potatoes, their irregular shapes and slightly crisp, golden edges adding texture. A rich, creamy Dijon mustard sauce is generously spooned over the chicken, with a small pool gathered at the base. The sauce is a warm, pale yellow, contrasting with the vibrant green of freshly chopped chives sprinkled over both the chicken and potatoes. The overall presentation is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's warmth and comforting appeal. A simple linen napkin and standard European cutlery complete the casual dining setting on a natural wooden table surface.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Wash potatoes. Place potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.

While hot, gently smash each potato with a fork or potato masher. Do not mash completely. Leave some chunks for texture. Season generously with salt, pepper, half of the minced garlic, and half of the chopped parsley.

Heat 30 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add smashed potatoes in a single layer. Cook, pressing gently, until golden and crisp on both sides, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove and keep warm.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in the same pan over medium-high heat.

Add chicken breasts to the hot pan. Sear until golden brown, about 4-5 minutes per side. Reduce heat to medium. Continue cooking until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F), about 5-7 more minutes depending on thickness. Remove chicken from pan. Rest on a cutting board, loosely covered.

Add chopped shallot and remaining minced garlic to the pan. Sauté until fragrant and softened, about 2 minutes. Deglaze the pan with chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Pour in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions or leave whole. Place chicken and smashed potatoes on serving plates. Spoon generous amount of creamy Dijon sauce over chicken. Garnish with remaining fresh chives and parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: For extra richness, a splash of white wine can be used to deglaze the pan before adding chicken broth.
Adjust the amount of Dijon mustard to your preference for a milder or stronger mustard flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Valrhona Chocolate Textures
recipes.visual_description: On a pristine matte black ceramic coupe plate, an elongated quenelle of gleaming dark chocolate crémeux forms the core. Beside it, a delicate, airy cloud of aerated chocolate rises gently. Fine, crumbly chocolate soil is artfully scattered, providing textural contrast. A single, gracefully curved cocoa nib tuile stands vertically, leaning against the crémeux, its translucent form studded with dark nibs, adding architectural height. Small, vibrant ruby-red drops of raspberry fluid gel are precisely dotted across the ample negative space, offering a striking color pop and acidic highlight. The minimalist plating emphasizes rich chocolate tones and varied textures, punctuated by bright red. The plate sits on polished dark wood, dramatically lit to create defined shadows. A crisp white linen napkin completes the elegant, understated scene.

ingredients.name: Chocolate Soil
ingredients.quantity: 50g dark chocolate (70% cacao), grated or finely chopped

instructions: Dark Chocolate Crémeux:
Heat milk, cream, and salt in a saucepan until simmering. Remove from heat.
Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a bowl until pale.
Temper egg mixture with hot milk mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring, until thickened (82°C). Do not boil.
Pour hot custard over chopped chocolate in a bowl. Let stand 1 minute.
Whisk gently from center outwards until smooth and emulsified.
Pass crémeux through a fine-mesh sieve. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill 4 hours or until firm.
Aerated Chocolate:
Combine glucose syrup and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Whisk in agar-agar until dissolved. Simmer 1 minute.
Pour hot liquid over chopped chocolate in a bowl. Let stand 1 minute.
Whisk until smooth.
Strain mixture into a siphon. Charge with 1 N2O cartridge. Shake well.
Refrigerate siphon horizontally for 2 hours.
Chocolate Soil:
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Combine flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in grated chocolate.
Spread mixture thinly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake 12-15 minutes, stirring halfway, until crisp and fragrant.
Cool completely. Break into desired soil texture.
Cocoa Nib Tuile:
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Whisk melted butter, powdered sugar, egg white, and flour until smooth.
Stir in cocoa nibs.
Spread very thin layers of batter onto a silicone baking mat using a stencil or offset spatula.
Bake 5-7 minutes until golden brown at edges.
Remove from oven. Immediately shape over a rolling pin or desired form while warm. Cool completely to set.
Raspberry Fluid Gel:
Blend raspberries until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds.
Combine raspberry puree, sugar, and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk in agar-agar until dissolved. Simmer 1 minute.
Pour mixture into a shallow dish. Chill until set, about 30 minutes.
Transfer set gel to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and fluid.
Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Store in a squeeze bottle or piping bag.
Assembly (Per Plate):
Pipe a quenelle of Dark Chocolate Crémeux onto one side of a chilled plate.
Dispense a small cloud of Aerated Chocolate next to the crémeux.
Scatter Chocolate Soil artfully near the crémeux and aerated chocolate.
Place one Cocoa Nib Tuile vertically or at an angle, resting on the crémeux.
Dot small drops of Raspberry Fluid Gel around the plate for color and acidity.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, vibrant orange-red tomato risotto is presented in a shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. The risotto flows gently, indicating its fluid, 'all'onda' consistency. On top, two or three thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks are nestled into the rice, showcasing a crisp exterior and tender interior. Bright green chopped basil is mixed throughout the risotto, with fresh whole basil leaves and a light sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese garnishing the top. A subtle drizzle of olive oil glistens on the surface. The plate sits on a rustic wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware (fork and spoon). The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting, emphasizing the dish as the focal point. The composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp white wine.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1/2 bunch, chopped, plus leaves for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (75°C internal temperature). Remove chicken. Rest.
In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil and 25g butter. Sauté diced onion over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast grains.
Pour in white wine (if using). Cook until absorbed.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well.
Add one ladle of hot chicken broth. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding more. Cook for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan and remaining 25g butter.
Fold in chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick chunks.
Serve risotto immediately. Top with chicken chunks, fresh basil leaves, and extra Parmesan.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (finishing with butter and cheese for creaminess)

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Pork and Potato Soup with Mustard
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty pork and potato soup is presented in a sturdy, deep ceramic bowl, reflecting a homely, rustic aesthetic. The rich, amber-brown broth is thick and comforting, cradling generous chunks of tender, braised pork and soft, cubed potatoes. Small ditalini pasta pieces are visible throughout the substantial liquid, adding texture. The soup's surface is garnished with a scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley, providing a fresh contrast to the deep, savory tones of the dish. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a basic metal spoon are casually placed beside the bowl, reinforcing the inviting, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The presentation is natural, unpretentious, and focuses on comforting satiety.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic cloves.
Peel potatoes and cut into 2 cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add pork cubes. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Return seared pork to the pot.
Add cubed potatoes. Bring soup back to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until pork and potatoes are tender.
Stir in pasta. Cook for an additional 8-10 minutes, or according to package directions, until pasta is al dente.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Apple Potato Mignardises
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature Chocolate Apple Potato Mignardises are elegantly arranged on a pristine, rectangular French porcelain serving platter. Each mignardise features distinct layers: a dark, glossy chocolate glaze topping a smooth, light orange-yellow apple-potato puree, which rests on a firm, dark brown chocolate rice crispy base. A delicate, off-white swirl of white bean vanilla cream adorns the top of each piece, providing a subtle contrast. The arrangement is clean and balanced, with consistent spacing between each square. The overall presentation is refined, showcasing the precise layering and smooth textures of the petite desserts. The platter is placed on a simple wooden surface in a modern bistro setting, illuminated by soft, natural light, creating a professional yet approachable aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Apple-Potato Puree: Combine diced sweet potato, diced apple, granulated sugar, lemon juice, cinnamon, nutmeg, and water in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat until very tender. Mash or blend until smooth. Cool completely.

Prepare Chocolate Rice Crispy Base: Melt 150 g dark chocolate and 30 g butter in a double boiler. Stir in puffed rice cereal until coated. Press mixture firmly into an 18x18 cm square pan lined with parchment paper. Chill 30 minutes until firm.
Prepare White Bean Vanilla Cream: Blend rinsed cannellini beans, powdered sugar, vanilla extract, and heavy cream until very smooth. Transfer to a piping bag. Chill.
Assemble Mignardises: Spread the cooled apple-potato puree evenly over the chilled chocolate rice crispy base. Chill 30 minutes. Cut into 8-10 uniform 4.5x4.5 cm squares.
Prepare Chocolate Glaze: Melt remaining 100 g dark chocolate, 20 g butter, and corn syrup in a double boiler. Stir until smooth. Let cool slightly to a pourable consistency.
Glaze Mignardises: Place cut squares on a wire rack over parchment paper. Pour chocolate glaze over each square, ensuring full coverage. Allow excess to drip. Chill until glaze is set.
Garnish: Pipe a small decorative swirl or dot of White Bean Vanilla Cream onto each glazed mignardise. Serve chilled.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Savory Beef and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Simple Savory Beef and Rice Skillet rests in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The dish presents a comforting mix of tender, crumbly ground beef and fluffy white long-grain rice, thoroughly integrated. Interspersed throughout are soft, vibrant red diced tomatoes and hints of translucent cooked onion. The overall color palette is warm, with rich browns from the beef, off-white from the rice, and pops of red. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a final, homely garnish, contrasting with the savory tones. The textures are soft and yielding, inviting a spoonful. The bowl is placed on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl on a casual cloth napkin. The scene is lit with soft, warm light, evoking a cozy family kitchen setting.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet or pot over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Drain excess fat from the skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in uncooked rice, diced tomatoes with their liquid, and beef broth.
Bring mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the skillet tightly.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift lid during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Ground Beef and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A modest, comforting portion of Savory Ground Beef and Rice Skillet rests centrally on a round, rustic ceramic plate. The plate is a warm, muted off-white or light grey, showing subtle handmade imperfections. The dish itself features golden-brown ground beef chunks mixed evenly with fluffy, tender white rice. Specks of bright orange diced carrots and vibrant green peas are interspersed throughout, adding natural color. A light, savory broth coats the ingredients, giving a moist, cohesive appearance. The texture is hearty and inviting. A sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped dark green parsley sits atop the mound of food. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. The setting is a well-worn wooden dining table. A simple, folded grey linen napkin is casually placed beside the plate. A standard silver fork rests on the table, ready for use. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, perhaps a blurred glimpse of a kitchen counter or a simple wall, reinforcing the homely setting without distraction.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and diced carrots to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, salt, pepper, and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add uncooked rice to the skillet. Stir for 1 minute to lightly toast.
Pour in beef broth and canned diced tomatoes with their liquid. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in frozen peas. Cover and let stand for 5 minutes off heat.
Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Salmon & Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mediterranean-inspired dish centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A thick, pan-seared salmon fillet, golden-brown and flaky, rests atop a bed of rustic roasted vegetables. The vegetables include golden-brown potato wedges, softened red onion wedges, bursting red cherry tomatoes, and glossy black Kalamata olives. Each component shows distinct cooking textures: crispy salmon skin, tender potatoes, and blistered tomatoes. A creamy, pale orange smoked paprika aioli is generously drizzled over the salmon and vegetables, creating a rich contrast. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered for a pop of color. The plate features moderate negative space, showcasing the natural arrangement of ingredients. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table and a cotton napkin beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the pan juices and aioli.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Prepare vegetables: Cut potatoes into 2cm wedges. Cut red onion into 2cm wedges.
On a large baking tray, toss potato wedges, red onion wedges, cherry tomatoes, Kalamata olives, smashed garlic cloves, and rosemary sprigs with 60ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and lightly browned.
While vegetables roast, prepare aioli: In a small bowl, whisk together yogurt, mayonnaise, minced garlic, smoked paprika, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Set aside.
Pat salmon fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 20ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear salmon fillets skin-side down for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy.
Flip salmon. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until salmon reaches an internal temperature of 63°C.
Remove salmon and roasted vegetables from oven.
Plate: Place a portion of roasted vegetables on each plate. Top with a seared salmon fillet. Drizzle generously with smoked paprika aioli. Garnish with fresh basil or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Sausage Ragout with Potato Gnocchi
recipes.visual_description: A generous single serving of Chicken and Sausage Ragout with Potato Gnocchi is presented in a deep, clean white ceramic bowl. The dish features tender, golden-brown potato gnocchi coated in a rich, rustic reddish-brown tomato ragout. Visible within the sauce are irregular, browned pieces of Italian sausage and succulent, slow-cooked chicken chunks. Diced carrots, celery, and onions add subtle color and texture to the savory sauce. The dish is topped with a generous sprinkle of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese and vibrant green, roughly chopped flat-leaf parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The textures are a harmonious blend of soft gnocchi, tender meats, and a velvety sauce. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a polished Italian-style fork, under natural, even lighting that highlights the food’s authentic appeal. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space around the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Montepulciano.
instructions: For the gnocchi: Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 20-25 minutes. Drain well.
Peel hot potatoes. Pass through a potato ricer or mash thoroughly. Spread mashed potato on a clean surface to cool slightly.
Sprinkle 200g flour over potatoes. Add egg yolk and a pinch of salt. Gently knead until a soft, cohesive dough forms. Do not overmix.
Divide dough into four portions. Roll each portion into a long rope, 2cm thick. Cut ropes into 2cm pieces. Gently roll each piece over a gnocchi board or fork tines.
Place gnocchi on a lightly floured tray. Cook gnocchi in batches in a large pot of salted boiling water. They are done when they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
For the ragout: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add sausage, breaking it apart. Cook until browned. Remove sausage and set aside.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion, celery, and carrot to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return browned chicken and sausage to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, partially covered, for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and sauce has thickened. Stir occasionally.
Season ragout with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in half of the chopped parsley.
Add cooked gnocchi directly into the ragout. Gently toss to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes to warm through.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Velouté de Poulet et Champignons Forestiers
recipes.visual_description: A luxurious, creamy Velouté de Poulet et Champignons Forestiers is presented in a wide, shallow bone china bowl. The pale, ivory velouté forms a smooth, flowing pool, leaving ample negative space. Precisely cut, small cubes of tender, poached chicken are arranged in the center. A single, golden-brown, thinly sliced crispy shiitake mushroom tuile stands upright, providing architectural height and contrasting texture. Vibrant green chive oil is artfully drizzled around the chicken. A scattering of delicate microgreens adds freshness. The bowl rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by an elegant silver spoon and a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Prepare the Chicken Stock for Poaching: In a saucepan, combine 500 ml chicken stock or water, bay leaf, peppercorns, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Poach the Chicken: Carefully add chicken breasts to the simmering liquid. Ensure they are fully submerged. Reduce heat to low, cover, and gently poach for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, cool, then dice into small, precise 1 cm cubes. Set aside.
Start the Velouté: In a large pot, melt butter over medium-low heat. Add diced shallots and sliced garlic. Sweat until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Do not brown.
Add Mushrooms and Potatoes: Add cleaned mixed forest mushrooms to the pot. Sauté for 5-8 minutes until softened and fragrant. Add diced potatoes. Stir well.
Simmer Velouté Base: Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are very tender.

Blend and Refine Velouté: Remove from heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until completely smooth. Pass the soup through a fine-mesh sieve (chinois) into a clean pot, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Finish Velouté: Return smooth velouté to low heat. Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and white pepper. Heat gently, do not boil. Keep warm.

Make Crispy Mushroom Tuiles: Preheat oven to 160°C. Toss thinly sliced shiitake mushrooms with olive oil and sea salt. Arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until crisp and golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Cool on a wire rack.

Prepare Chive Oil: Blanch chopped chives in boiling water for 10 seconds, then immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Drain well and squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched chives with neutral oil until very smooth and vibrant green. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or coffee filter for a clear oil.

Plate the Dish: Ladle warm velouté into the center of a wide, shallow soup bowl, leaving generous negative space. Arrange a few precise cubes of poached chicken in the center of the soup. Carefully place one crispy mushroom tuile upright or delicately angled into the velouté. Drizzle a few drops of chive oil artfully around the chicken. Finish with a few delicate microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Pork Belly, Potato Gnocchi, Dijon Jus, Garlic Pangrattato
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely plated starter portion rests on a pristine round, high-rimmed bone china plate, centered with abundant negative space. A precisely cut, dark mahogany rectangle of slow-braised pork belly, approximately 5cm by 4cm, sits elegantly on one side, its top showcasing a deeply caramelized, crisp skin. Adjacent to the pork, three to four perfectly formed, ridged potato gnocchi, golden-brown from a quick pan-sear, are arranged organically. A delicate, glossy pool of amber-hued Dijon jus is artfully spooned onto the plate, enhancing the composition without overwhelming it. A light scattering of golden-brown, irregular garlic pangrattato provides textural contrast over the gnocchi and jus. A few vibrant green, finely chopped parsley leaves are meticulously placed for a final touch of color and freshness. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a sharp triangle, lies neatly beside modern, polished silver cutlery. Soft, dramatic directional lighting casts subtle shadows, highlighting the dish's textures and colors against an ultra-minimalist background, ensuring the food remains the sole focal point.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.quantity: 4 cloves (2 for braising, 2 for pangrattato), minced

instructions: For the Pork Belly:
Preheat oven to 150°C.
Score pork belly skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork belly, skin-side down, until deeply golden and crispy. This takes 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other sides for 2-3 minutes each.
Remove pork from pan. Drain excess fat, leaving 1 tablespoon.
Add chopped onion, carrot, celery, and 2 minced garlic cloves to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Deglaze with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return pork belly to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure liquid comes halfway up the pork.
Cover pan tightly. Braise in the preheated oven for 2.5-3 hours, or until pork is very tender.
Remove pork from braising liquid. Strain liquid and reserve for the jus. Discard solids.
Place pork belly between two cutting boards. Place a heavy weight on top. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, to press and firm up.
For the Potato Gnocchi:
Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender. Drain well. Peel while hot.
Pass potatoes through a potato ricer or mash thoroughly. Spread on a clean surface to cool slightly and release steam.
Create a well in the center of the riced potatoes. Add flour and egg yolk.
Gently mix ingredients with a fork, then briefly knead until a cohesive dough forms. Do not overmix.
Divide dough into portions. Roll each portion into long ropes, about 1.5 cm thick.
Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces. Roll each piece over the tines of a fork or a gnocchi board to create ridges.
Dust gnocchi lightly with flour. Set aside.
For the Dijon Jus:
Pour reserved braising liquid into a saucepan. Bring to a vigorous simmer over medium-high heat.
Reduce liquid until it thickens to a glossy, coating consistency. This takes 10-15 minutes.
Whisk in Dijon mustard. Remove from heat. Swirl in cold butter until melted and emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.
For the Garlic Pangrattato:
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add torn bread pieces and remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook, stirring frequently, until bread is golden brown and crispy. This takes 5-7 minutes.
Remove from heat. Season with salt.
To Serve:
Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut pressed pork belly into 4 equal, neat rectangles.
Place pork belly pieces, skin-side up, on a baking sheet. Roast for 10-15 minutes, until skin is crispy and meat is heated through.
Meanwhile, bring a pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Cook gnocchi in batches until they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Plate each portion: Arrange one crispy pork belly rectangle on a side of a clean white plate. Place 3-4 gnocchi next to the pork, creating an organic arrangement.
Spoon a delicate pool or smear of Dijon jus onto the plate.
Sprinkle garlic pangrattato over the gnocchi and jus. Garnish with a pinch of fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Chocolate Brownie Bites
recipes.visual_description: The brownie bites are arranged casually on a well-used wooden dining table, placed directly on a simple ceramic plate with natural imperfections. They are cut into irregular, generous squares, showcasing a dense, fudgy texture. The surface is a deep, rich brown, with visible melted chocolate chips peeking through. No decorative garnishes are used; the focus is solely on the inviting, homemade appearance of the brownies. The background is minimal, highlighting the food. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen. Portions are ample, reflecting a comforting, homemade feel. There are no strict geometric arrangements, just a natural pile of ready-to-eat snacks for relaxed family sharing. The entire plate is visible, showcasing an authentic home kitchen scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature.
Pair with a glass of milk or coffee.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 20x20 cm baking tin with parchment paper.
In a food processor, combine cooked sweet potato, rinsed black beans, and oil. Blend until smooth.
Transfer mixture to a large bowl. Add grated apple, brown sugar, cocoa powder, rice flour, baking powder, salt, and vanilla extract. Mix until just combined.
Fold in chocolate chips.
Pour batter into prepared tin. Spread evenly.
Bake for 25-30 minutes. A toothpick inserted should come out with moist crumbs.
Let cool completely in tin. Cut into irregular, generous squares.
notes: These bites are naturally moist and fudgy. They store well in an airtight container at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, rustic Chicken Cacciatore with Tagliatelle is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally positioned. The rich, deep red tomato sauce, studded with tender, irregular chunks of boneless chicken thigh, diced red bell pepper, and sliced mushrooms, cascades generously over a nest of golden tagliatelle pasta. The chicken pieces are plump and visibly tender, retaining their natural shape. Fresh green chopped parsley is scattered over the top, providing a bright color contrast and a hint of freshness. A generous sprinkle of pale yellow grated Parmesan cheese adds a delicate texture. The pasta is perfectly al dente, with a slight sheen from the sauce. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated with natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pan. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, chopped rosemary, and thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is tender.
While chicken simmers, cook tagliatelle according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain well.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve chicken cacciatore over a bed of tagliatelle. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For a richer flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and remove bones after cooking.
The sauce can be made ahead of time and reheated.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Honey-Cider Glazed Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared salmon fillet, skin crisped to a golden-brown, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The salmon is presented as a whole, succulent piece, its rich orange hue contrasting with the surrounding elements. Beside it, a vibrant medley of roasted root vegetables is artfully arranged. Deep ruby-red beet wedges, bright orange carrot batons, and golden-brown potato wedges are scattered organically, showcasing their slightly caramelized edges and tender interiors. Finely chopped fresh rosemary and a light drizzle of glossy, amber honey-cider glaze adorn the salmon and vegetables, adding aromatic and visual accents. The plate maintains moderate negative space, allowing each component to breathe. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and scrub beets. Cut into 2 cm wedges.
Peel carrots. Cut into 2 cm thick batons.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2 cm wedges.
In a large bowl, toss beets, carrots, and potatoes with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Mince garlic cloves.
Remove rosemary leaves from stems. Chop finely.
In a small saucepan, combine apple cider and honey. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce cider mixture by half, about 10-12 minutes, until slightly thickened. Set aside.
Pat salmon fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy.
Flip salmon. Add butter, minced garlic, and chopped rosemary to the skillet.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Cook for 6-8 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F).
Remove vegetables from oven. Toss with a drizzle of honey-cider glaze.
If using, quickly wilt spinach in the salmon skillet after removing salmon, or steam lightly.
To plate, arrange roasted vegetables on each plate. Place a salmon fillet beside vegetables.
Drizzle remaining honey-cider glaze over salmon and vegetables.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Beef Biryani is presented centrally on a round white porcelain plate. A mound of long-grain basmati rice, cooked to fluffy perfection, forms the base. Visible within the rice are tender, dark brown chunks of slow-cooked beef. Scattered throughout are golden-brown caramelized onion slivers, providing textural contrast. Bright green flecks of fresh cilantro and mint leaves are interspersed, offering a vibrant color pop. The rice exhibits subtle hints of saffron, lending a warm, inviting hue. The overall presentation is natural and abundant, showcasing distinct layers of ingredients without being overly structured. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small, white ceramic bowl of cooling raita and a single metal spoon. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and mint).
Serve with Kachumber (chopped onion, tomato, cucumber salad).
Offer lime wedges on the side for a fresh squeeze.
Traditionally eaten with hands, or a spoon.
instructions: Rinse basmati rice several times. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain.

Marinate beef: Combine beef chunks with ginger-garlic paste, yogurt, all ground spices, 1 teaspoon salt, and slit green chilies. Add 4 green cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 2cm cinnamon stick, and 1 bay leaf. Mix well. Marinate for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the refrigerator.

Heat 3 tablespoons ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Fry onions, stirring frequently, until deep golden brown and crispy. Remove half the fried onions and set aside for layering and garnish.

Add marinated beef to the pot with remaining onions. Sear beef chunks on all sides for 5-7 minutes. Add 100ml water. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 45-60 minutes, or until beef is nearly tender. Stir occasionally.

While beef cooks, prepare rice: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add 1 tablespoon salt, 2 green cardamom pods, 2 cloves, and 1cm cinnamon stick. Add drained basmati rice. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until rice is 70% cooked (still firm but pliable). Drain immediately. Discard whole spices.

Assemble biryani: Layer half of the partially cooked rice over the beef in the pot. Sprinkle half of the reserved fried onions, half of the chopped mint, and half of the chopped cilantro over the rice.
Add remaining rice over the first layer. Sprinkle remaining fried onions, mint, and cilantro. Drizzle saffron strands soaked in warm milk evenly over the top.
Seal the pot: Place a tight-fitting lid on the pot. For traditional dum cooking, seal the edges with a strip of dough (flour and water). Alternatively, use foil under the lid.
Cook on low heat: Place the sealed pot on a very low flame or a tawa (griddle) over low flame. Cook for 20-25 minutes. This allows rice to steam and flavors to meld.
Rest: Turn off heat. Let biryani rest, undisturbed, for 10-15 minutes before opening.
Serve: Gently fluff biryani with a fork. Mix lightly to combine beef and rice layers. Serve hot.
notes: Marinating the beef overnight enhances flavor and tenderness.
Ensure the pot is sealed well for effective dum cooking.
Adjust green chilies for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Roasted Mediterranean Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared salmon fillet, skin side up, is positioned slightly off-center on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The salmon features a crisp, golden-brown skin and flaky, pink flesh. Around the salmon, artfully arranged but not rigidly, are roasted baby potato halves, vibrant green broccoli florets, softened red onion wedges, and burst cherry tomatoes, interspersed with dark, glossy Kalamata olives. Each vegetable exhibits a slight char and tender texture. A light drizzle of the lemon-basil pan sauce cascades over the salmon and vegetables. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered as a final garnish. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for dipping in the pan sauce and vegetable juices.
A small glass of the dry white wine used in the sauce can complement the meal.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half for juice, half for wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
On a large baking sheet, combine potatoes, broccoli florets, red onion wedges, cherry tomatoes, and pitted Kalamata olives.
Drizzle vegetables with 45ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Stir halfway through.
While vegetables roast, pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season salmon generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place salmon fillets, skin-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip salmon. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Cook for 6-8 minutes, or until salmon reaches an internal temperature of 63°C.
Remove salmon from skillet. Set aside.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce wine by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in butter and juice from half a lemon until sauce is emulsified.
Stir in fresh basil. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
notes: This dish balances fresh, high-quality ingredients with refined cooking techniques for a sophisticated yet approachable main course.
The pan sauce adds depth and moisture, elevating the simple roasted components.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Potato and Bean Pasta Bites
recipes.visual_description: A comforting stack of Crispy Potato and Bean Pasta Bites rests on a simple, everyday ceramic plate, possibly with a slightly imperfect rim, in a muted, warm tone. The bites are golden-brown with a visibly crispy exterior, showing the rustic texture of the pan-fried surface. Some small, irregular bits of mashed bean and tiny pasta shapes are discernible, hinting at the hearty interior. Each bite is a modest, irregular patty shape, not perfectly uniform. A few fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley leaves are casually sprinkled over the top, adding a fresh contrast. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing the natural grain of the wood. A casually folded, plain cloth napkin sits nearby. The lighting is warm and inviting, suggesting natural light from a kitchen window or cozy overhead kitchen fixtures, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. Portions are generous, showing 4-5 bites on the plate, ready for casual sharing or individual enjoyment.
instructions: Boil 500g potatoes until tender. Drain well. Mash thoroughly in a large bowl.
Cook 100g small pasta according to package directions. Drain well.
Drain and rinse 400g canned cannellini beans. Mash roughly with a fork.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a medium pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute more. Remove from heat.
Add mashed beans, cooked pasta, sautéed onion and garlic, 1 egg, 30g all-purpose flour, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper to the mashed potatoes. Mix all ingredients until well combined and cohesive.
Form the mixture into 12-16 small, flat patties, each about 5-6 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Heat the remaining 45ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Fry patties in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Adjust heat to prevent burning.
Transfer fried patties to a plate lined with paper towel to drain excess oil.
Serve warm, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Root Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Hearty Chicken and Root Vegetable Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. The soup fills the bowl, showcasing chunky, irregular 1.5 cm diced pieces of tender potato, vibrant orange carrots, and pale green celery, along with substantial 2 cm chunks of cooked chicken. The broth is a comforting, golden hue. A light scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley rests on the surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall arrangement is natural and casual, as if served in a home kitchen. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone is casually draped beside the bowl. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a lived-in family dining area with subtle, unobtrusive elements like a simple salt and pepper shaker set. The entire bowl is visible, with adequate negative space around it.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion, carrots, and celery into 1.5 cm cubes. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Add diced potatoes, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Return seared chicken to the pot. Simmer, uncovered, for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Spiced Sausage and Chickpea Stew with Herbed Bulgur
recipes.visual_description: The Moroccan Spiced Sausage and Chickpea Stew is presented in a deep, wide white porcelain bowl, mounded slightly in the center. The stew features rich, reddish-brown sauce, tender chunks of browned sausage, vibrant diced carrots, and soft chickpeas. Sliced mushrooms and softened onions are visible throughout the stew, adding earthy tones. A light sheen from the olive oil catches the light. Beside the stew, a generous portion of fluffy bulgur wheat is neatly piled, flecked with bright green chopped fresh basil. The dish is garnished with several whole fresh basil leaves scattered over the stew and a bright yellow lemon wedge positioned on the rim of the bowl. The color palette is warm and inviting, with earthy browns, vibrant orange, creamy white, and fresh green accents. The plate is clean with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro style with a simple wooden table surface. A clean white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish. A subtle, culturally authentic element, such as a small decorative Moroccan tea glass or a patterned ceramic coaster, is visible in the soft-focus background, complementing the dish without distracting from it. The portion is refined and appropriate for a single serving in a casual dining restaurant.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread for scooping the stew.
Offer a side of plain yogurt or a dollop of yogurt cheese for a cooling contrast.
Accompany with fresh mint tea.
instructions: Slice sausages into 2 cm thick chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown sausage chunks on all sides. Remove sausages and set aside.
Chop onion, dice carrots, slice mushrooms. Mince garlic and grate ginger.
Add onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add garlic, ginger, smoked paprika, cumin, cinnamon, and cardamom. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Stir in mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Return sausage chunks to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, vegetable stock, and honey.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 25 minutes.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Add to the stew. Simmer for another 10 minutes, uncovered.
While stew simmers, prepare bulgur. Cook bulgur according to package directions. Fluff with a fork.
Chop fresh basil. Stir half into the bulgur.
Serve Moroccan spiced sausage and chickpea stew hot over herbed bulgur. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Moroccan Chicken Tagine is presented in a traditional glazed ceramic tagine base, its domed lid removed to showcase the inviting contents. Golden-brown braised chicken pieces, tender and succulent, are nestled among bright orange carrot batons and soft, deep red tomato wedges. The rich, aromatic sauce, infused with spices like turmeric and saffron, coats each ingredient with an amber hue. Slices of preserved lemon and whole green olives are visible, adding contrasting colors and textures. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green cilantro adorns the top, providing a pop of freshness. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small, fluffy mound of couscous in a white porcelain bowl and a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and authentic textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fluffy couscous or warm, crusty Moroccan bread (khobz) for scooping.
Offer a side of harissa for those who prefer more heat.
Serve with a glass of traditional Moroccan mint tea.
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt, pepper, and half of the Ras el Hanout.

Heat olive oil in a large tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, grated ginger, remaining Ras el Hanout, cumin, turmeric, and paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken broth and crushed tomatoes to the pot. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add carrot batons, tomato wedges, cinnamon stick, preserved lemon slices, and green olives around the chicken.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the tagine or pot tightly.
Simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove cinnamon stick. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet-Seared Chicken with Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Skillet-Seared Chicken with Caramelized Onions is presented on a simple, cream-colored ceramic plate with a slight rim. Two pan-seared chicken thighs, their surfaces a rich golden-brown from the sear, are placed slightly overlapping in the center of the plate. The chicken pieces are thick and irregular, showcasing their natural shape. Piled generously beside and partially under the chicken are the deeply caramelized yellow onions, soft and glossy with shades of golden-brown and amber. A few fresh thyme sprigs, still vibrant green, are casually placed over the chicken and onions. The overall color palette is warm browns and yellows with hints of green. The textures are a contrast between the slightly crisp exterior of the chicken and the tender, yielding onions. The dish is arranged naturally, as if served directly from the skillet onto the plate at a home kitchen table. The plate sits on a well-used, light-toned wooden dining table. A simple, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed nearby. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen setting, with natural light from a window or soft overhead fixture. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with mashed potatoes.
Serve with steamed green beans.
Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add sliced onions to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook onions, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet. Nestle them into the onions and broth. Add fresh thyme sprigs.
Simmer for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Serve immediately.
notes: Caramelizing onions takes time but develops deep flavor. Do not rush this step.
Adjust seasoning to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Rice Pudding with Chili-Caramelized Croutons
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of warm Coconut Rice Pudding is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl. The pudding is creamy, off-white, with a smooth, fluid consistency. Scattered across the surface and partially submerged are golden-brown, irregular chunks of chili-caramelized bread croutons. The croutons exhibit a glossy, crisp texture, with subtle flecks of red chili visible for color contrast. The clean, inviting presentation features moderate negative space on a simple wooden table. A cotton napkin is folded beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and sheen of the pudding and the crispness of the croutons, creating an approachable, refined restaurant-style appearance. No distracting elements are present, focusing solely on the dish's balanced composition.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. Drain well.
Combine rice, coconut milk, 50 g sugar, and salt in a heavy-bottomed saucepan.
Bring mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 25-30 minutes, until rice is tender and mixture is creamy. Add vanilla extract.
Remove rice pudding from heat. Cover and let stand 5 minutes. Pudding will thicken slightly upon standing.
Cut stale bread into 2 cm irregular cubes.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add bread cubes. Toss to coat. Cook until lightly golden.
Combine remaining 50 g sugar, chili flakes, and 50 ml water in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Cook until mixture turns light amber caramel.
Pour hot caramel over bread cubes in skillet. Stir quickly to coat all cubes. Be careful, caramel is hot.
Transfer caramelized bread cubes to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Separate cubes to prevent sticking.
Bake in a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) for 8-10 minutes, until crisp. Let cool completely.
Spoon warm rice pudding into individual serving bowls.
Top each bowl with a generous scattering of chili-caramelized croutons. Serve immediately.
notes: For extra richness, use full-fat coconut milk.
Adjust chili flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Broccoli Cheddar Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Broccoli Cheddar Risotto rests on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto forms a flowing, creamy base, its pale golden hue interspersed with vibrant green broccoli florets (small, intact florets) and streaks of melted, pale orange cheddar. On top, two or three thick, golden-brown chicken medallions (2cm thick) are placed, showing their perfectly seared crust and moist interior. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a final pop of color. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table, with a crisp white cotton napkin folded neatly beside it. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's textures and colors without harsh shadows. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting an approachable yet refined dining experience.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4 minutes per side until golden. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 190°C. Cook 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove, tent with foil, rest 5 minutes. Cut each breast into thick 2cm medallions.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Blanch 2 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
In a large saucepan or Dutch oven, heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook 5-7 minutes until translucent. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the saucepan. Stir 2 minutes to toast grains. Pour in white wine (if using). Stir until fully absorbed.

Begin adding hot chicken broth, one ladleful (approx. 120ml) at a time. Stir constantly until liquid is almost absorbed before adding the next ladle. Continue for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente.

Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 40g butter and grated cheddar cheese until melted and creamy. Fold in blanched broccoli florets. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
Ladle a generous portion of creamy risotto onto each plate. Arrange 2-3 chicken medallions atop the risotto. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Potato & White Bean Mignardises with Crispy Vermicelli
recipes.visual_description: Eight uniform 3cm square sweet potato mignardises are arranged in two neat rows on a rectangular white porcelain serving platter. Each mignardise features a golden-brown sweet potato base, topped with a precisely piped swirl of pale vanilla bean cream. The base is soft, earthy orange. The cream is smooth and glossy. Delicate golden-brown, crispy vermicelli shards rest atop the cream, adding fine texture and caramelized color. A tiny vibrant green mint leaf is placed on each.
